Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker pleads guilty to all charges

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group.
  • Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick, a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin.
  • Industry observers note that A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group.

Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick, a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin.

Industry observers note that A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital, where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger.

Sources indicate that as we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft, Samsung, Nvidia and UK telecom firm BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of injuries or property damage. In July 2026, that 'no longer a danger' determination was presumably made, as Kurtaj was released from hospital and moved to prison to await retrial.

According to recent reports, he has now pleaded guilty to multiple hacks carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, including the Rockstar hack that led to the GTA 6 leak. He also pleaded guilty to assaults on workers while in custody, which the BBC report states included "multiple biting incidents.".

Sources indicate that as I mentioned when Kurtaj was moved from hospital to prison, the whole thing strikes me as odd. The big question is how Kurtaj's state of mind at the time of the crimes will influence the outcome of his guilty plea, given that a previous court determined that he needed multiple years of institutionalization. BBC tech reporter Joe Tidy, who's been following the case since Kurtaj's transfer, also described it as "an unusual move" in his report.

Sources indicate that coincidentially, one must assume, Grand Theft Auto 6 rolls out for consoles on November 19. Kurtaj will be sentenced at a future date. The leaker who goes by Cyberleek, who recently distributed several GTA 6 gameplay videos apparently taken with a development build of the game, remains at large.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones are the most recent entry in Sony's 1000X series, which has been around since 2016. They're the best over-ear headphones in terms of audio quality currently on the market—but not everyone can (or needs to) drop nearly half a grand on headphones.

Industry observers note that the WH-1000XM5 are a generation older and were at the top of their class until they were supplanted by the XM6. On the plus side, by virtue of being older, they're presently discounted to $198 (down from the original $399.99) during Amazon's early Black Friday sale. That 50% off brings it down to the lowest price they've ever reached, a good deal for premium headphones that still sound incredible, even in 2026.

I have been a loyal customer of the 1000X line for many years; they're my go-to headphones for most activities. The WH-1000XM5 received an "outstanding" review from PCMag for their top-notch audio quality and exceptional audio when using the best-in-class active noise cancellation. The headphones are also well-designed to be comfortable for long listening sessions. The ear controls use tapping and swiping, which isn't my favorite, but it's what all modern headphones are moving toward. There's a companion app that lets you adjust your EQ settings to your liking, including what the swiping and tapping functions do.

These headphones also have a stereo 3.5mm connection, which is perfect for those who want to use a cable and not worry about battery life. And speaking of battery life, Sony says you can expect about 30 hours, but it will vary depending on your use of ANC. They are compatible with AAC, LDAC, and SBC codecs and have multipoint connection, meaning you can pair them with more than one device at the same time.

Industry observers note that personally, I think the value for the money you get with the XM5 for $198 is better than paying full price for the XM6. If you're looking to get ahead of the Black Friday chaos and secure an amazing deal on great headphones, this is it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping doesn't just take us back to the arena, but also returns us to District 12 and the Covey population first introduced in Suzanne Collins's novel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.
  • According to recent reports, whitney Peak plays Lenore Dove Baird, the girlfriend of Joseph Zada's Haymitch Abernathy, and – as you might have guessed from her surname – a relation of Lucy Gray Baird, played by Rachel Zegler in the Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes film.
  • GamesRadar+ sat down with the Sunrise on the Reaping cast in London, and we asked Peak if she drew inspiration from Zegler's Lucy Gray while crafting her own version of Lenore Dove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping doesn't just take us back to the arena, but also returns us to District 12 and the Covey population first introduced in Suzanne Collins's novel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.

According to recent reports, whitney Peak plays Lenore Dove Baird, the girlfriend of Joseph Zada's Haymitch Abernathy, and – as you might have guessed from her surname – a relation of Lucy Gray Baird, played by Rachel Zegler in the Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes film. The two women don't just share a name, either, but also a rebellious, free-spirited nature and a hatred for the Capitol.

GamesRadar+ sat down with the Sunrise on the Reaping cast in London, and we asked Peak if she drew inspiration from Zegler's Lucy Gray while crafting her own version of Lenore Dove.

"Absolutely," indicates Peak. "I think also just sort of setting the tone or looking for inspiration, listening to her sing was really great in getting me there. And then also, I think they're kind of strung together, just in Suzanne's writing. I think they share a lot of the same pieces, and so it's pretty good to just sort of refer back to the source material.".

Lenore Dove's relationship with Haymitch is a bright spot for them both, though, naturally, tragedy lies ahead when Haymitch is reaped on his sixteenth birthday and forced to compete in the Second Quarter Quell, a more brutal edition of the deadly Hunger Games.

"It was so notable to me to make that side of the film really happy and energetic, and just make it feel like nothing bad could happen, and have that love at the start of the film so the rest of the film works," Zada tells us of his first day shooting with Peak, in a scene featuring the young couple stealing a moment together in the Meadow, a green space on the outskirts of District 12. "And being able to work with Whitney and play that scene was fantastic. And also, it's just such a beautiful location as well.".

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters this November 20. For more, check out our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies left of 2026.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.
  • As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed.
  • The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a latest lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

It has been revealed that torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
  • Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did.
  • For Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that big a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.

Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did. GTA 5 is an exotic and sun-kissed heist movie, a mould that GTA 6’s tale of gun-toting love in Vice City very much looks to follow. That leaves Sleeping Dogs protagonist Wei Shen standing next to Niko Bellic. One might be kicking faces in Hong Kong and the other might be getting into shootouts in Latest York, but both are fresh off the boat in places both familiar and alien. They find themselves caught between two lives.

For Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop. For Niko, it’s a balancing act between trying to settle old scores and start a fresh life in post 9/11 America. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a pork bun to chow down on. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a hotdog to chow down on. Both of their games are beloved for delivering tales which get the player invested in Wei and Niko specifically, that excel in putting you into the emotional shoes of these two underworld operators whose worlds are tearing at them from multiple angles as they claw their way to the top of the food chain.

Despite my headline gag, they do this with a comparably minimal amount of in-depth life-simmy details, like those that’re baked into Red Dead Redemption 2 (and GTA 6, to a degree) as some of the main selling points. Wei can buy a pork bun, the vendor loudly informs him that by doing so he’s avoiding the possibility of never becoming a whole man, but there’s no ‘whole manliness’ meter which demands to be satiated with regular pork bun munching, lest Wei become a less than whole man. All it does is give him a temporary health regeneration boost, because as we all know, the first thing the doctors do if you’re admitted to hospital with grievous wounds after a fight is serve you a scrumptious meal that miraculously closes up your cuts in minutes.

Sleeping Dogs dedicates all of its life simming effort to making you feel the weight of Wei’s torment as he grapples with an unsustainable double life of sinning and saintly acts. Like GTA 4, it’s not got the time, tech, or budget to adorn itself with animations or systems that replicate every aspect of Wei’s day-to-day existence in excruciating detail. It’s simply assumed, rather than demonstrated, that some of the back alleys he wanders down to bust drug dealers probably smell a bit unpleasant. He doesn’t have over 60 species of bird to catalogue as he commutes from North Point to the businessman-infested Central district, then on to the houseboat-heavy Aberdeen and gated communities of Kennedy Town. Though, he does keep nicking jade statues, in order to persuade his kung fu instructor to teach him some fun new ways to knee baddies into submission.

He can sing his lungs out to nail I Fought the Law at one of Hong Kong’s few karaoke booths or lose all of his cash playing mahjong, but he doesn’t have an endless laundry list of optional hobbies long enough to suck players who aren’t even particularly trying to get distracted in for hundreds of hours.

Then again, if he wanders into his Central apartment, Wei can take a piss. In truth, I’d forgotten about this prior to my recent revisit, but it is a wonderfully simple feature that really emphasises how things’ve changed for games like these in the years since 2012. I press one button when the prompt pops up near the loo, and Wei unzips before dribbling a rather loud trickle into the bowl. Then, he’s done. I can get him to wash his hands if I wish, but no bladder meter has gone down and no dirtiness meter is being satiated by my scrubbing. If Wei doesn’t take regular whizzes, no NPCs comment that he’s looking a bit pained, and his walking animation doesn’t dynamically adjust to huddle his legs closer together.

You could ask what was even the point of animating Wei’s pissing if it’s a pointless and totally optional activity, outside of arguably doing a tiny bit of work in helping Shen be convincingly human (and it unquestionably being quite funny the first time you stumble across it). By looping what would once have been one-note button presses into systems that help them play a more active role in fleshing out the world and the routines of its inhabitants, uber-detailed games like GTA 6 - at their best - add an extra layer of definition to the tales and adventures they depict.

They often feel like the sort of game Sleeping Dogs might’ve been if it’d had their tech and its budget was the GDP of real world Hong Kong. The question is, when limitations like that don’t apply to the degree they once did, where the line lies between extra layers which tangibly deepen the player’s experience and overindulgent bloat?

According to recent reports, sleeping Dogs, despite working in its own takes on elements of GTA, Saints Row, and I’d argue RGG Studio’s earlier Like A Dragon/Yakuza entries, is an unquestionably lean and focused game. Less isn’t necessarily more, especially if you were to ask slumbering canines-loving teenage me, who would’ve bitten your hand off for Hong Kong to boast even a third of the extra features and activities GTA 6 and Red Dead 2 pack into their life of crime sims.

Industry observers note that the latter two are games that wouldn’t have been possible to make, at least in a format the masses would be able to play, back in the era when Sleeping Dogs and GTA 4 represented what an open-world crime game typically looked like. They’ve eaten up what used to be the domain of arcade racers like Midnight Club and hunting sims to step closer to being something reminiscent of Better Than Life, the addictive VR everything game from the Red Dwarfverse, which takes over players’ lives by simulating a world where everything they want can play out in reality-mimicking detail.

They aim to be far, far more than what defined their predecessors, and to use that to appeal to an ever-expanding audience. What I’m intrigued to see, whenever I get my hands on Rockstar’s latest work, is whether those like me who come to it having recently played a game like Sleeping Dogs will find a game that feels like it’s being pulled in a million different directions, to the point that it loses something of what historically has been at the centre of its fundamental appeal.

Or, to put it another way: is there a point at which you’ve eaten so many pork buns in one sitting that you begin to stray away from the self-actualisation which steady consumption of them is known to facilitate?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Generations of moviegoers grew up with the James Bond movies, making it one of the most recognizable (and profitable) franchises in the film industry. Ever since Daniel Craig's Bond run ended with No Time to Die, those fans have been curious on who will take on the mantle of 007 next. Robert Pattinson was just confirmed for the role, and folks are sounding off online about this choice. Pass me the popcorn, cuz they're not holding back.

The Bond movies (which are streaming with an Amazon Prime subscription) have made household names out of actors like Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig. Robert Pattinson already has this status, which is a big reason why there's already so much discourse about his casting. Let's break down what people are saying.

No Time to Die's ending killed off Craig's Bond, and fans have spent years taking bets on who would replace him. Now we finally know that Robert Pattinson will have that honor, and there are plenty of folks who are thrilled with this news after his acclaimed roles in projects like The Odyssey, The Drama, and Primetime. Some of those excited responses from social media read:.

Robert Pattinson has been an A-list actor since starring in the Twilight movies, and since then he's spent years building a diverse career, both in indie films and major blockbusters like The Batman. There are no franchises quite as huge as James Bond, so this is once again going to put him at the center of the pop culture landscape. Clearly the 40 year-old actor impressed director Denis Villeneuve when working with him on Dune: Part Three (which hits theaters this December).

Given how strongly cinephiles feel about the James Bond franchise, there are also plenty of naysayers who aren't pleased about Robert Pattinson taking on the mantle of 007. Those critics are definitely making their voices known on the casting announcement, with some responses reading:.

Clearly the fandom is not in agreement about whether or not Pattinson was the right choice to play 007. There are plenty of folks who are not happy about this choice, and who would prefer to see Henry Cavill as James Bond. The Man of Steel actor has expressed interest in the role for a while now, and even auditioned back when Craig was hired. We'll just have to wait and see if the Mickey 17 actor wins over his naysayers.

It's presently unclear when the 26th James Bond movie will be released, but since casting is still underway it seems like it'll be 2028 at the earliest. For now fans can see Robert Pattinson and Denis Villeneuve's collaboration when Dune: Part Three arrives December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grace Kelly always had a deep passion for astrology.
  • Actor Richard Burton was also in attendance, accompanied by his wife Elizabeth Taylor, even though she was born under the sign of Pisces.
  • Guests were required to adhere to a dress code devised by Kelly, inspired by the colors associated with the sign of Scorpio.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grace Kelly always had a deep passion for astrology. Born on November 12, 1929, she was a Scorpio, and very proud of it. To celebrate her 40th birthday on November 15, 1969, the Princess of Monaco organized a party themed by her astrological sign, resulting in the extravagant Scorpio Ball, held at the Hôtel de l’Hermitage in Monte Carlo. For the occasion, she only invited celebrities who were also Scorpios. Among the 60 or so guests were Swedish actress Hjördis Paulina Genberg, American actor Rock Hudson, and Italian actress Virna Lisi.

Actor Richard Burton was also in attendance, accompanied by his wife Elizabeth Taylor, even though she was born under the sign of Pisces. An exception was made for the actress, who was granted special permission thanks to her husband’s astrological sign—Scorpio, born on November 10. For the occasion, Taylor chose to dazzle, wearing a Cartier diamond necklace with an estimated value of $1 million around her neck—a gift from Burton two weeks earlier. She also wore a spectacular evening cape by Tiziani, made of black velvet and adorned with two rhinestone scorpions on the front and a third on the hood.

Guests were required to adhere to a dress code devised by Kelly, inspired by the colors associated with the sign of Scorpio. Red, black, and white were therefore strongly recommended. The princess, for her part, opted for an off-the-shoulder black velvet dress by Balenciaga from the fall-winter 1967 couture collection. Two ruby brooches set with diamonds—a wedding gift from Prince Rainier III—completed her ensemble.

The decor also reflected the evening’s theme. Red candles, portraits of famous Scorpios, and a lavish cake adorned with golden scorpions set the tone. No detail had been left to chance: The waiters, wearing powdered 18th-century wigs, dressed in velvet suits embroidered with sparkling stars and held silver candelabras adorned with red candles.

It has been revealed that princess Grace was seen on numerous occasions alongside Carroll Righter, an astrologer and Hollywood columnist nicknamed “the astrologer to the stars.” According to People magazine, the princess’s birth chart also revealed a Scorpio ascendant, while her Midheaven was in Leo. In astrology, the Midheaven is associated with career, public image, and reputation. Some attributed her commanding presence and magnetism in the spotlight to this configuration.

Kelly embodied the mysterious aura that her admirers associated with her astrological sign. Unfortunately, that light was extinguished on September 14, 1982, when the Princess of Monaco lost her life in a tragic car accident on the hills above the principality.

Originally published in Vanity Fair France.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Una watch is pretty much made to be hackable, with its interchangeable parts and open development environment.
  • Because the Una watch has a regular USB-C port, you don’t need to remember any specific cable, dongle, or adapter to charge it.
  • (You can also charge some other devices from a phone, including an Apple Watch, but you’d need to carry around that specific adapter, which is why nobody bothers.).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Una watch is pretty much made to be hackable, with its interchangeable parts and open development environment. But it’s also pretty barebones at launch, without many features available yet. However, here are five things I’ve discovered I can do with it—and I hope to expand this list quite a bit as the device and its community mature.

Because the Una watch has a regular USB-C port, you don’t need to remember any specific cable, dongle, or adapter to charge it. I knew that, but it didn’t occur to me until recently that I didn’t need a computer or a wall outlet to plug into the other end. I was able to take a USB-C to USB-C cable—the same kind I might carry around to charge my phone—and plug one end into my watch and the other into my phone. It charged!

(You can also charge some other devices from a phone, including an Apple Watch, but you’d need to carry around that specific adapter, which is why nobody bothers.).

Industry observers note that the Una watch doesn’t have any built-in sleep tracking, but a few community-built apps aim to provide it. The Slumber app, for example, will let you know how long you slept and compare your most recent bedtime with when you usually get to bed. There are no sleep stages (honestly: refreshing, since watches are rarely good at this anyway), and the analysis is done on the watch itself.

It has been revealed that but if what you’re really hoping for is a recovery score or an overnight HRV reading, the HabitLab app combines that with habit tracking. Every evening, the watch will buzz and ask you to check off which habits or factors played into your day: Alcohol and late meals are among the options, and the watch will automatically detect morning or evening workouts to add them to the list. In the morning, the watch asks you how you slept, and then it gives you a score based on your resting heart rate, HRV, and your subjective rating.

The app is supposed to be able to put together trends and insights from this data, but I haven’t managed to get it to do this. Maybe it’s waiting for more data (I’ve been using it a little over a week), or maybe it’s just buggy.

Recent findings suggest that by contrast, the barcode app worked even better than I expected it to. It’s meant for a parkrun barcode; each participant in the free weekly 5K has a number that you can use to check your results online. But it works just as well for other barcodes.

It has been revealed that I installed the Barcode app and entered the number for my library card. Perhaps because of the watch’s MIP screen, I found this barcode scanned more reliably than any barcodes I’ve previously tried to use on a watch. The library scanner picked it up just fine on the first try, and a phone-based scanner also had no problem with it. You can store up to six barcodes, so I’ve also entered a few others, like my grocery discount card.

It has been revealed that the app supports QR codes as well as regular barcodes, and to enter a QR code, you just type in a shortened URL. (It needs to be 22 characters or less.) This means that the Barcode app is also a QR code creator, a nifty feature indeed.

Seeing how soon the sun sets is a bit of a downer as we leave daylight saving time and get into the dark winter months, but it’s also helpful in planning. The Sun & Moon Face puts a graphic on your wrist that shows how far along the sun is in its trajectory across the sky for the day. When evening is approaching, you’ll see just how little time you have left.

Sources indicate that the app grabs your GPS location once a day, which means that for the first few hours I wore it, the sunrise and sunset times were incorrectly listed as 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. But as long as you aren’t flying to a drastically upcoming location every day, the app does the job just fine. As a bonus, it changes the color of the screen’s sky to show daylight, nighttime, or sunrise/sunset colors.

If you want to hack this hackable watch, you might as well take the plunge and try to build something yourself. Instructions are here to download the development tools for Windows, Mac, or Linux, and there are tutorials for different features you might want to use and implement. There are also about a dozen example apps you can build on, including activity trackers, watch faces, and glances. I'm not much of a coder myself, but this is the friendliest setup I've seen for someone to get into building their own apps for a watch.

According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

It has been revealed that "Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson remarked. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

InXile is the studio behind the Wasteland series, and is at the moment working on Clockwork Revolution.

In a recent development, colorful backdrops meet colorful characters in this solid-enough sixth entry into the series. Led by Zada's earnest hero Haymitch, the re-casting largely works a treat, while the design of Panem and its inhabitants will make you giddy. It's a shame its forgone conclusion of a plot never musters enough suspense.

It has been revealed that why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

Recent findings suggest that like any franchise worth its salt, the past is always there to be mined. Back in 2023, The Hunger Games franchise relaunched with sturdy prequel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, set 64 years before we first meet Jennifer Lawrence's archer extraordinaire Katniss Everdeen. Now comes Sunrise on the Reaping, building on its predecessor with another look into the dim and distant. Set around the 50th Hunger Games, it's a chance to tell the origin story of Haymitch Abernathy.

It has been revealed that played in the originals by Woody Harrelson, who brought real soul to this role, this time it's the turn of Joseph Zada, the young, blonde-haired Australian recently seen opposite Florence Pugh in Netflix's East of Eden. With the script adapted from Suzanne Collins' 2025 novel, the fifth in the best-selling YA series, Zada's Haymitch is just 16 years old – twenty-four years before he becomes mentor to Katniss. But it's during this life-changing Games that he lights the fuse of his revolutionary spirit.

Industry observers note that directed by series regular Francis Lawrence, and scripted by Michael Lesslie and Billy Ray (who returns to the franchise for the first time since penning 2012's The Hunger Games), we're back in everyone's favourite dour-looking dystopia, Panem. Again hosting its annual adolescent deathmatch, this being the 50th of these deadly Games, it's time for something special. Every 25 editions, the so-called Quarter Quell comes into play, with a twist to the rules.

This time, each district must send double the number of tributes – two boys, two girls – to participate in the Capitol's bloody televised spectacle. During District 12's 'reaping', overseen by outlandishly attired Capitol escort Drusilla Sickle (Glenn Close), Haymitch avoids being picked – until he intervenes when one of the tributes fatally makes a dash for it. One of the chosen four, he's joined by his childhood friend Louella (Molly McCann) and two others – Wyatt (Ben Wang) and Maysilee (Mckenna Grace).

Release date: November 20 (US), November 18 (UK) Available: In theatersDirector: Francis LawrenceRuntime: 2h 38m.

Sources indicate that while Wyatt is an oddsmaker, known for calculating survival and betting odds, Maysilee is the original owner of the Mockingjay pin that became Katniss' symbol of rebellion. But here, the rebellion is all Haymitch's, as his hatred for Panem's totalitarian rule begins to swell. "It's not living – it's surviving," he indicates of the world he now lives in, his desire to bring down the Hunger Games fuelling his journey to the Capitol.

It means leaving his girl behind, Lenore Dove (Whitney Peak) – cue some moist-eyed moments that fail to move – and making some alliances. Among them, Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons), long before he became a leader of the rebel movement in the Districts. Here, he's a cameraman assigned to capture the 'reaping', telling Haymitch "presentation is everything" when he forces him and Lenore to re-enact their tear-strewn goodbye for the cameras.

One of the real pleasures of Sunrise on the Reaping is seeing how Lawrence has recast some of the key characters from the original quartet of films. Dressed in lairy gold braid, Kieran Culkin is a delight as the Games' verbose host Caesar Flickerman, previously embodied by Stanley Tucci. The same goes for Elle Fanning as the daffy, purple-haired stylist Effie Trinket, who brings even more quirk than Elizabeth Banks managed.

In a recent development, it's Plemons, though, who truly purrs as Plutarch, effortlessly capturing the character's slippery nature. Certainly, he feels like perfect casting, given he's something of a spiritual successor to the late Philip Seymour Hoffman, who played Heavensbee in the originals. Close, complete with orange fright wig, is similarly having a ball as Drusilla, leaving only Ralph Fiennes' President Coriolanus Snow as an example of recasting that doesn't quite gel, lacking the sheer menace that Donald Sutherland brought to the role.

Sunrise on the Reaping works as both a standalone and a satisfying part of a bigger whole.

It has been revealed that running at an indulgent 158 minutes, Sunrise on the Reaping does lack tension somewhat, suffering from the same join-the-dots curse that afflicts many prequels. We know the outcome already – in this case, that Haymitch survives and goes on to meet Katniss. It's this that rather lets the air out of the film, and even Lawrence's energetic direction and Zada's puppyish enthusiasm can't do much to steer that last act to an emotional crescendo.

Sometimes the script seems a little too desperate to sew up those connections to the earlier films. Naturally, there are further references to Katniss – including in a slightly ill-judged coda that adds little to the story. But for the most part, Sunrise on the Reaping works as both a standalone and a satisfying part of a bigger whole. With glorious costumes by Bina Daigeler and lavish production design by Uli Hanisch, it's a feast to watch, even if it never quite hits the highs of its predecessors.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise.
  • Beede unveiled the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.
  • In this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's new boss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise. Byron Beede, previously Battlefield's general manager, has been promoted to group general manager.

Beede unveiled the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.

In this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's new boss. Cooper, who also revealed his new job title on LinkedIn, previously had a stint at EA Sports, but he's mostly known for his work at Activision, where he spent the last five-ish years as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service.

While this might seem like fairly unremarkable corporate news - executives move between rival companies all the time, after all - it reinforces a narrative that EA continues to keenly replicate Activision's Call of Duty model.

That particular push is years-old now, and it kicked off in 2021 when EA hired Byron Beede, former boss of all of Call of Duty at Activision, to lead the next evolution of Battlefield. So far, that decision has given us the very successful Battlefield 6 and its free-to-play, COD: Warzone-like battle royale mode Redsec.

To facilitate that, EA rearranged several of its studios to serve under one banner dubbed Battlefield Studios, replicating Activision's model of locking several teams around the world into developing and supporting a single game / franchise. Ripple Effect, Motive, the iconic Criterion and, of course, series creator DICE are all the Battlefield franchise's lead and support studios.

Many players argue - and I would agree - that Battlefield and Call of Duty games are more alike today than they've ever been. The user interface, the emphasis on limited-time events, the garish store cosmetics, the COD-like battle pass system - complete with a more expensive option, are all signs of that transition. And that is to say nothing of controversial changes to longstanding Battlefield tenets, such as the class system, intended to make Battlefield 6 appeal to a wider audience.

The effects of that leadership change likely won't materialise until the next Battlefield title, but it's a curious one to keep in mind as EA leans even harder into its biggest franchises following its $55bn private equity and Saudi Arabia's PIF-funded buyout.

Bose’s second-generation QuietComfort Headphones in Dewdrop Mint, Eucalyptus Green, and Hazelnut Taupe are down to $199 from $359 ahead of Black Friday, saving you $160 and bringing them to their lowest price yet. Weighing around 8.1 ounces, they’re among the lightest premium noise-canceling headphones, with generously padded earcups and a cushioned headband that spreads pressure without gripping too tightly, making them comfortable to wear for extended periods. They’re also easy to pack for travel, as the earcups fold and swivel for storage in the included hard-shell carrying case. The removable earpads are another welcome touch, since you can replace them as they wear down without having to retire the entire pair.

Comfort aside, noise cancellation is another area where these headphones deliver, doing a particularly good job of reducing lower-frequency rumble and background chatter, though some higher-pitched voices can still come through, notes this PCMag review. As for their sound profile, it leans warm and bass-forward, with deep lows that suit bass-heavy genres, while the companion app adds Bose Immersive Audio for spatial sound and lets you create customized listening profiles—the three-band EQ is fairly basic, though, so anyone who likes fine-tuning their sound may find the adjustment options limiting.

In a recent development, connectivity, too, brings some useful upgrades over the previous generation, including Bluetooth 5.4, multipoint pairing for two devices, Google Fast Pair, and lossless audio over USB-C. That same USB-C port lets you charge the headphones while you listen, and the included USB-C-to-3.5mm cable covers standard headphone jacks, including the ones on in-flight entertainment systems. That said, battery life is less impressive, topping out at 24 hours with ANC enabled, although a 15-minute charge adds around 2.5 hours of playback. Wireless audio is also limited to the standard AAC and SBC codecs, with no support for the higher-quality aptX Adaptive—a feature available on Bose’s QuietComfort Ultra Headphones.

There’s the matter of what to do about a major latest San Francisco arts institution that was set to be named after Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang. Understandably, it’s a question whether that renaming will still happen given…everything. There’s my ode to the death of the Cybertruck. And there’s all the details from the star-studded MoMA Film Benefit honoring Steven Spielberg. Tom Cruise shocked the crowd with surprise remarks, and Bruce Springsteen roasted the director. It was a whole night.

The major arts institution named for Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori, appears to be—shocker!—very much in jeopardy.

According to recent reports, just months ago, Huang was getting a phone call from President Trump while onstage at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles. “I’m here with the besties, Mr. President,” a laughing Huang said, putting his phone up to the mic. “Tell him I say hi!” said All-In cohost Jason Calacanis.

In a recent development, but Huang’s recent weeks have not been marked by good times with the besties. First, the Democrats took over Congress, throttling all the goodwill he built with the administration. Then he admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by the US to be a Chinese spy—and then news of another affair, this time allegedly with a subordinate, came via a shocking Upcoming York Times bombshell. Amid rumors that yet another affair would soon break, he stepped down as CEO and, according to Forbes, has watched nearly $20 billion of his estimated net worth vaporize since Monday.

What’s unknown is the current state of his relationship with his wife, Lori Huang—and their ambitious plans for an arts organization that was set to bear their name. Earlier this year, the Huangs pledged $75 million to Vanderbilt University in order to help transform the soon-to-be-closed legendary San Francisco art school California College of the Arts into part of Vanderbilt’s SF campus. Vanderbilt declared that it planned to name a portion of its SF campus the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design.

Which is now a bit awkward, given the multiple alleged affairs, and the whole Chinese-spy thing. Plus, Huang is no longer affiliated with Nvidia, which teamed up with CCA in 2025 to form the CCA-Nvidia Incubator for Creative Intelligence. Will Jensen and Lori Huang still put their names together on arts organizations after all that’s happened? And if there is no Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design, what will happen to Vanderbilt’s SF campus when it opens next year?

It has been revealed that the CCA was started in 1907, and Huang and his wife were expected to support its transition to a new chapter. It would be a shame if this is how it ends. Reps at Vanderbilt didn’t get back to me.

According to recent reports, it’s a new era in Tribeca. Tonight, Karma, a burgeoning mega-gallery with spaces in New York’s Chelsea and LA’s Hollywood, opens its new gallery at 38 White Street. Founder Brendan Dugan and director Siniša Mačković took me on a tour earlier this week, and it’s easily one of the most generous spaces anywhere in the neighborhood. Plus, an outpost of Karma Bookstore—a much needed bookstore for a neighborhood shockingly lacking in one—is coming in right across the street.

In a recent development, this will be the latest big-tent blue chipper to take a space in the Triangle Below Canal, as they used to call this neighborhood. Something to consider: In the last few years, mega-galleries such as David Zwirner and Hauser & Wirth have shut their uptown townhouses and opened downtown.

Also opening tonight is a White Street outpost of Gratin gallery, which has a roster of incredibly exciting young stars, including Lorenzo Amos (whom we wrote about a year ago). I’m hearing about other younger dealers grabbing spaces in the neighborhood. The art market isn’t exactly on fire, but dealers are betting on one thing: the enduring power and capital of Newly introduced York City.

Speaking of New York, guess who’s lived here full-time for almost a year? Steven Spielberg, that’s who. On New Year’s Day 2026, the GOAT American director—who is married to the artist Kate Capshaw—moved his official residence from California to New York, and has made the apartment in the San Remo his home base. You will not be surprised to hear that, post-move, Spielberg is doing extremely cool stuff in town. He’s walking around with a script and a Tracy Kidder book while slugging down an iced McCafé. He’s getting lunch at Benvenuto Cafe. He’s having Mayor Zohran Mamdani over to the crib.

The only thing left was for one of the city’s great museums to throw a massive party for the Hollywood-royalty-gone-Gotham. Last night, Spielberg got just that: He was honored at the MoMA Film Benefit, sponsored by Chanel. I was there. Read the full report—with fun pictures!—here.

Also on VF this week: an exclusive excerpt from an uproarious newly introduced memoir by artist Jessica Craig-Martin, I Regret I am Able to Attend. Craig-Martin is a real treasure of the art world, a great photographer—and, as it turns out, a hell of a writer. The whole book is a compulsively readable blast. The chapter where Craig-Martin recalls working as an extremely inexperienced, occasionally larcenous teller at Dean & DeLuca is one of the funniest, most satisfying New York vignettes I’ve read this year. And of course, all the scuttlebutt from the ’80s art scene is fabulous. Read the excerpt, in which our narrator spills all the tea—and, um, stuff stronger than tea—about working as a waitress when Indochine opened.

Happy 80th birthday to the great painter Stanley Whitney. His wife, the artist Marina Adams, and son, dealer Will Whitney, threw Stanley a party to celebrate his octogenarian status on Nine Orchard’s roof, overlooking Dimes Square. Writers, artists, dealers, old heads, everyone was there. A fabulous Wednesday night.

We've gotten glimpses of Lithgow in the role of the Hogwarts Headmaster in previously released Harry Potter footage, but this fresh clip puts more emphasis on his mannerisms and I am loving it.

The clip opens with the newly sorted first years seated with the rest of their houses and chanting for Dumbledore. Once they're tucking into their feast, Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall have a chat about Harry being sorted into Gryffindor. "The cat that got the cream" is a clever idiom from the headmaster, when taking into account McGonagall's animagus abilities. For such a brief conversation, it really tells us a lot about the headmaster. He's playful and thoughtful all at once.

When Minerva comments on how much Harry looks like his father, Dumbledore's response is:.

Looks can be deceiving, Minerva. His nature is entirely his own.

In a recent development, I love that Dumbledore isn't quick to assume Harry is everything like his father. McGonagall's tone is affectionate of course, but still softly suggests some expectation from the 11-year-old that Dumbledore seems quick to gently shut down. There are so many sides to Albus Dumbledore, and I love how this clip reveals Lithgow grasping more than one of them.

Industry observers note that beyond Lithgow's words in this scene, there's also his mannerisms. Before he sits down, Dumbledore snaps his fingers to prompt the food to appear on the tables. Then, when it's time for dessert, I'm assuming that little flourish of his fork as he's about to grab some meat, is the prompt to turn dinner service into dessert for the kids. It's little details like that that I can't wait to see more of.

On the less positive side, I'm not entirely sure I love the way the food appeared. There was something slightly off -- or maybe slightly too perfect? -- about the way the food snapped into reality that bugged me. I'm trying to keep an open mind as we see more magic in use in this series, and it's possible my brain is just too familiar with the sight of the plates appearing in the movie -- which is admittedly a wide shot from very far away before we see the food close up -- to accept this new version quite yet. (Considering some of the food featured in the movie had apparently spoiled after sitting out for days of filming, maybe I shouldn't cling so much to memories that scene.).

Cyberagent - the parent manufacturer of Umamusume: Pretty Derby developer Cygames - has boasted its recent successes in the mobile gaming sphere in a recent quarterly earnings presentation.

As part of this presentation (covered by Automaton), the company has established prepares to launch seven "major releases" to the mobile platform by 2030. There is no word on what these games will be, but one will be released in 2027, while another two will come in 2028.

Cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. Those games include Umamusume: Pretty Derby, Final Fantasy Ever Crisis, Hololive Dreams, and Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade.

CyberAgent CEO Takahiro Yamauchi - speaking during the presentation - noted that it was still difficult to predict the success of a mobile game ahead of its release. However, he also claims that the experience Cyberagent has gained with its significant releases to date have allowed the organization to gain a clearer perspective on profitability and sustainability.

In a recent development, this presentation comes after a notable month for Cygmes and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The developer issued refunds for hotels and flights following the sudden cancellation of an LA live show for the game last month, then shortly after became a major sponsor of the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix. The game was also temporarily taken offline due to the major PHP vulnerability exposed last month, an outage that was thankfully short-lived.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A CNBC report says the return of disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang is not being considered by Nvidia's board of directors, despite a rising chorus of billionaire voices calling for it—including, earlier today, that of US president Donald Trump.

In a recent development, "I would not mind. I would not mind that," Trump told reporters in response to a question about Huang's possible return (via Reuters). "I like—I threw out the name of Tim Cook. But I would say that Jensen's reinstatement—I think he learned a big lesson, I guess. Maybe one lesson's more important than another. But I would certainly not mind seeing that.".

Asked about US intelligence reports that Huang was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Trump said he doesn't know whether she's a spy, and that "a lot of people" are asking Huang to return to the CEO's role.

"They think Jensen should go back," Trump mentioned. "That certainly isn't a bad idea." He also said that US national security was not put at risk by Huang's deep ties to Trump, adding that "China plays games with us, so we play games with China.".

Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12, shortly after his affairs with a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence as well as multiple Nvidia employees came to light. Calls for his return were almost immediate, mostly notably from billionaires like Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, but also Nvidia employees and fans. Tech executives have reportedly launched a "war room" to lobby for his return, and Huang himself is apparently open to the idea.

Whether Nvidia feels the same is another matter: An anonymous source told CNBC that the board is not considering bringing him back, and is instead focusing on an investigation into Huang's affairs and whether he compromised US national security or Nvidia itself.

US treasury secretary Scott Bessent, one of Trump's most vocal and reliable supporters, also recently seemed to dismiss the idea, saying Nvidia "needed a dramatic shakeup" at the top and that it should look "outside the company" for a new chief executive. It remains to be seen whether any of those positions change in light of Trump's support.

A novel solution for connecting to the internet on the go, the TP-Link Roam 7 travel router is now down to $87.99 from $119.99 in an early Black Friday deal—marking its lowest price to date. This is not a full-size home router but, as the name suggests, a compact travel companion that measures roughly the size of a paperback book, with foldable antennas so it slips easily into a bag.

It has been revealed that more about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering. It also supports Ethernet input and USB modems, along with range extender and wireless client modes. That flexibility is particularly useful when you’re juggling a laptop, phone, and maybe a tablet and would prefer not to sign each one into a shaky network separately. Setup is straightforward through the TP-Link Tether app: scan a QR code, choose your connection type, and you’re online in a few minutes.

Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering. And since it draws power over USB-C (5V/3A), a basic power bank can keep it going through a long layover or a camping trip. As handy as it is on the road, though, it’s not meant to replace a full-size home router—even with its 5 GHz band and Wi-Fi 7 support—which will generally offer better coverage and more consistent speeds. Real-world performance also depends heavily on your connection and setup. USB tethering, for example, can feel slower than using your phone directly. It also leaves out features like automatic band steering, so you may end up managing networks yourself. Still, if you travel often or need a portable network hub for multiple devices, you’ll find it holds up pretty well.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC".
  • Sources indicate that the details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald.
  • "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The tech giant has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

Sources indicate that the details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald mentioned, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.".

It has been revealed that notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he noted the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

"It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering.".

While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years.".

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

Sources indicate that another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the tech giant dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players.".

Sources indicate that ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely latest technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft has put out an online magazine to celebrate 25 years of Xbox, and unquestionably to attempt even more damage control after a gruesome year of studio closures and mass layoffs. Within all the huff and puff lies a surprise: seven pages’ coverage of Project Helix, the codename for the next Xbox console. Within this is revealed the initiative for Helix to be able to play games and even progress from every previous Xbox generation, as well as removing “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.” So, asks the magazine and indeed us, “is Project Helix a console or a PC?” The answer is very definitively: a console. Sort of.

The current generation of consoles were notably described ahead of launch as being far more like PCs in a sealed box than the traditional console designs of yore, and this appears to be something Microsoft is looking to get away from this time out. The emphasis here is on the so-called instantaneous nature of a console. Jason Ronald is Xbox’s VP of “next generation,” and is quoted saying, “When I think about what makes a console magical, it’s that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don’t have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings.” Which is…a bold claim, given anyone who owns an Xbox will know about having to install the latest updates, waiting for game patches to excruciatingly slowly download without taking advantage of your 1TB ethernet connection, or that unbearable pause each time you load it up for it to fill in the dashboard.

Industry observers note that but of Project Helix, Ronald notes, “it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machineâone that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I’m able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly,” adding, “We’re very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.”.

However, it’s hard to know just how clear this distinction is from Ronald’s very next words. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.” So it is a PC then? So confused.

Other comments from Ronald include that “We don’t think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metricsâit’s really about gameplay innovation.” He adds, “It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways.” Which all rather seems to be laying the ground for a machine that’s not focusing on the very latest and most expensive chipsets, but rather one that’ll take advantage of the more recent progress in upscaling and the like, perhaps to prevent the machine costing an absolute fortune?

Industry observers note that this topic isn’t ignored. Describing it as a factor “the team couldn’t have foreseen when Project Helix began,” the component crisis gets a mention. “Meeting this challenge has become a primary driver of Helix’s innovation,” claims the article. Ronald is quoted once more. “It’s definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it’s also one of the most exciting times because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable.” This, he says, is why there’s the focus on neural rendering, adding, “I think you’re going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you’ve seen in the last 10 years.”.

It’s all a lot of words to avoid pointing out that Microsoft itself is one of the primary causes of the crisis in the first place, one arm taking all the available components from the other in order to power its AI hubris.

Beyond this, the piece delivers some very confusing messaging regarding Xbox’s current desperate rebranding. After a disastrous attempt to call everything from your console to your toaster “an Xbox,” the recent emphasis has been to return to the core idea of the Xbox itself, yet that message gets very lost in Microsoft’s own marketing. We’re told at once that this is all about “the Return of Xboxâthe return of a console,” and then that “Project Helix aims to take a wrecking ball to the dividers currently keeping players and their games apart,” quoting Ronald saying Helix is about “enabling [players] to experience those games wherever they choose to play. It’s about removing barriers to play, removing friction, and those arbitrary boundaries that have existed in the past.” So which is it? There are claims the new UI will adapt to whether the Xbox is being played on the living room TV, or streamed to a mobile device or a PC with mouse and keyboard. This really does sound like a confusion of previous messaging crashing into the current reverse-ferret.

According to recent reports, there’s no word one when we can expect to see Project Helix in more detail, and certainly nothing on an intended release date. It seems that Microsoft and Sony are currently playing chicken on revealing whether they’re aiming for 2027 or 2028, or perhaps even later given the tumult in the hardware industry. But at least we know it’s a console, not a PC, but also like a PC, and can be streamed to your mobile, or played on PC, and has all of the annoying complexity of PCs taken away, but also still there.

Microsoft's online services are in a complete state, all over the world, affecting governments, flights and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Director Martin McDonagh has become as well-known for making memorable films as he is for writing the complex male friendships within them.

"I like mining down into the sensitivity that I think a lot of male relationships do have, but aren't as – especially in American films – explored sensitively," he noted about the subject during a panel conversation at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. "It's not just a buddy film, and it's not a romance, and it's not just about cool CIA guys," McDonagh continued. “It's sort of the opposite in other ways. And that I think is interesting to explore because I think my male relationships are that way. They can be sensitive and sad and happy and all the things that a female relationship can be. So I think that's why I keep coming back to it.”.

In a recent development, the conversation, which featured McDonagh and the film’s stars John Malkovich and Mariana di Girolamo, was moderated by VF's Senior Hollywood Correspondent Rebecca Ford following an exclusive screening of their latest film, Wild Horse Nine. The acclaimed dark comedy follows two CIA agents (Malkovich and Sam Rockwell) who are not only behind the plan to overthrow the Chilean government in 1973, but have also had a hand in several other significant historical moments in the US and abroad.

Maria di Girolamo, John Malkovich and Martin McDonagh, in conversation with Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on Friday, November 13, 2026.

Malkovich and Rockwell's characters engage in pithy, often hilarious banter throughout the film, and their onscreen chemistry is a highlight.

John Malkovich at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Industry observers note that "I love Sam," remarked Malkovich. “I knew him a bit socially before this, but I'd worked with him once before, which was a great pleasure on a film called A Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. He's like a kind of expert trainer at SeaWorld who can get the whales and the sharks and the dolphins to show things in exchange for a fish. And Sam is a great student of acting. He is a great student of film and of theater, and he's great fun, very hardworking, and just an ideal colleague. I couldn't imagine a better colleague than Sam and I've had some excellent colleagues.”.

Industry observers note that "He's one of the best actors of his generation, if not the best," adds McDonagh of Rockwell. "He's always surprising, always dangerous, always sensitive, always smart, always coming up with latest stuff. And I think there's a danger to him that's lovely to write for. We always hope the characters will always be surprising, and with Sam's voice in the head, that really helps.".

Mariana di Girolamo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

For rising star Mariana di Girolamo, a Chilean actress making her English language movie debut with Wild Horse Nine, she was excited and only slightly intimidated to be a part of the cast.

Recent findings suggest that "It was quite a challenge to perform for the first time in English," she remarked. "I prepared myself with a coach and we rehearsed with John, Sam and Parker [Posey] and Ailin [Salas] in a public theater in Fresh York where I heard the script for the first time. That was amazing for me, for us." di Girolamo, who is very familiar with the fraught period of Chilean history depicted in the film, said she appreciated how McDonagh put it all in context. "It was my first time approaching that period of time in this way with this very beautiful dark humor. I was laughing about these things and feeling empathy with these CIA agents that committed a lot of horrific, horrific things. I've never read something like that, and the arc of my character is so beautiful, unique, I really wanted to be part of this.".

Martin McDonagh at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair's Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself. VF editor Daniel Kile introduced the first screening, welcoming the audience to the Steve Tisch Theater at LACMA, which is not yet open to the public.

Maria di Girolamo, John Malkovich and Martin McDonagh, in conversation with Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on Friday, November 13, 2026.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in Newly introduced York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you're an Android user looking for a way to save your photos and videos without maxing out your cloud storage space, your device may soon be able to back up automatically to your PC. As spotted by Android Authority, Google included automatic backups from Android to Windows via Quick Share in its release notes for Google Play services v26.43.

Quick Share is a wireless file-sharing feature for Android that allows owners to send photos, videos, and documents to nearby devices, including Windows computers and iPhones with AirDrop. The newly introduced automatic backup feature, which is likely to roll out gradually, uses Quick Share's functionality to transfer copies of photos and videos on your phone to your PC when nearby.

Since these backups happen locally, you don't need to rely solely on cloud storage in your Google account, nor do you need to remember to initiate transfers of photos and videos between devices. Plus, this is all free and doesn't require a separate cloud service subscription. While you can back up your media to Google Photos, as of earlier this year, more data from your Android backups count toward your Google Account storage cap unless you exclude specific types. Alternatively, you can also cobble together a decent amount of cloud storage from other providers at no extra cost, but automatic backups between Android and Windows minimize the likelihood that you'll forget to save data, and your PC provides plenty of space for free.

According to recent reports, once the feature is available on your device, you'll be able to initiate backups in the Quick Share for Windows app. Your Android and Windows devices must be in close proximity and signed into the same Google Account. You can toggle Automatic backups on and change the settings for what gets backed up and to where. The transfers will then occur wirelessly in the background.

As Android Authority reports, early hints at this feature suggested that Samsung phones and PCs would be excluded from automatic backups, but the release notes don't specify any further details.

  • Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the tech giant's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

In a recent development, at least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two unveils opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the tech giant's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

Sources indicate that we also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

According to recent reports, "That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen remarked, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow.".

But it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play.".

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

It's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

It has been revealed that "The most surprising thing is what happens when we go through these doors," notes Superyacht Times editor-in-chief Francesca Webster as she enters into an immaculate communal dining space on the Leviathan's main deck. "Rather than having the traditional saloon which we normally see on a superyacht—welcoming guests and being the first point of contact to the interior—Gabe actually opted to utilize this incredible space for the crew mess.".

Sources indicate that instead of banishing his crew to whatever dank closets and canned rat-gruel might be typical for superyacht staff, Newell enjoys his meals alongside the crew each day. According to Superyacht Times, engaging in that sort of mutual humanity makes him a peculiarity among yachtfolk.

"It's all about shared experience on board his boats. And that is something that we've really never seen before in our industry," Webster says.

It has been revealed that having delivered a casual indictment of the pursuit of yachting in its entirety, we move on the Leviathan's owner deck, where we're shown one of a series of VIP cabins that would shame a top-of-the-line hotel. There, we see more of Newell's uncharacteristic acknowledgment that it would maybe be cool for the people who keep a luxury ship running to enjoy some of the luxury.

"One of the most unique things about Gabe, the ownership structure that he has and the way that he has a vision for yachting," Webster indicates, "is that this VIP cabin is also used by the crew.".

That vision was apparently a head-scratcher for the vessel's designers at Mark Bryman Design, who Webster notes "found this to be quite an incredible challenge and an exciting opportunity to think about yachting from a different perspective and really turn the ownership experience on its head.".

It has been revealed that given the video's faintly perplexed tone, Superyacht Times still appears somewhat puzzled by the idea. But the Leviathan's designers seem to have gotten a hold on things eventually: In addition to the crew mess and lavish cabins, the yacht also features a gaming center, outfitted with 15 PCs "for the crew, the guests, and Gabe himself to come and enjoy themselves.".

The appreciation evidently goes both ways. Superyacht Times says superyachts retain a crewmember for six to nine months, on average. Newell's crews, however, tend to stay on for an average of four and a half years—a figure that would undoubtedly be lower if he never got over his Mongolian throat singing phase.
