Sources indicate that one user felt the the game went too far in associating itself with the original creators. âIncluding the series name is one issue,” they wrote on X, “but I think listing the authorâs name on the store page was the biggest mistake [made in selling this game].â Others pointed out the risk of it being confused for an official work. âThe problem is that the chance of a rights holder intervening and blocking the sale of a fan game is much higher than it is for a doujin manga,â remarked one. âIt has a risk of being mistaken as an official game adaptation, and thereâs the chance it could harm [official publisher] Kadokawaâs profits if they choose to release a game with the same concept.â.

Sources indicate that if a series explicitly allows fans works, often the sale of stated worksâeven onlineâcan be permitted in select circumstances provided they don’t attempt to be seen as an official work. Some IP holders may put specific conditions on derivative works, with the expectation that fans will adhere to the rules. For example, Uma Musume creator Cygames notes that, while fans can create doujin, they are not allowed to create adult sexual works, in part due to the characters being based on real horses. One doujin creator summed it up well: âThe reason doujin tend to be allowed to exist is that they often consist of what-if scenarios that authors would like to see, but would probably not feature in the original work, meaning they donât compete with the core media. However, even if it was a doujin work, if someone wanted to create and sell a manga that was in a style that could be mistaken for the original and could be viewed as a potential continuation of that story, the chance people would intervene could increase greatly.â.

In a recent development, this is where the line was crossed in the eyes of many, leading the creator to pull the game from sale. Without permission from the rights holders, it can feel against the spirit of doujin to create something like this, regardless of a fanâs intentions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • But expansion packs are more than just a stack of a few levels, they're also an opportunity to adjust to the MMO economy.
  • There are ways to remove this money, sure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has a unique problem—it's intended to be a "forever" version of baseline Azeroth, with no planned level-increasing expansions and an emphasis on horizontal progression with only minor vertical item level increases.

But expansion packs are more than just a stack of a few levels, they're also an opportunity to adjust to the MMO economy. Which so often suffers because, well, you're essentially printing money all the time. Every enemy killed, every resource node farmed, every trash item sold, effectively adds more money into the world.

There are ways to remove this money, sure. Repair costs, flight paths, goldsinks like a mount grind, dual spec, or respec fees. But if someone's dedicated to grinding, they can put together a hundred gold in a few hours. Or, in this case, thousands.

In a recent development, as shared by WoWHead, a gold farm was discovered in Blackmaw Hold, one of its new dungeons, and thoroughly rinsed over the past couple of days: "In Blackmaw Hold, there is a room filled with around 30 Blackmaw Devotees. These creatures are non-elites that only auto-attack, but can drop a lot of loot.".

Recent findings suggest that all of that loot adds up. Silver drops and vendor items, motes, quest items—and hey, sometimes there's just a good grinding spot in an MMO. I personally made my mount money by rinsing a lucrative little ogre spot with a lot of iron ore. But in that case, I was able to scrape together a humble 15 gold an hour and a half, an honest wage for an honest day's work, whereas these folks have been raking in thousands.

Here's a clip of one such streamer leisurely jogging about with 4,000+ gold in his bags: "I slept for four hours, man, if I didn't sleep, I could've hit 5k.".

Sources indicate that this is, uh, bad—streamers are in a sense the very tip of the iceberg. If their farming spot has breached containment, then you can bet that ambitious gold sellers and farmers have already been on that grindset for longer. Exactly how much longer is up for debate, mind, since Blackmaw Hold is a high-level dungeon; but these guys are efficient. Even my leisurely pace, taking in the sights, has seen me hit level 51 since launch.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Unsurprisingly, parts of the community are baying for blood: "All of the gold that entered into the economy needs to be removed and everyone involved needs to be banned. This single exploit left unaddressed will affect WoW Forever for its entire lifespan. This gold was created by vendoring items in a raw gold farm. It's gold that was never meant to, designed to, or expected to enter into circulation. Inflation is about to ripple everywhere," writes one player on the WoW subreddit.

Making things slightly more awkward for Blizzard is the fact that the aforementioned streamer I linked above, Ziqoftw, has commentated on PvP tournaments in an official capacity before. He's made the argument on his X account that this wasn't an exploit, and that while the farm was absolutely very lucrative, a hotfix doesn't necessarily mean an exploit happened.

"Hotfixing something because it's too strong or because they don't want players to do it doesn't mean it's bugged, it means that it's too strong," Ziqo writes.

The game's terms of service define "exploits of any in-game bugs, and thereby granting you and/or any other user an advantage over other players not using such methods" as grounds for a ban, so I suppose the question is whether this was considered a bug or not.

On the one hand, it's definitely unintended, otherwise it would've been hotfixed. On the other, MMO players are like water—they'll seep into any weakness your game design has. Should Blizzard have, as Ziqo points out, given this massive group of enemies in a dungeon the exact same loot table as a normal, grindable mob out in the open world? I could probably tell you that's a bad idea.

The question right now is: What the hell does Blizzard do about it? I've reached out to the developer for comment, and I'll revision this article if I receive a response.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that sony has announced that several more games are getting a Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) upgrade on PS5.
  • Sony has announced that several more games are getting a Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) upgrade on PS5.
  • While it's not quite as good as PSSR on the PS5 Pro, QSSR still does a noticeable job of adding detail and clarity without impacting performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sony has announced that several more games are getting a Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) upgrade on PS5. Introduced in September, QSSR is an AI-guided upscaling technology similar to the PS5 Pro's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), and it originally supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei. That lineup is expanding over the next couple of weeks to include games like Control Resonant, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, The Finals, No Man's Sky, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam. While it's not quite as good as PSSR on the PS5 Pro, QSSR still does a noticeable job of adding detail and clarity without impacting performance. Sony added that since QSSR shares elements with PSSR, it makes games that support the PS5 Pro upscaling tech a "natural" fit for an upgrade on regular PS5 consoles. https://youtu.be/JYEQkLnlV7o Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is a good example, given Insomniac Games' familiarity with PSSR. The QSSR update is now available for the game, and Insomniac's head of technology, Mike Fitzgerald, stated it'll apply to both Fidelity and Performance modes. For Control Resonant, Remedy Entertainment senior graphics programmer Erik Jansson said that QSSR will offer noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail, and the update will be available in December. While there's no exact date for when Arc Raiders and The Finals will be updated, players can expect "increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements," according to Embarl Studios technical art director Mikael Linderholm. Hello Games founder Sean Murray said that the No Man's Sky QSSR update will be out in a "few weeks" and will see the game look sharper on PS5 while maintaining "the best possible" frame rate. Finally, Paul Rustchynsky, game director at Expression Games, said that Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will also look cleaner and sharper on PS5 when the update is eventually available. If you're interested in seeing how different several of the games look with QSSR enabled, you can click the links below to see comparison videos: Control Resonant Arc Raiders No Man's Sky Hell Let Loose: Vietnam The PS5 turns six years old later this month, and as of November 10, it has surpassed 100 million consoles sold. Ordinarily, all eyes would be on the next PlayStation generation at this point--which Sony indicates it is working on--and advances like QSSR may squeeze more life out of the PS5 before its successor arrives. Whatever form the next PlayStation takes, don't expect it to be cheap, as the current generation has gotten more expensive since 2020 and the PS6 could cost over $1,000. Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden recently touched on the topic, and he spoke about how true innovation from Sony would come in the form of cheaper hardware, not just better graphics.

In a recent development, the whole endeavor began as it usually does, with a search for the perfect dress. Stylist Brad Goreski and his assistant Clarke, who work with my mother, Demi Moore, sourced the ensemble after finding Mom’s beautiful black ruffled two-piece (adorably also Carolina Herrera).

Around 6:50 p.m. on Saturday, my older sisters, Scout (in cocoa-brown beaded Elie Saab) and Rumer (in whimsical archival Vera Wang), florist Eric Buterbaugh, Brad, my mom and I are about to leave her house for the Baby2Baby Gala, an annual fundraiser for the non-profit that dedicated to providing diapers, clothing, and other basic necessities to children and families in need across the country.

Demi is taking photos against a pale brown backdrop when I hear her say, marginally worried, “Yes, the outfit is amazing, but they didn’t give me pockets.” I cannot fault her. A pocket, particularly in an evening gown, creates an entirely different architecture for one’s night.

It has been revealed that when we make it to the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, Rihanna is blasting and a gorgeous electric General Motors car, part of the silent auction, is parked out front. I’m holding the bottom of my dress to avoid any “yard sales” on the carpeted floor when I hear, “Is it you? I hope it’s you!” It’s my very newly introduced, lovely friend Jackie Tohn, whom I met at a Nobody Wants This premiere party.

Recent findings suggest that inside, beautifully dressed people laugh and chat. I spot Miranda Kerr, who is both a Baby2Baby board member and major donor, and pass Nara Smith leaning over a dolled-up Elsa Hosk while “Espresso” blasts from overhead speakers.

Table 4 is front and center. Some could say the best seats in the house. Fitting, as Baby2Baby is honoring my mother with the Giving Tree Award tonight. The scene around our table is a frenzy of joyful energy. I make a beeline for Paris Hilton to thank her for the facial I received at her spa this week, while Dancing With the Stars alums Rumer and Jenna Dewan immediately pull out their phones to compare pictures of their kids.

Then I spot Sofia Richie Grainge and her husband, Atlantic Records CEO Elliot Grainge. I snake through throngs of elegant people and poke Elliot’s back twice. “Elliot, it’s Tallulah! We went to Wildwood together!” He instantly remembers me. “Tallulah was the cool girl in class,” he tells Sofia. I blush, but don’t feel the need to correct him.

Scout approaches and says, almost incredulously, “Hi, I’m Scout…you guys just signed me at Atlantic Records.” Elliot grabs her shoulders. “We’re so happy to have you. Are you happy with us?” She can’t say “yes” fast enough.

The program begins with Keke Palmer, who completely owns the stage, telling hilarious stories about her son before shifting into heartfelt candor about the gift of watching him grow. Kerry Washington thanks the sponsors and reveals Baby2Baby’s newly introduced permanent headquarters, “a promise to millions of children. Not just for today, but for decades to come.”.

Sources indicate that then Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, the organization’s CEOs, come to the stage, sharing the work—no, the magic—they have created over 15 years. Their first gala in 2012 raised $1 million. Last year’s raised $18 million. To date, they’ve distributed an astonishing 850 million essential items to people in need across all 50 states, responded to over 150 disasters, developed their own diaper production line during COVID, and expanded into mental health support for new mothers. The mission remains the same, but the scale is impossible to comprehend.

Sources indicate that now Rumer, Scout, and I are all crying during a short video about two families impacted by Baby2Baby. The feeling is palpable for the rest of the room.

As the live auction begins, I catch my mom discreetly reading over a printout of her speech. I don’t feel nerves coming off her, but a desire to match the elegance and integrity surrounding us.

Andrew Garfield takes the stage and speaks directly to my mom about the woman he knows. “She is a miracle,” he claims.

Industry observers note that then it’s Demi’s turn. Holding her gleaming award in two hands, she thanks Andrew for carving out time amid his Artificial press tour. My mother adores Andrew, a feeling shared across our family.

Recent findings suggest that alone on stage in her Carolina gown (sans pockets), she asks everyone to breathe. “Inhale. Exhale.” That breath, she notes, is the relief Baby2Baby provides when a mother no longer has to choose between dinner and diapers. “Your child matters, you matter, and you are not alone.” She leaves us with the idea that the essence of this work is to be remarkably human. Baby to baby, mother to mother, soul to soul.

According to recent reports, then Cardi B takes the stage and the atmosphere shifts with a jolt. Everyone is on their feet dancing. The official after-party begins, but I’m turning back into a pumpkin in towering satin stilettos. It was a remarkably beautiful night, and I’m left with the overwhelming desire to do more—to show up for someone who may not have the ability to show up for themselves or their precious loved ones.

But for this on-scene reporter’s inaugural correspondence, it was ultimately Baby2Baby2Bedtime.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, physical games are dying, unless your game is called The Legend of Zelda.
  • “After just one week in market, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is 2026’s best-selling physical video game in the US,” Circana senior director and video game industry advisor Mat Piscatella posted on Bluesky on November 16.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NintendoPhysical GamesRemakeThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time.

According to recent reports, physical games are dying, unless your game is called The Legend of Zelda. The Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time just sold 1 million physical copies in its first week in the U.S., the most of any release since Tears of the Kingdom released in 2023.

“After just one week in market, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is 2026’s best-selling physical video game in the US,” Circana senior director and video game industry advisor Mat Piscatella posted on Bluesky on November 16. “It is the 1st title to surpass 1M physical units in a US launch week since 2023’s The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.”.

Nintendo previously announced that Ocarina of Time sold 5.2 million copies globally across physical and digital in its first four days, which blew the original game’s debut on Nintendo 64 out of the water. It’s a wild number when you consider it’s a Switch 2 exclusive. The newest Nintendo console has only been out for roughly 18 months and only has an install base of around 26 million units, making the attach rate for the game nearly one in five.

There are, of course, two ways to take the Ocarina of Time remake’s physical game sales milestone. The first is to see it as a sign of how strong Switch 2 owners’ attachment to cartridge-based gaming remains even as digital swallows most of the market for game sales. The other is to note that no other game has managed to sell 1 million physical copies in the U.S. within its first week in over three years.

It has been revealed that physical game sales in the U.S. hit a 30-year low in 2025. Back in July, amid the frenzy over Sony’s announcement of the end of PlayStation discs in 2028, Piscatella pointed out that only seven PS5 games released in the first half of 2026 had sold more than 100,000 physical copies at the time. Total spending on physical games actually bounced upward this past August, however, which appears to have been thanks to Switch 2 game key cards.

Physical games might be dying, but on Switch 2 they’re not going without a fight.

GTA 6 And These Other Games Can Justify An $80 Price, Expert Indicates

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1266 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it.
  • In a recent development, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it.
  • It has been revealed that according to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott, $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. That's a full $20 more than what GTA 5 cost in 2013 and $10 more than many other substantial AAA games today. Is $80 going to become the "new normal" for AAA games, or is it, along with Nintendo's Mario Kart World and Tears of the Kingdom for Switch 2, an outlier at $80? According to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott, $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games. Some developers will purposefully price their games lower to draw in more consumers--he pointed to games like Expedition 33 ($50), Phantom Blade Zero ($60), and Oblivion Remastered ($50) as examples. A scene from GTA 6. Elliott remarked that when GTA 6 inevitably becomes a huge success with its $80 and $100 editions, some publishers will be "jumping for joy" because they'll take this as a signal that the market will indeed accept these higher prices. However, Elliott said he hopes the industry doesn't learn the wrong lessons from GTA 6 and its $80 price point. "GTA 6 is as inelastic as things get in entertainment. People will pay anything to get their mitts on this one, which makes it seem like the perfect Trojan horse for an industry-wide price rise," he said. "The $80 price point will be a Godsend to some publishers, but it’ll be a snowball's chance in hell for others. After all, this kind of stuff can be zero-sum. When a player spends $100 on GTA 6, their remaining budget shrinks," he added. Elliott went on to list off some of the studios and game franchises that could likely get their fanbases to buy in at $80. He said these include the next big God of War game after Laufey, the next Naughty Dog game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and future Forza titles (assuming Xbox strips them out of Game Pass). Additionally, Elliott said From Software "has the cache" to charge $80 for its new games, while Hogwarts Legacy 2 could also up the price to $80. Elliott added that some of the top sports games could charge more, but that might be a tougher sell considering those games are full of microtransactions already. "So not all games were created equal, and mid-tier AAA publishers--and also bigger publishers offering smaller games or remakes--will price downward at $40-$60," Elliott said. There are a lot of factors at play here. For starters, GTA 5 introduced at $60 back in 2013, and that same $60 is worth $86 today after inflation, making GTA 6--at least its $80 edition--effectively cheaper than GTA 5. At the same time, many people are acutely aware that their pay has not kept up with inflation, while the federal minimum wage hasn't moved up since 2009. GTA 6 is also coming out at a rough time for many people, with gas and grocery prices surging, and the cost of everyday goods generally spiking due in part to increasing inflation. And anyone heading to a store to buy a console to play GTA 6 on is in for some serious sticker shock, as game consoles today are more expensive than ever due to the AI craze. New video games generally staying the same price over the years has had serious negative effects on the entire industry, experts have said. It's part of the reason why publishers now try to squeeze people more with DLC, battle passes, microtransactions, collector's editions, paid early access, and more. Recently, an Xbox advertising chief said price increases would be a hard sell, so the manufacturer is turning to ads to help offset ballooning budgets and keep the business healthy.

Recent findings suggest that there are a lot of factors at play here. For starters, GTA 5 rolled out at $60 back in 2013, and that same $60 is worth $86 today after inflation, making GTA 6--at least its $80 edition--effectively cheaper than GTA 5.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, many people are acutely aware that their pay has not kept up with inflation, while the federal minimum wage hasn't moved up since 2009. GTA 6 is also coming out at a rough time for many people, with gas and grocery prices surging, and the cost of everyday goods generally spiking due in part to increasing inflation. And anyone heading to a store to buy a console to play GTA 6 on is in for some serious sticker shock, as game consoles today are more expensive than ever due to the AI craze.

According to recent reports, newly introduced video games generally staying the same price over the years has had serious negative effects on the entire industry, experts have said. It's part of the reason why publishers now try to squeeze people more with DLC, battle passes, microtransactions, collector's editions, paid early access, and more. Recently, an Xbox advertising chief said price increases would be a hard sell, so the manufacturer is turning to ads to help offset ballooning budgets and keep the business healthy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the company's official website raised confusion--and curiosity-- about a classic 3DS Zelda game. A "History" page on Nintendo's website lists every mainline Zelda game in release order, including the release date and which platforms you can play for each entry. The site marks every game that's playable for Nintendo Switch Online subscribers--and the 2013 3DS game The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds was marked as such. The NSO icon has since been removed from the site. At the moment, the Nintendo Classics library allows NSO subscribers to play select NES, SNES, and Game Boy games, while the Expansion Pack subscription includes access to Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Virtual Boy games. There's currently no way to play 3DS games on Nintendo Switch, prompting the question of whether this was an error on Nintendo's website or an accidental leak that A Link Between Worlds will somehow be playable on Switch. GameSpot has reached out to Nintendo for clarification on the matter. Nintendo's official website briefly listed A Link Between Worlds as a playable game through NSO. The site appropriately labels the Zelda games featured on Nintendo Classics if they are only playable with the Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack subscription, which applies to Ocarina of Time (the original), Majora's Mask, A Link to the Past/Four Swords on GBA, The Wind Waker, and The Minish Cap. If this labeling for A Link Between Worlds were true, it would be surprising if the Expansion Pack were not required to play it. Nintendo Classics also lacks any Wii or DS games, so jumping straight to 3DS would be a bizarre move for the service. Whatever the case, A Link Between Worlds is a magnificent entry in the Zelda series that deserves to be experienced. GameSpot's 9/10 review of the game called it an "absolute treat to play" with some of the "best Zelda dungeons in years.".

Three Ways to Avoid CAPTCHA Prompts When Using a VPN

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (991 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that VPNs make it harder to track your online activity across websites, but it also makes them suspicious about your origins.
  • Sources indicate that that noted, you don’t have to keep clicking on those traffic lights over and over.
  • CAPTCHAs are simple puzzles that websites use to filter out bots and spam.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that VPNs make it harder to track your online activity across websites, but it also makes them suspicious about your origins. When you borrow an IP address that hundreds of other people are also using for any number of reasons, you’re much more likely to get repeat verification requests from online firewalls.

Sources indicate that that noted, you don’t have to keep clicking on those traffic lights over and over. You can simply switch to a more reputable VPN server. Moreover, browsers now offer persistent access tokens to eliminate CAPTCHA requests, while VPNs offer dedicated IPs to keep sites from getting suspicious. Here are three easy fixes for repeat CAPTCHA prompts when using a VPN, so you don’t have to trade convenience for online privacy.

CAPTCHAs are simple puzzles that websites use to filter out bots and spam. They’re supposed to be easy for people but hard for robots, such as simple object recognition tasks or audio-visual challenges. However, they can still disrupt your browsing experience if they happen too frequently.

Most modern CAPTCHA providers, like Google's reCAPTCHA v3 or Cloudflare Turnstile, start working long before they give you a puzzle to solve. It usually starts with a risk score that studies your IP address, browser and device signals, or recent online activity.

If the CAPTCHA provider can’t confidently identify your request as human based on those signals, it requests that you complete a puzzle before deciding if the request should be blocked. That means when you get repeat CAPTCHA requests, there’s something affecting your browser’s risk score. For example, popular VPN servers spread the same IP address across any number of users, which can easily make a website mistake you for a bot farm. If you change your IP address frequently by switching servers often, that might look suspicious too.

Luckily, there are ways to deal with frequent CAPTCHA requests using tools and services available with your browser and VPN. Cloudflare has already cut its CAPTCHA requests by 91% using its Managed Challenge platform. Apple has also been shipping token-based verification on devices since iOS 16 and macOS Ventura. In June 2026, Cloudflare even confirmed a joint effort called the Private Access Control Tokens (PACT) standard with Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Shopify.

While there’s no direct off switch for CAPTCHAs, you can use different fixes to improve your browser’s trust signals when using the internet. That way, you’re less likely to be hounded by verification requests.

Industry observers note that the easiest fix for repeat CAPTCHAs is to stop connecting to whichever server your VPN app picks automatically. Proton recommends choosing servers with lower traffic load. In fact, its apps display load as a percentage to help you avoid the most crowded options. I'd also skip massive traffic hubs like New York or London, since that's where most traffic originates from. Servers in smaller cities located nearby are often just as fast but never as populated.

Industry observers note that you should also avoid changing IP addresses too frequently, which can look suspicious on its own. Pick a server that seems to behave well, then continue using it for at least one session. Also remember you’re more likely to get premium server options if you’re on a paid VPN strategy. Major platforms like ExpressVPN, Surfshark, Proton, and Nord are particularly likely to have a larger server collection to pick from.

Costs nothing more than your current subscription.

Easy to switch to a different location.

Server reputations shift over time.

Hopping between servers often can backfire.

Free plans limit server options.

It has been revealed that private Access Tokens (PAT) let you verify the authenticity of your request using your device rather than an IP address. Apple calls it Automatic Verification, where an Apple server validates your device and Apple Account to assign you an anonymous token.

According to recent reports, to enable Automatic Verification on an iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification. On a Mac, open System Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, there’s no equivalent feature for Windows, Android, and Linux people. That remarked, Cloudflare offers the Silk extension for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge that serves a similar function. A quick look at the ratings will tell you it’s not as effective, but Cloudflare’s upcoming cross-browser standard called PACT seems promising once it is released.

Enabled by default on Apple devices.

Doesn't depend on your VPN or IP address.

Doesn’t share personal details with websites.

Native support for Apple devices only.

Not every site requests privacy tokens.

Chrome and Firefox extensions can be unreliable.

If you pay a bit extra for a dedicated IP add-on, VPN providers can assign you a unique IP address that isn’t shared with anyone else. For example, NordVPN offers dedicated IPs in 30 countries for $2-5 a month and Surfshark charges $3.75 a month for it.

It has been revealed that there are also dedicated providers like Private Internet Access, which charges $3.99 per month for a zero-trust setup so not even their employees know which IP address is assigned to you. On the other hand, Proton VPN offers dedicated IPs only to business initiative people, so you’ll need to be on the Workspace Standard, Premium, or Enterprise intends to get one.

That said, there is a trade-off here too. NordVPN itself admits that a dedicated IP makes it easier to link online activity back to a single user. Also, many websites can still tell that the IP address originated from a VPN data center rather than a consumer’s device.

Get unique IP addresses with pristine reputation.

Works across desktop, mobile, and even smart TVs.

Also functions as an allowlisted address for work.

Add-ons cost more on top of the VPN subscription.

Offers less anonymity than shared VPN servers.

Locations are locked in once you pay.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has been in the wild for one week, and now we have all kinds of stats to sink our teeth into as they relate to the most popular races, classes, and faction in the latest version of developer Blizzard's MMORPG. Forever launched November 4, becoming the biggest launch in WoW history by concurrent and returning players. Aside from that fact, Blizzard hasn't shared additional information on exactly how many characters have been made or what classes are most popular. For that, we turn to Raider.IO, a WoW stat-tracking website more commonly used in the modern version of the game to provide rankings and details related to raids and Mythic+ progression. A snapshot of WoW: Forever stats after one week. According to the site, close to 3.9 million characters have been created across all regions and rulesets so far. Around 48% of those characters are on the Alliance, with nearly 52% being on the Horde. The most popular two races aren't all that surprising--undead and humans. Despite being the most boring choice imaginable, humans have always been a popular choice in WoW Classic thanks to their strong passives and the ability to be most classes. In Forever, they presently make up 37% of the Alliance population. Undead, on the other hand, are getting a massive boost from being the only Horde race to currently have access to Paladin. They make up nearly 40% of the Horde. It won't shock you to learn then that Paladin is Forever's most-played class, with undead Paladin being the most-played race-and-class combo. https://youtu.be/miSndSl23bI?si=HvpVU0DwfYesBiVS Skyborne elves are WoW's newest playable race, available to both factions. Around 10% of all characters are Skyborne, and faction-wise they are fairly even. Around 10% of Skyborne are Alliance and close to 11% are on the Horde. It has been revealed that the most popular two races aren't all that surprising--undead and humans. Despite being the most boring choice imaginable, humans have always been a popular choice in WoW Classic thanks to their strong passives and the ability to be most classes. In Forever, they currently make up 37% of the Alliance population. Undead, on the other hand, are getting a massive boost from being the only Horde race to currently have access to Paladin. They make up nearly 40% of the Horde.

It won't shock you to learn then that Paladin is Forever's most-played class, with undead Paladin being the most-played race-and-class combo.

Industry observers note that skyborne elves are WoW's newest playable race, available to both factions. Around 10% of all characters are Skyborne, and faction-wise they are fairly even. Around 10% of Skyborne are Alliance and close to 11% are on the Horde. Consdiering how popular blood elves are in other versions of the game, the number of Skyborne feels low by comparison, though the fact they cost $30 to access probably has something to do with that.

As for what rulesets are most popular, the normal (PvE) server is far and away the biggest, with over 2 million characters. The PvP ruleset isn't too far behind with around 1.5 million characters. Those two rulesets dwarf the size of the game's two RP rulesets, which combined have around 250,000 players.

In a forum post, Blizzard confirmed its goal is for PvP servers to be as close to 50/50 faction balance as possible, and would be placing restrictions on creating Horde characters on PvP rulesets in an effort to make that a reality.

"World of Warcraft: Forever's PvP is at its best when the Alliance and Horde are on equal footing, and we are dedicated to helping maintain that balance so that we can all witness battles at the epic scale that has made WoW: Forever PvP so memorable thus far," Blizzard mentioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem are very selective about when they work on a project together, but the opportunity to costar in director Florian Zeller's timely psychological thriller Bunker was too enticing to pass up.

"When [Zeller] came to us with this powerful, very necessary story to tell, we looked at each other and there was no way to say no to this," Cruz said during a post-screening discussion at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room on Sunday. "I'm very, very happy that we did it.".

Bunker revolves around a married couple, Miguel (Bardem) and Sofia (Cruz), whose 17-year marriage is tested when Miguel, a famous architect, is presented with a life changing work opportunity.

Industry observers note that “I really wanted to work with them because I truly believe they are [two] of the greatest actors working today,” Zeller said during the panel discussion moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross. “I was also very excited and interested to have them together onscreen because they are also a real couple. I thought it would be an interesting and unique opportunity to approach something that has to do with authenticity, with the truth. Not to say that this is their story, because of course this is not their story.”.

Florian Zeller at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

Cruz mentioned she felt a kinship with her character's concerns. “We have so many things in common in terms of this sadness and frustration and anger that you feel in terms of where is the world going if we don't wake up soon,” she said. “I hope it's not too late, but especially the experiment that is being done on younger people, children, teenagers, it just makes me very furious.

“It's something that affects me so much as an actress, as a mother, as a citizen of the world, that I felt completely a need to play Sophia,” she continued. “And of course it was not the only reason, but it was a significant privilege to be able to say those lines. And [Zeller] is such a master of writing and I am a fan of all his work. And same for Javier, who is not here with us today, he's doing theater, but we are very careful in terms of choosing when to work together.”.

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

Industry observers note that cruz praised Zeller’s ability to provide a supportive, safe working environment and his strong point of view. “We felt really, really safe with him, he's so talented. He doesn't need any kind of manipulation and he never treats the audience as not intelligent because the audience can feel everything,” she explained. “And that has become really the most key thing for me. Don't over-explain, don't underestimate the audience ever because the thermometer is really working. And also with young people more and more and more. That is my hope to continue to go to see films on a big screen. They're coming back thank God. So let's create more possibilities so they can keep doing that.”.

Cruz also said that she and Bardem have similar approaches to their work and the preparation it requires. “It's true that we share the same passion and we have done this since we were teenagers,” she said. “We love exploring and studying and feeling that healthy fear of the unknown because every time you begin a project, in a way, it's really starting from zero. So it's a really good thing to share.”.

Zeller called his collaboration with the couple “a fascinating journey. It takes a lot of courage or fearlessness to do that, I think, for actors.” He also revealed that he initially referenced Stanley Kubrick's seminal thriller Eyes Wide Shut as a point of reference for Bunker, but realized it might not be setting the proper tone, given the circumstances.

According to recent reports, “I remember that the first time I spoke with [Cruz] and Javier about this project, I mentioned a film that was somewhere in my mind, Eyes Wide Shut. Not to say that there is any kind of connection between the two films, but as you remember, Eyes Wide Shut at the time, Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, they were together," he mentioned. "And I remember as a viewer that it was so interesting to be in a position where you do not know exactly what you're invited to watch… but Javier [later] told me, ‘You should not mention this film too often because remember at the end of the shooting they broke up.’ And then I realized that the director, Kubrick, died soon after. So I was like, ‘Okay, I'm going to stop mentioning this film.’ But the real difference I would say is that we knew that the destination of that film was the last image of the painting that you saw, which means that it was about how to reconnect with the other.”.

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to be a gigantic commercial success, but just how significant will the launch be? Investor's Business Daily compiled data from a series of analyst reports about the game and its owner, Take-Two, and the consensus is that it's going to be a juggernaut. In terms of sales, Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets said GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies during Take-Two's fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2027. He said the game could sell 45 million units alone during the game's launch quarter, which is well ahead of the estimates of 34.2 million that IBD compiled. "This is an outlier in every respect," Circana's Mat Piscatella told the publication. "There have been some big game launches in the past, but nothing quite at this scale, not only in terms of the investment, but in terms of the anticipation. It's in its own league." GTA 6 is launching with an $80 standard edition and a $100 Ultimate Edition. Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok said he's forecasting 50 million unit sales for the fiscal year 2027, and that the blended average selling price will be close to $90. According to Sensor Tower, early data suggested preorders were skewing toward the $100 edition, but by launch, it could be around 50/50. Matthew Cost of Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, said if GTA 6 does indeed have strong sales out of the gate, this could create a "large potential audience" for the next iteration of GTA Online. Rockstar has not said anything yet about an online mode for GTA 6, but given the huge success of GTA Online for GTA 5, it's all but guaranteed that GTA 6 will incorporate online multiplayer as well. Cost said this is a big deal for investors and may represent "the next major catalyst" for Take-Two's stock price. Take-Two's share price is down about 10% so far in 2026, and currently trades around $228/share.. A latest version of GTA Online for GTA 6 would no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways to spend more money, and that could be frustrating for fans but great news for investors who want to see bigger returns. D.A. Davidson analyst Wyatt Swanson said Take-Two's share price could surge to $300 in part because he believes Rockstar will release a PC edition of GTA 6 and usher in GTA Online 2.0. These releases would "enable structurally higher margins" for Take-Two, he said. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has already sold 12 million copies and generated $1.2 billion in revenue. GTA 5, meanwhile, took 72 hours to clear $1 billion in revenue--GTA 6 reached that a week before release, apparently. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

#16576. Industry News: AMD introduces Capacity Aware Scheduling to the Linux kernel, which sure is the thing I'd do if I were introducing Zen 6 LP cores next year

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (635 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: AMD introduces Capacity Aware Scheduling to the Linux kernel, which sure is the thing I'd do if I were introducing Zen 6 LP cores next year

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that AMD's Vishal Badole recently posted two Linux kernel patches (via TechPowerUp), and these both pair up to introduce Capacity Aware Scheduling (CAS) for AMD heterogeneous processors.
  • It has been revealed that up until now, AMD's performance scaling driver for Linux (amd-pstate) treated all cores as equal, assigning tasks regardless of core strength.
  • But Zen 6's full lineup is currently suggested to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that AMD's Vishal Badole recently posted two Linux kernel patches (via TechPowerUp), and these both pair up to introduce Capacity Aware Scheduling (CAS) for AMD heterogeneous processors. If that sounds like gibberish to you, effectively, this lays the groundwork to more efficiently handle AMD chips that have different core types.

It has been revealed that up until now, AMD's performance scaling driver for Linux (amd-pstate) treated all cores as equal, assigning tasks regardless of core strength. AMD's current heterogeneous design pairs full-fat Zen 5 and lower-caste Zen 5C cores together in Zen 5 chips nowadays, but there is far less actual difference between these two core types than in the P-cores and E-cores of modern Intel architectures.

But Zen 6's full lineup is currently suggested to be quite different. Also shared in a Linux patch earlier this year, Zen 6 is set to introduce a new Low Power core type (which is set to run at a very low power, as you might guess from the name), and that is a core type that would really benefit from Capacity Aware Scheduling.

Recent findings suggest that what AMD has called Performance and Efficiency cores up until now is not the same as what Intel has called Performance and Efficiency cores. AMD's Efficiency cores are effectively just compact versions of the Performance cores, whereas Intel's E and P cores have different microarchitectures and are specifically tailored for different use cases.

The upcoming Zen 6 LP cores appear to be similar to Intel's LPE (Low Power Efficiency) cores you will find in its Panther Lake chips. And as such, the need for CAS makes more sense. If AMD LP cores take after Intel LPE cores, they will be tuned down to run on a very low power limit, so differentiating between cores will allow the system to more efficiently divvy up tasks.

Industry observers note that the introduction of CAS isn't just good for the eventual introduction of AMD Zen 6 LP cores (or whatever they will be called when they launch). Badole explained that this change should help even with current heterogeneous processors (Zen 4 and Zen 5). They say, "The scheduler sees every CPU as having identical capacity and treats performance and efficiency cores as interchangeable. Tasks are therefore placed and balanced without regard to core strength, which hurts both throughput and energy efficiency on hybrid systems.".

Up until now, the extra efficiency gains from CAS would only be a bonus, but if Zen 6 LP cores are low-power enough, it could be needed for them to operate properly, given what we expect will be a much lower power draw, and therefore much lower performance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I knew Spider-Man: Brand New Day would make a ridiculous amount of money when it landed on this summer's 2026 movie schedule. What I didn't expect was to hear Sony's top movie executive making a serious case for Tom Holland's latest superhero adventure to earn a Best Picture Oscar nomination. But here we are, and apparently, the studio is prepared to put some real effort into making it happen.

In a recent development, sony Pictures Motion Picture Group chairman and CEO Tom Rothman recently spoke with Variety about the movie's extraordinary success and why he believes it deserves Academy voters' consideration. With Brand New Day earning roughly $2.5 billion worldwide and breaking the domestic box office record, Rothman thinks there's something special about how audiences connected with Peter Parker's story. He explained:.

The reason it did as much business as it did is not because it's a superhero movie, it's because it's a super person movie.

In a recent development, I actually get what he's saying. While I enjoyed the action in Brand New Day, what stuck with me was how much of the movie focused on Peter's loneliness after the events of No Way Home. Here's a guy who can swing between skyscrapers and take down some of Marvel's most dangerous villains, but he can't get the people he loves to remember who he is. That's a pretty miserable situation, even by Peter Parker standards.

Audiences clearly responded as well. The film received overwhelmingly positive reviews. It also became the highest-grossing movie in North American box office history, an accomplishment I imagine Sony will mention quite a bit over the next few months. But does all that mean it deserves an Oscar nomination?

Rothman certainly thinks so. When asked whether or not a strong box office means Brand Newly introduced Day should be a Best Picture contender, he responded:.

According to recent reports, once upon a time there were five best picture nominations, and then it was expanded to ten, to try to make room, I think, for quality commercial filmmaking… we’re biased, but we think [it should be nominated] so. We hope people will think about it.

In a recent development, sony is backing up those comments with an actual campaign. According to Deadline, the studio has hired awards consultants and is planning special screenings and filmmaker Q&As beginning ahead of Thanksgiving. There's also talk of a theatrical rerelease designed to put the movie back in front of audiences and Academy voters.

In a recent development, of course, superhero movies have historically struggled to crack the Best Picture category. Black Panther earned a nomination in 2019, followed by Joker the next year, but neither won. Even Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight missed a Best Picture nomination, despite earning eight Oscar nods and winning two.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

As for Spider-Man, the character, he hasn't exactly been an Academy favorite. Sam Raimi's Spider-Man 2 won Best Visual Effects in 2005, while Into the Spider-Verse took home Best Animated Feature in 2019. Although no movie starring the web-slinger has ever competed for Best Picture.

Still, I can understand Rothman's reasoning. Director Destin Daniel Cretton made a movie that made room for surprisingly intimate character moments, even amid all the enormous superhero spectacle. CinemaBlend's Jerrica Tisdale previously explained why that balance made the movie work so well, and I think it's a fair argument. Whether Academy voters agree is another matter entirely.

The nominations for the 99th Academy Awards will be announced Jan. 21, 2027, and Brand Newly introduced Day will have some stiff competition. After watching what Sony and Marvel accomplished with Peter Parker this summer, I'm certainly not going to dismiss the idea outright. Besides, if anybody deserves a little recognition after everything he's been through, it's Peter Parker. The poor guy could use a win.

Most Spider-Man movies, past and present, are available to stream with your Disney+ subscription.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Bialy] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally mentioned, “You may think we’re crazy.
  • Sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, while the Breaking Bad universe would eventually expand to include dozens of characters, the pilot was actually a tidy affair. At its center was Walter White, whose journey would require an actor of extraordinary depth and nuance. It’s not an exaggeration to say that the success or failure of Breaking Bad would rest primarily on his sagging shoulders.

Industry observers note that SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Bialy] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally mentioned, “You may think we’re crazy. We hope you don’t fire us before you hire us. But what about Bryan Cranston?” And he said, “By golly, that’s who I want. I worked with him on The X-­ Files.”.

Sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time. We were doing Aaron Sorkin’s fresh play [The Farnsworth Invention], and Bryan came in and read. We were blown away. He was so talented on Malcolm in the Middle, obviously, but this was live theater with a lot of language. Anyway, Bryan didn’t get the role, but his audition was incredible. And I never forgot it.

Sources indicate that VINCE GILLIGAN, creator: Bryan was the only guy I was thinking of when I wrote the script. I had written an episode of The X-­ Files called “Drive,” which came out in 1998, and I was lucky enough to hire him to play the bad guy.

Sources indicate that we were really struggling to cast this role because we needed a guy who could be really scary, someone who could make us feel like our hero, Agent Mulder, could get his head blown off at any second. But also, he had to be kind of an asshole. [Throughout the episode] he’s ranting about the government. He’s ranting about stuff like, “Agent Mulder— is that a Jewish name?”.

He’s a thoroughly unlikable guy. And yet you had to feel bad for him, for what happens to him at the end of the episode. You had to feel sympathy.

Recent findings suggest that we only had a day or two left before production was going to start. We were going to have to settle on somebody. We had plenty of actors come in who were scary as all get out, but they weren’t necessarily likable. And then this guy walks in the door: Bryan Cranston. Never heard of him before. And he nails it in the audition. As he left, we all stood up and shook his hand, and then I looked to the other producers and to Rick Millikan, our casting director, and I noted, “Off to wardrobe!” He was that good.

Sources indicate that when I came up with the idea of Breaking Bad, I thought, This is a guy who, again, is going to be very unlikable. He’s going to do a lot of unlikable things, and the audience still has to sympathize with him. Who would be good for this role? I know! That guy, Bryan Cranston. And I wrote it for him. I never really had anyone else in mind.

It has been revealed that MELISSA BERNSTEIN, co-executive producer: He was in an episode of X-­Files, playing this racist, and somehow, over the course of the episode, you go from loathing him to feeling badly that he doesn’t make it. He just was able to make someone so unsavory be human. Vince also said, “And he’s so great with comedy. I just feel it in my bones that he could bring those chops to drama—­his sense of timing, the way he embodies those choices physically. He’s perfect.”.

BRYAN CRANSTON: I instruct young actors all the time that without a healthy dose of luck, you will not have a career. And this [episode of The X-­ Files] was a lucky break for me.

It has been revealed that I had just gotten back from shooting this little movie that I wrote and directed, called Last Chance. I spent all of our money on it, and by the end I was like, Wow, what are we doing on this film? But we rolled the dice on it, and now I was back in town and got a call from my agent about an audition. I noted, “Whatever it is, let me know, because I really could use the money.” It just so happened that my look at the time, from this movie that I did, was a perfect look for this guy [on The X-­Files]. So, I went in, and I got the job—­and I was grateful for it.

It’s only in retrospect that I realized Vince Gilligan wanted to see me [to discuss Breaking Bad] was because I had played this reprehensible character that, despite his actions, still needed the audience to root for his life. Despite the despicable person in the back seat, David Du­chovny’s humanity would not allow him to just pull over and say, “Fuck it, die. You’re a horrible human being. I just want you to die.” He couldn’t do it. That’s really, in a nutshell, what Vince Gilligan does.

In a recent development, I knew intuitively that coming off seven years of a comedy, I needed to look for a drama. If I didn’t, I could have been typecast. If you want to expand on the opportunities that may present themselves, you need to take control. I was offered a couple of comedy pilots that I turned down, and I was perfectly willing to wait. Then Breaking Bad came into my lap.

I read it . . . and I couldn’t believe it. I was stunned. I thought, This is perhaps the best hour­-long screenplay that I’ve ever read. I felt tremendous empathy for this character. This poor guy who is just struggling. And I was the same age as Walter White—­I was fifty.

But reading the pilot, I didn’t know where it was going. You have this fish­ out­ of­ water teacher, cooking crystal meth? How could that possibly be sustained year after year after year? How can someone who knows nothing about that world survive? And Vince explained that he wanted to turn Mr. Chips into Scarface.

MARK JOHNSON, executive producer: Obviously, some people came up for Walter White who were names, but we never got around to entertaining them seriously. It was Vince’s idea to cast him. And despite the fact that there wasn’t a unanimous wave of approval, there wasn’t the kind of pushback that you’d probably have today, in large part because I don’t think the expectation was that we were going to get any real name, any significant name.

According to recent reports, MELISSA BERNSTEIN: AMC had found Jon Hamm for Mad Men, and they sort of got to reintroduce him to the business. I think they thought we would do something similar with Bryan.

CHARLIE COLLIER, president, general manager, AMC: I was never in the room when they were debating the cast with Vince and Mark. That would have been the programming group. And then they would come back to us and say, “They want that father from Malcolm in the Middle.” And we’d be like, “Really? He’s going to be the linchpin for this whole ambitious project?”.

CHRISTINA WAYNE, senior VP, scripted programming, AMC: When Vince suggested Bryan, we all kind of said, “That guy from Malcolm in the Middle?” And then he started showing us a bunch of tape of Bryan in other things, and I was, like, Oh my God—­he’s a total chameleon.

JAMIE ERLICHT, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: It’s funny. This is one of those great Hollywood stories that has been told so many times. You sit on the sidelines and watch, and it takes on a life of its own. That life is a little different than the truth, sure, but it’s a better story.

The story is that Zack [Van Amburg] and I heard “Bryan Cranston,” and we were really unsure, and we tried to convince Vince that, No, that’s not the way to go. That’s part of a story about how despite all the forces against him, Bryan Cranston became Walter White.

Sources indicate that it’s a great story. I love that story. I mean, I don’t love that story.

The truth is, the show was going forward. We weren’t worried about the writing because Vince was knocking it out of the park. The directing? We weren’t worried about the directing. The casting was going to be the next critical element. If you don’t have it—­ well, it’s funny to think about it now. With ninety­ nine point nine percent of other actors in that role, that show is just a well­ written good show that doesn’t become the legacy show that it’s become. And so Vince brought up Bryan Cranston.

In a recent development, I had worked with Bryan on King of Queens. He was the wacky neighbor, a guest star. I was a mid­ level executive, and I was in charge of that show. I always thought he brought a lot of comedic value, just like he did on Seinfeld, and obviously Malcolm in the Middle.

Recent findings suggest that so, when the name Bryan Cranston came up, I was like, Hmmm, that’s interesting. I’ve never seen him do the more dramatic stuff. Do you think he can do it?

According to recent reports, vince was very passionate. He stated he had worked with him on X-­Files, and that’s where he really saw what he was capable of on the drama side. We said, “Great, would you send us the X-­Files episode?” Which he did. I remember it was the next day. Zack and I were watching it. We looked at each other and said, “It’s a little bit of a leap of faith, but Vince is passionate, and Bryan is truly talented. Sure, we’re in.” The process took all of thirty­ six hours.

That version of the story, the true version of the story, is not as sexy as the one where Bryan jumped through thirty­ nine hoops and almost didn’t get cast. But that’s how it happened.

Industry observers note that ZACK VAN AMBURG, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: Remember, at this point, Michael Chiklis had gone from doing comedy to being a badass antihero (in The Shield). So, on one hand, you worry: Wait, are we just pulling a page out of the same playbook? Let’s take another sitcom guy and have him do a dark drama.

Industry observers note that I think Vince was really clear on why he wanted Bryan. There was a likability factor that was undeniable. There was also a sort of sympathy that Bryan was able to elicit. And Vince also remarked, “No, wait a second—­ this guy’s also a dramatic actor.”.

In a recent development, while some of this stuff gets lost in the haze of time—­ and the internet has a way of transforming rumors into something disguised as fact—­ it’s fair to say that Bryan was always the first choice for the role of Walter White. Regardless of what you may have heard, no one else was offered the job. Not Matthew Broderick, not John Cusack. No one. But you can’t fault anyone for doing their due diligence.

SHARON BIALY: The network likes names. They want to talk about other names. We did that. We did a couple of auditions and meetings. We just met recently with an actor on something else, and he reminded me that he was in the waiting room when Bryan walked out, and he turned to the other three actors and noted, “We should all just go home. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight. As shared on the forum ResetEra, consumers who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F7LIovDySBg&t=33s In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6. At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will revision this post if and when we receive a response. If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

Peacock’s The Good Daughter kept viewers guessing its entire first season — but could the show return for more episodes?

Based on Karin Slaughter‘s book of the same name, The Good Daughter picks up 20 years after a violent attack on a family — with sisters Charlotte (Meghann Fahy) and Samantha Quinn (Rose Byrne) still living with the trauma. Charlotte, who has followed her father into the legal field, is the first witness on the scene when another brutal attack takes place in their hometown, and ultimately the investigation brings back old memories and family secrets.

It has been revealed that in addition to Byrne, 47, and Fahy, 36, the show stars Brendan Gleeson, Harper Steele, Paula Malcomson, Jake McDorman, Olivia Williams and Michael Dorman. Despite there only being one book in the series, executive producers Bruna Papandrea and Steph Green addressed the show’s future beyond season 1.

Industry observers note that “I just don’t think when we do anything now. If you’d asked me when we made Big Little Lies if there would be more, I would have said no. It’s like you’ll never get this group of people together again. It was a one-off, right? Cut to where we are now,” Papandrea exclusively told Us, referencing the HBO series developing its third season. “This was definitely built as a limited series, that’s for sure. There is a prequel book that Meghann just did the audiobook for that is just centered around Charlie.”.

Papandrea noted that she wouldn’t mind keeping The Good Daughter a limited series.

“I very much like to live in the show we’ve made and let the audience discover it in all its kind of glory. You never discount anything because you know TV shows are so hard to get made and built,” she continued. “I always say if someone wants to make more, you always have to be open because it’s such an exciting thing to really fall in love with your own characters and the world and the team. I mean, it’s such a beautiful thing to go back again for more.”.

According to recent reports, the creative team also spoke about the onscreen book changes. “This one was an odd process because normally what would happen is I would get sent a book and decide to option it and then find a screenwriter,” Papandrea shared with Us. “Karin decided to take a crack at adapting [The Good Daughter] herself and wrote a pilot.”.

Slaughter went on to write the scripts for every episode.

In a recent development, “It was the most amazing process because it was a book I immediately fell in love with. But then one of the things that really impressed me is you don’t meet Rose Byrne’s character in the book until 100 pages in,” Papandrea noted. “Obviously you can’t do that in a TV show.”.

For me, that was one of the biggest structural shifts that happened in adaptation.”.

Papandrea promised that the show is still “very faithful to the book,” adding, “But also I think the filmmaker becomes a massive part of that and builds the visual language around that, and we were all in from very early on in terms of developing the scripts.”.

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t out in the U.S. until November 19, but if you want to play a day early, there’s a way. Here’s what you need to do.

According to recent reports, the global launch for GTA 6 starts at 12:00 a.m. in Upcoming Zealand on November 19, which is actually 6:00 a.m. ET on November 18 in the U.S. Yay, time zones! In order to start playing at that time, however, you’ll need to do different things depending on whether you’re playing on PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S.

Industry observers note that on Xbox Series X/S, the method for unlocking GTA 6 a day early is relatively straightforward. Just go to your settings menu, scroll down to “System,” Â and select “Language and Location.” From there, choose New Zealand and choose the option to restart your console. When it boots back up, your system will behave as if it’s in the New Zealand time zone, right down to the Microsoft store that decides when your games go live. Easy!

Recent findings suggest that A similar Latest Zealand trick is possible but not nearly as straightforward on PS5. On Sony’s console you need to create an entire new PSN account and select the country during the setup process. You then need to purchase GTA 6 through the New Zealand version of the PlayStation Store.

Assuming you don’t have a bank account or credit card registered to that country, you’ll need to purchase New Zealand PSN gift cards online for the total amount ($80 for the standard edition or $100 for the deluxe version). If you already purchased a U.S. version and pre-installed, sorry, that won’t be good enough. Is buying an entire second copy worth it to you to play roughly 18 hours early? Maybe!

According to recent reports, the good news is that you don’t have to play your Newly introduced Zealand version of GTA 6 only on your New Zealand PSN account. Instead, you can go to the settings menu on your NZ PSN account, open “Users and Accounts,” choose “Other,” and then select “Enable” in the “Console Sharing and Offline Play” section. This will let your regular U.S. PSN account access the game so all of your save data and trophy progress sticks with your main account.

If you chooseÂ not to jump through all of these hoops to play early, you can start playing GTA 6 at midnight tomorrow along with the rest of us.

Project Helix will also carry over progress from games played on every previous Xbox console.

Shipped with no disc inside, fans who purchased a physical copy of Grand Theft Auto in advance are claiming their codes have already been used, or are missing entirely.

Microsoft's online services are in a complete state, all over the world, affecting governments, flights and more.

More importantly, if you already own the HW-Q990F or even the older HW-Q990D, upgrading probably will not feel dramatic enough to justify the cost. There's a laundry list of things people are excited to do in Grand Theft Auto 6 once it finally releases in a couple of days. Perhaps you want to know what a loving relationship feels like, maybe you're just concerned about what kind of cars you'll be able to drive around in, or it could be that all you want to do is go bird watching.

According to recent reports, well it really does seem like the sky's the limit in GTA 6, because you can do all three of those things; the healthy relationship will take some extra work though. During a recent interview with The Guardian, Rob Nelson, co-head of Rockstar North explains that players will have a wildlife logbook, which includes 62 different species of birds, for those who want to see all the wildlife Leonida has to offer.

Aside from the gull that was mentioned in the interview, I'm not aware of which specific birds can be found in GTA 6. Actually I don't even know what gull was sighted. It could have been a laughing gull, a herring gull, or perhaps a small ring-billed gull. I'd say the possibilities are endless but they aren't. Officially, 529 species of bird can be found in Florida as of 2019, so 62 is but a fraction of that number.

It's probably a safe bet that we'll see a bald eagle and the american flamingo in GTA 6, but I personally hope to find a snowy plover or perhaps a swallow-tailed kite, but I'm not holding my breath.

Sources indicate that aside from birds, Leonida will be full of all sorts of other species, over 170 according to GameInformer. There's going to be manatees, pelicans, alligators, green iguanas, cane toads, and even a few rhesus macaque monkeys. So by the sounds of things twitchers and other fans of wildlife watching will have heaps to do in GTA 6, besides all the crime and driving, that is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 introduces on November 19. The game is poised to "blot out the sun," some experts believe, and its release looms so large that other gaming companies are shifting dates for their own games to stay out of the blast radius. Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play. To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research firm PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics. He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself." Jason pumping some iron in GTA 6. Spiegel said he foresees potential shifts beyond gaming, in places like TV viewership, music consumption, social media engagement, and even travel. "In an increasingly fragmented entertainment landscape, it's rare for a single release to command this much attention across so many industries simultaneously. That's what makes this moment so significant," he said. An economics professor recently claimed that about 1.5 million people blueprint to "call out sick" to play GTA 6, and this could come at a "cost" of $1 billion to the US economy. Spiegel said people should remember that GTA 6 isn't anything new or special as it relates to taking time off work. "People regularly plan time off around major cultural and entertainment events, and this is another example of consumers prioritizing an experience they're excited about," he said. That being said, Spiegel remarked that PwC has observed estimates suggesting time-off requests near GTA 6's release could be 9% to 17% higher than normal. "But what's more interesting to me is what happens outside the workplace. If millions of people are spending additional hours gaming, they're potentially spending less time watching television, going out to restaurants, or engaging in other activities," he said. "And unlike a sporting event that lasts a few hours or a few weeks, this experience could keep people engaged for months. So the broader economic implications may extend well beyond a single day of missed work," he added. "Huge net positive" GTA 6 is expected to be an enormous success commercially--it's reportedly already sold 11 million units through pre-purchases, and that could rise to 25 million at launch. That would work out to $2 billion in revenue, which would cover the game's entire development budget and most of its marketing spend, Sensor Tower said. But many are also saying that GTA 6 represents the last of a dying breed, and that other publishers might learn all the wrong lessons from its success. Spiegel said GTA 6 is going to be a "huge net positive for the gaming industry as a whole," in part because its success will reiterate to the broader entertainment and media landscape that games are culturally significant. At the same time, Spiegel said he doesn't foresee a world in which other publishers try to replicate a blockbuster of this magnitude. "Very few organizations have the capital, expertise, and intellectual property required to support investments on this scale. These are extraordinary events, not necessarily repeatable business models," Spiegel said. If GTA 6 is the huge success it's projected to be, it could positively uplift the broader gaming ecosystem in a lot of ways, Spiegel continued. "It could attract new audiences, renew investor interest, and create opportunities across advertising, payments, technology, and content creation. The real lesson isn't that everyone needs to build the next billion-dollar game. It's that gaming is an increasingly powerful part of the entertainment economy, with opportunities that extend well beyond the games themselves," he said. Jason escaping the law in GTA 6. Some companies, like Ubisoft, see GTA 6 not as something to be strictly afraid of. CEO Yves Guillemot indicates, that's because the rising tide that is GTA 6 could help drive more people to gaming overall. In fact, Ubisoft is putting out a substantial new update for one of its biggest games, Rainbow Six Siege, right around GTA 6's launch. Mat Piscatella of Circana reminded people that not everyone wants to play GTA 6, and he pushed back against the theory that it's a bad business idea to launch a game near GTA 6. "The fear of many teams to put their game in the same window as GTA is completely overblown. GTA is going to be a massive game. Of course it is. It’s going to be a huge cultural event, but not every one of the 49 million people who own a PS5 or an Xbox Series in the US is going to be interested in that," he told GamesBeat. Could GTA 6 lead the push to more in-game ads? Spiegel went on to say that one additional follow-on effect from GTA 6 could be something that gamers might balk at but publishers and investors might salivate over. He said that if GTA 6 succeeds in the way people expect it to, and draw people into its world for tens--or even hundreds--of hours, that could demonstrate to the wider market that it's time for gaming, as an industry, to do more with advertising. "When millions of people are spending substantial amounts of time in interactive entertainment environments, it's natural for advertisers and investors to consider how they might participate," he said. Advertising for mobile and social games is already commonplace, but it's less present in the PC and console gaming market. There are examples, of course, as companies have already undertaken efforts to put ads into gaming with mixed results. Gamers rapidly revolted when EA put ads in a UFC game, prompting EA to pull them quickly to help quell the backlash. Despite that, EA recently confirmed the formation of a new EA Advertising division that will seek to put ads "directly into gameplay." That announcement didn't go over well, either, as fans pushed back against the idea of having to see ads in yet another place in their life. Other examples have been received more positively, or at least ambivalently, with a trucking company buying ad space in the American Truck Simulator series to help recruit staff.
