📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC." Prominently featured in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, VP of next-gen Jason Ronald remarked the Xbox Series X|S successor is designed to build on the successes — and hard lessons — of previous Xbox generations, with fewer barriers to play. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games." Ronald added that the Project Helix family of devices isn't purely focused on traditional next-gen themes like better graphics, but on thinking ahead to create "innovative" experiences. "We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K, or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics--it's really about gameplay innovation," Ronald explained. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WB0C8z2j6nA Project Helix will also let "hardcore" gamers customize their gaming experience, but how much will all of this cost? Xbox isn't revealing a ballpark figure for Project Helix yet, but Ronald did mention the company is aiming to balance state-of-the-art gaming with an "affordable" price tag. Game preservation will also play a key role, letting users bring their Xbox library with them, and Ronald teased Project Helix as a brand that spans multiple facets of gaming, from living room experiences to handheld sessions and cloud streaming. As a sign of things to come, the Xbox mode on the recently released ROG Xbox Ally was mentioned as the direction the gaming division is headed. The news on Project Helix comes at a time when Xbox has had several highs and lows throughout 2026. This year saw several first-party games release and earn plenty of acclaim, while the anniversary celebrations included a special-edition Xbox Series X that few people could get their hands on — for retail price, that is. At the same time, the rise of Asha Sharma as Xbox CEO has seen scores of jobs and studios slashed from the Xbox family as the company undergoes a "reset" aimed at making it more profitable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In August 2024, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. suspended his presidential campaign and endorsed Donald Trump, bringing his ragtag bunch of supporters—crunchy mamas, anti-vaxxers, and conspiracy theorists; testosterone bros, peptide enthusiasts, and people who put a “COEXIST” bumper sticker on their car in the 1990s—along for the ride. But now that the blue wave or tsunami—pick your tortured water metaphor—has come to pass, the fractures within MAHA threaten to break the movement apart, driven by bitter disappointment with the Trump administration.

Sources indicate that “I think we are seeing a fracturing of the MAHA movement as those concerns start pulling people in different directions,” says Sandro Galea, dean of the Bursky School of Public Health at Washington University in St. Louis. Groups that are interested in healthier food are not necessarily the same as groups opposed to vaccines, he points out; it’s not a sure thing that those groups will continue to find common cause.

The crack-up didn’t start with the midterms, though the fact that most MAHA-backed candidates lost certainly accelerated it. Earlier this year, Trump had to withdraw his nomination of MAHA darling Casey Means for surgeon general after her stance on vaccines made it impossible for Republicans to get enough votes to support her confirmation. In May, MAHA ally Marty Makary, the commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, resigned, reportedly because of pressure from the administration to authorize fruit-flavored vapes. And in October, Calley Means—Casey’s brother—resigned from his high-level post under Secretary Kennedy at Health and Human Services, with MAHA outrage on unmet promises growing.

Three days after the midterms, Joe Rogan released a bomb-throwing, names-naming, two-plus-hour interview with Calley Means, in which the former Kennedy adviser used the word “demonic,” possibly in the literal sense, eight times.

Recent findings suggest that the major takeaway was that Susie Wiles seemed to have told Kennedy to go sit in a corner and play by himself. All roads to Trump went through her office, and according to Means, she slow-walked, watered down, or outright quashed many MAHA priorities. According to Means, she did this primarily because of her and her family’s financial ties to lobbying on behalf of big business.

Wiles did not respond to a request for comment, but a spokesperson for Wiles previously told Axios that these allegations were “outrageous, defamatory, and provably false.”.

Industry observers note that means argued that MAHA managed some wins: Trump signed an executive order to boost research on the use of psychedelics for treating mental health conditions. The fresh food pyramid instructs Americans to eat more steak than oatmeal. (In this economy?) There have been other MAHA victories too: The administration made it easier for Americans to get a handful of unproven injectable peptides, including the “Wolverine stack.” Trump signed an executive order in support of regenerative farming. The administration requested changes to the labels on testosterone products in an effort to make the hormone easier to prescribe—good news for Pete Hegseth’s promise of a “high-T Department of War.” It asked food manufacturers to voluntarily phase out some food dyes. It has sought to reduce the number of recommended childhood vaccines.

Means did not cite the United States recently losing its measles-elimination status as a win, though that was also a result of MAHA talking points.

It has been revealed that the MAGA-MAHA mind meld provided plenty for the wellness bros, but precious little of what MAHA moms were expecting from their alliance with Trump. Tiffany Cianci, a high-profile MAHA advocate who goes by @thevinomom on Instagram, says the results were “small things,” not the massive systemic changes that had been promised.

In an emailed statement, a spokesperson for HHS pushed back on this narrative, writing, in part, “HHS has delivered the most sweeping public health reforms in modern history…Across the federal government, the administration has transformed food and nutrition policy, invested more than $1 billion in regenerative agriculture and farm modernization, and taken action to address harmful chemical exposures.”.

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. delivers remarks during an event at HHS in August. The event highlighted a series of 'landmark actions' to improve the nation's food.

It has been revealed that for the MAHA moms, there are two original sins of Trump 2.0. The first is the administration’s outright support for glyphosate, an herbicide that has been classified as a probable carcinogen by a World Health Organization agency. The second is its failure to put out a definition of ultra-processed foods, which the movement sees as the first step toward curbing those foods, particularly in school lunches. One was never released; Means alleged to Rogan that ultra-processed-food initiatives such as this were stymied by White House officials including Wiles, who he remarked told him, “I need sugar money.” Reporting found that food CEOs leaned on the White House to make the definition go away.

Recent findings suggest that A White House official noted on background that the definition for ultra-processed food remains a priority and is actively being worked on by relevant agencies. White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said that “the MAHA coalition has found a champion in President Trump…The administration has already secured extensive victories for the MAHA agenda, including overhauling the dietary guidelines for Americans, axing artificial ingredients in our food supply, and investing in regenerative farming.”.

However, the Trump administration has arguably hindered research on ultra-processed foods in other ways. A leading scientist who was studying ultra-processed food’s link to diabetes and obesity took early retirement from the National Institutes of Health last year after NIH officials, he noted, censored the reporting of some of his study results because the study didn’t prove the hypothesis of ultra-processed-food addiction as they had hoped it would. If he’s to be believed, one of our best hopes for understanding the health risks of ultra-processed foods exited due to the actions of MAHA officials. (Vanity Fair has reached out to HHS for comment on the allegations of censorship; an HHS spokesperson previously told The New York Times, “NIH scientists have, and will, continue to conduct interviews regarding their research through written responses or other means. We remain committed to promoting gold-standard research and advancing public health priorities.”).

It has been revealed that “We do have a food supply that’s nearly 70% ultra-processed food,” claims Jessica Knurick, a registered dietitian and science communicator on social media. She counters that many of MAHA’s alleged priorities are aligned with the hopes of public health workers and nutritionists—yet the movement writ large has eroded trust in the very professionals who do that work. “They really want fewer environmental toxins. If you want that, you need strong regulation on corporations,” she says. “They voted in an administration that is decisively deregulatory.”.

“All of the things that the MAHA movement claimed to have wanted,” she adds, “this administration has legislated in the exact opposite direction.”.

Sources indicate that see, for instance, the glyphosate debacle. Instead of curbing the herbicide, something for which he’d long been an advocate, Kennedy got on board with Trump’s support of it, including an executive order that actually prioritized production of the chemical under the bizarre guise of national security. Then the administration supported Roundup weed killer manufacturer Monsanto, now owned by Bayer, in a case before the Supreme Court, which resulted in a decision shielding the manufacturer from state-level lawsuits brought by those who believed they’d been harmed by the glyphosate-containing product. (Glyphosate-based Roundup products are no longer produced for the US residential market.).

Sources indicate that this flew in the face of everything MAHA believed about Kennedy’s priorities. Vani Hari, a MAHA influencer who goes by the Food Babe, has been called both the Jenny McCarthy of food and a Democratic infiltrator. She thinks that the last nearly two years resulted in some positive change. She also tells me that she’s become somewhat disillusioned: “There have also been deeply disappointing decisions, particularly when it comes to glyphosate and pesticides.”.

Recent findings suggest that despite it all, the HHS secretary continues to be deified by the vast majority of MAHA leaders, who don’t blame Kennedy for these setbacks. Cianci, however, blames just about everyone involved. “What I see within MAHA right now is a fracturing into one very, very small sliver that loves the proximity to power and the fundraising. They unfortunately tied their hitch to the wrong horse, which is partisanship,” she indicates. “And you have the rest of us that actually want our kids to be healthy.”.

Supporters of the Make America Healthy Again movement are seen at a news conference on removing synthetic dyes from America's food supply, at the Health and Human Services Headquarters in Washington, DC, 2025.

If there is a road forward for MAHA, it might be best exemplified by Elizabeth Frost, a community health advocate and the leader of MAHA Ohio. She comes by her skepticism of the pharmaceutical industry honestly, after growing up in Appalachian Ohio during the height of the opioid epidemic. She now runs a political consultancy in the state, which she indicates works with both parties.

Beginning last year, Frost partnered with epidemiologists from Yale to find out how the people of East Palestine, Ohio, were still being affected by toxic exposures after the 2023 derailment of a train filled with hazardous materials. Frost went to bat for the scientists, lending her local grassroots credibility to their study on water quality in the town.

It has been revealed that “I think there is a broader anti-corporate movement in America that hasn’t really been given a home with either established party because both parties have their own pet corporate interests,” she tells me. After Kennedy’s ascent, she had hoped for a focus on the MAHA issues that enjoy broad support. “Vaccines are not the most popular issue even for MAHA. Most people in MAHA would prefer for the majority of time to be spent talking about issues that are a little bit more unifying”—rather than something like Steak ’n Shake’s now using beef tallow for its french fries. “It’s just not where people’s hearts are.”.

Speaking of no heart: Stephen Miller has been promoted to chief of staff after Wiles was forced out in the wake of the midterms. Both Calley Means and Secretary Kennedy have celebrated the move. “Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration. It’s time to unleash the Kraken,” Kennedy wrote on X.

But some MAHA moms are not so sure about the kraken. Cianci says that within MAHA, “people are very, very, very uncomfortable” with Miller. “If you’re just going to do what you’ve been told to do and take it to the extreme—he’s like the human embodiment of the paper clip problem,” she says.

Industry observers note that frost is similarly concerned about how things might go under Miller. “I don’t expect that on environmental exposures, industrial contamination, a strong streak against corporate influence—I doubt we’re going to get those things,” she claims. She is also dismayed by MAHA leadership’s embrace of convicted rapist Russell Brand. “What the hell are we doing?” she wonders.

A person familiar with MAHA thinking who spoke on background counters that while it’s fair to say that Miller might be polarizing, he is also not beholden to corporate interests the way Wiles was, making him far less likely to block the scrutiny of pesticides and healthy food policies.

According to recent reports, cianci, Frost, and Hari all hope that MAHA will survive by focusing on policy over partisanship. “I also believe MAHA’s future must be bipartisan,” Hari wrote in an email.

Cianci sees opposition to data centers as the next massive problem on which MAHA can lead. And she hopes that the anti-corporate tilt she sees in MAHA will spread. “We had a record number of candidates get elected to Congress this year that turned down all corporate PAC money. That is indicative of the MAHA movement. That is indicative of anti-corruption. And I think they’re going hand in glove.”.

In a recent development, frost would like to see Republicans work with progressives like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez on shared goals, like getting pesticides out of the food supply. She wants legislators to realize that “the way to hold their seat is to work across aisles on concerns that their constituents care about.”.

In a recent development, perhaps MAHA can reinvent itself by leveraging some of its most popular problems to make common cause with Democrats. After all, 30% of midterm voters told pollsters that they support the MAHA movement, while many more—the vast majority of Americans—say that food additives and pesticide use should be more regulated. A plurality of Americans do not want data centers in their communities. The movement’s best hope for staying relevant is probably the (currently very pissed) MAHA moms, whose concerns about food and pollution were always the most broadly resonant parts of the MAHA platform—rather than a yen for peptides, beef tallow, or testosterone.

According to recent reports, most people want to be able to afford healthy food and effective health care. Trump’s rule has not made those things more accessible, with high cost of living, massive cuts to Medicaid, the ending of certain Affordable Care Act subsidies, and reductions in federal funding for SNAP benefits.

The challenge with a rebrand is that the connection to MAGA is right there in the name. But Trump’s presidency clearly has a shelf life, and MAHA wants to outlast him. “If anyone has any ideas on how to change the name of a political movement,” Frost says, “let me know.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, kelly Clarkson never fails to entertain or make me emotional on The Voice. I enjoy seeing her bring out the heartfelt words of encouragement, maybe even more than I enjoy watching her attempt to steal country singers from Riley Green. (But only slightly.) She never shies away from tearing up, or channeling what she learned from her American Idol days, which is what she used to give advice to contestants whenever The Voice goes live.

In a recent development, something about the way the singer digs deep into the emotions really hits home. The Clarkson's advice may be a little "dark" as she reminds contestants to live in every moment, but there’s also something beautifully human about it. Clarkson is possibly influenced by the passing of her ex-husband Brandon Blackstock when she reminds her team that life is short. She shares with People ahead of The Voice’s live shows in early November what she tells contestants:.

I know this sounds dark and I don’t mean it to. I mean it to sound so beautiful and in the moment and present, but you just don’t know how long you have on this planet. We’re artists, enjoy the moment. You might mess up and that’s OK, as long as people want to watch people being incredible at what they do.

Clarkson knows exactly what they’re experiencing. Not only did she go through a similar competition on American Idol, but she often performs live at concerts, events, and even during her former show’s “Kellyoke” segments. This is part of the reason her talk show was so popular, even winning multiple daytime Emmys for outstanding series.

According to recent reports, while Clarkson has definitely upped her zany antics, including trying to give a contestant her hair, she’s also continues to bring the emotions. There’s always at least one singer who brings Clarkson (and the rest of us) to tears, and it all has to do with her appreciation for experiencing every moment. That’s exactly what she wants her team to know, even if it makes her sound like a mom:.

I didn’t want them to be so nervous. It sounds really cheesy but really being present in the moment like, ‘Hey this is a really special thing that you’re getting to do right now. Really take that in.’ I’m such a mom.

As a mom of two, this has likely impacted her outlook on competition, especially when it comes to younger contestants like 13-year-old Brianna Cameron. Though who didn't share a tear during "Inseparable"? However, it’s not all emotional on The Voice as Clarkson reminds us yet again why she may just be the funniest Coach.... even if this season gave her some humorous competition. Whether it’s engaging in some smack talk with her fellow coaches or upping the goofy hijinks, it’s obvious she’s having a good time.

Season 30 has been a blast, and it’s largely due to the four coaches, which includes Adam Levine and newbie coaches Queen Latifah and Riley Green. However, while I’ve enjoyed the zany zingers and even the duck blind prank, it’s the emotional moments and performances that seem to land a little harder.

In a recent development, you can watch new episodes of The Voice every Monday on NBC and the next day with a Peacock subscription. The season is quickly winding down with the finale just around the corner on December 14.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Miley Cyrus is reflecting on her lifelong bond with her late godmother and mentor, Dolly Parton, following their joint 2027 Grammy Award nomination.

“My Aunt Dolly is one of the greatest songwriters the world has ever known,” Cyrus, 33, said via a Monday, November 16 tweet. “She never made music for recognition but to make the world a happier place through her songs.”.

Industry observers note that cyrus and Parton received a Best Country Duo/Group Performance Grammy nomination on Monday for their remake of “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” alongside Lainey Wilson, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire. Parton was also nominated a second time in that same category for her and the Zac Brown Band’s duet, “Butterfly.”.

The 2026 reinterpretation of Parton’s inspirational 1977 single “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” was released to raise money for pediatric cancer research at Nashville’s Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt.

Reflecting on her latest Grammy nomination, Cyrus shared that it was particularly meaningful since Parton gifted her a vinyl copy of her 1977 album New Harvest…First Gathering — featuring the original version of “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” — “a couple Christmases ago.”.

Recent findings suggest that “To be nominated alongside her, Lainey Wilson, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire for Light of a Clear Blue Morning is a beautiful way to honor her enormous heart,” Cyrus tweeted on Monday. “This cover supported pediatric cancer research at Vanderbilt’s Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital, a cause close to her heart.”.

She added, “I miss her calling on big days like this but feel her in every moment. Love you Aunt Dolly. Congratulations to these beautiful women and all the other nominees.”.

Cyrus publicly mourned her mentor when Parton’s rep confirmed the legendary country music singer-songwriter’s death at age 80 following “a brief battle with cancer” in August.

“The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share. Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” Cyrus wrote via Instagram on August 25. “What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. 🦋.”.

Industry observers note that the “Wrecking Ball” singer continued, “I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things.”.

Cyrus broke down on stage during an October show at the Hollywood Bowl, revealing she’d only ever seen Parton perform “live in concert one time in my entire life” — and it was at the very same historic Los Angeles area venue.

“Now, I spent a lot of time backstage and … if she was playing the show, I’d be standing right beside her in a matching costume,” she beamed.

The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will air on ABC and Disney+ Sunday, February 7, 2027, from Los Angeles’ Crypto.com Arena.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, november is a huge month for video games. Nintendo dropped its remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2 last week, and the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI is right around the corner. But the game we've been waiting for most of all also rolled out this month: WendyQuest, the free RPG from Wendy's. (No, this is not a joke.).

Despite the absurdity of a hamburger chain making a full video game (complete with Wendy's-themed puns), the thing is, this game is pretty solid—even if it is a promotion at the end of the day. WendyQuest's main purpose is to offer customers coupons they can use toward purchases in real life, though it's a bit of a commitment. It took me just under an hour of gameplay before I earned my first coupon, and Wendy's says it takes roughly 15 hours to beat. All that to say, this is a pretty unique marketing campaign.

I was surprised booting up WendyQuest on my iPhone. This doesn't necessarily feel like a thrown-together product. On the flip side, the production quality is quite high. The music is solid and very much traditionally RPG; there are even three save slots, in case you plan to return to this RPG again and again.

Recent findings suggest that there's even a story, albeit cheesy (no pun intended): As the game explains, the "Four Great Spirits of Flavor" created Savoria, "a food-rich paradise." All was well until Mech Corp, led by the evil Dr. MechBorg, built robots to take over Savoria. The plot is far from compelling, and the writing can be a little over the top, but hey, I'll give them credit: They thought through a full story here.

Recent findings suggest that you play as Wendy, the "representation of true culinary excellence and taste as dictated by the four ancient spirits of flavor." Wendy (or The Wendy, as some call her) is tasked with saving the world, traveling between villages and picking up new characters along the way. The game world even has "real" Wendy's locations you can visit. These act like inns and shops in other RPGs, giving you a chance to heal while also buying equipment.

According to recent reports, like other RPGs, WendyQuest uses turn-based combat. You have to charge up your attacks, but stop before they hit 100%, or you'll miss. (It took me a while to master the timing.) I'm pretty impressed with how challenging some of these battles can be, though you are quickly given the option of an amulet that gives you a huge leg-up in combat. You don't have to take it, but it makes fights easier if you're only in it for the coupons. That, combined with the spatulas the game encourages you to buy, lets you mow down enemies. You can also utilize your companions here: "Frygor," for example, can either attack enemies with a barrage of fries, or use those fries to build a shield to protect you.

In a recent development, while there are tons of enemies to fight, the key baddies are the "mechs." There are five in total, and after you defeat each, you get a coupon. Spoiler alert: The first mech drops the "Fry Stone," which nets you a coupon for a free order of medium fries—though you need to buy something in tandem, as well as use the Wendy's app. While I stopped my gaming here for this article, the other four coupons are:.

Free biscuit or croissant (I didn't even know Wendy's sold biscuits and croissants).

Again, it's wild that WendyQuest has a 10+ hour campaign, with over 1,000 lines of dialogue to boot. I'm not sure this is a game I'm going to see through to the end, but I'll admit, it's a fun marketing approach from Wendy's. Sure, they could have run a promotion in the Wendy's app to give people coupons, but instead, they built an entire RPG. I respect it. You can download the game for iOS, Android, or Steam.

Xbox Is Looking For Smarter Ways To Stop Its Next Console From Costing A Fortune

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • No one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap.
  • According to recent reports, no one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap.
  • Industry observers note that according to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap. The ongoing memory shortage has driven current-gen console prices skyward since 2024, with the Xbox Series X rising from $500 in 2020 to $800 in 2026. Project Helix is projected to cost as much as $1,800 at launch, but Microsoft aims to keep the price down when it eventually releases the device. According to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely fresh technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable," Ronald said in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." In a nutshell, neural rendering uses AI to predict and generate high-quality video game frames while using only a portion of hardware power, similar to upscaling technoligies like PSSR, DLSS, and FSR. This could enable next-generation visual leaps while keeping the console accessible and reasonably priced for consumers. The other benefit is that the AI software models can improve over time through updates, as console hardware remains fixed over its lifespan, hence Ronald's quote about improvements reaching Project Helix over a few years into its run. It remains to be seen how these breakthroughs will be spread across Project Helix, which Ronald teased as a family of devices that can address home, mobile, and cloud gaming needs. Xbox suggesting that it's working smarter to deliver an affordable gaming experience is an idea that Shawn Layden touched on recently, as the former PlayStation boss spoke about how Sony should be less concerned with chasing improved graphics and rather focus on making a cheaper PS5-level console instead. Meanwhile, Sony is squeezing more life out of the PS5 generation with AI-guided upscaling technology, and the base model PS5 got its own version of this in the form of Quick Spectral Super Resolution. Originally available for only two games, QSSR is coming to more titles in the future, like Control Resonant, Arc Raiders, and No Man's Sky.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beyoncé and Taylor Swift are just a few of the big names who have broken Grammy records over the course of the awards show’s history.

In 2023, Beyoncé became the most-awarded artist in Grammys history with the 32nd trophy of her career, taking home the trophy for Best Dance/Electronic Album for Renaissance. It was her fourth win of the 2023 ceremony.

Two years later, Beyoncé added even more Grammy wins to her resume thanks to Cowboy Carter, becoming the first Black woman to win Best Country Album. She also won Album of the Year and Best Country/Duo Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” with Miley Cyrus.

Another Grammys favorite, Billie Eilish, swept the 2020 awards show with wins in the biggest categories of the night, including Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Record of the Year and Best New Artist, when she was just 18 years old.

Sources indicate that the popular fried chicken chain KFC has declared a frankly absurd GTA 6 promotion: a fake funeral so people have a “legitimate” excuse to take the day off to play Rockstar’s latest. The fake funeral for a woman, "Ann Alibi," will take place Thursday, November 19 at 11 AM at KFC Robina in Queensland. People can attend in person or watch the funeral by livestream. The local restaurant is part of a region of Australia known as the Gold Coast, which KFC says is the equivalent of GTA 6's Vice City (which itself is a stand-in for Miami). RIP "The service will include a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest. All the appropriate arrangements for a fitting farewell," KFC said. The restaurant is also handing out free fried chicken to anyone who highlights up in person. For those who can't make the services, KFC will offer free delivery through its app across Australia on November 19. Anyone planning to eat fried food and play video games should be mindful of what might happen to their controller ... unless you got your hands on the limited-edition "greaseproof" controller that Microsoft put out years ago. People in Australia will be among the first in the world to play it since the game unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play GTA 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that after well over a year of rampant speculation, Amazon MGM Studios and director Denis Villeneuve have found their James Bond, and it's Robert Pattinson. As many have noted, Pattinson's casting as Bond marks the first time an established movie star has been brought on to play 007 (Roger Moore and Pierce Brosnan were TV stars prior to earning their license to kill), and some folks are lamenting that the fun of a Bond transition is getting to watch an actor grow into the role. Pattinson, however, offers moviegoers a different opportunity: Just how will this actor, who's renowned for playing weirdos and affecting strange accents, approach a character who hasn't exhibited much of a sense of humor since Roger Moore surrendered his Walther PPK in 1985?

Pattinson's run as Edward Cullen in the "Twilight" movies led many to underestimate him as an actor. He played the vampire Edward Cullen as a brooding emo teenager (though he's actually 104 years old), and, at least until Bill Condon came on to direct the final two installments, the films generally didn't ask much of him. He also might've hurt himself with his portrayal of a young Salvador Dali in 2008's "Little Ashes," where his interesting physical and vocal choices are undone by a perfectly awful Spanish accent.

According to recent reports, but once he got clear of "Twilight," Pattinson began flaunting his versatility in films like David Cronenberg's "Cosmopolis," David Michôd's "The Rover" (where he's deeply moving as a twitchy southerner who can't take care of himself), and Josh and Bennie Safdie's "Good Time" (which lets him cut loose as a low-level New York City criminal). No actor has stepped into the role of Bond with as varied a resume as this. And it only gets more varied the further along you read.

One of Robert Pattinson's zaniest performances can be found in David and Nathan Zellner's "Damsel," a dark Western comedy where he plays an eccentric pioneer who speaks in a high-pitched twang. He's an overbearing type who's not nearly as smart or entertaining as he thinks he is. Contrast this with his sublime turn as a tormented sea dog in Robert Eggers' "The Lighthouse." There, Pattinson makes for a weathered, sour delight as a lighthouse keeper who detests his tyrannical superior (Willem Dafoe) — the same chap who happens to be his only companion in this Maine lighthouse (circa 1890).

If you're looking for hints as to how Pattinson might play James Bond, he's conventionally charming and suave as agent Neil in Christopher Nolan's "Tenet," yet he plays Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves' "The Batman" as more of an aloof and dour oddball than most other actors have. If Denis Villeneuve wants a dark and brooding 007, then Pattinson's Caped Crusader might be a helpful point of reference.

For those hoping that Villeneuve might lighten up the James Bond franchise, look at his filmography. It's highly unlikely he'll let Pattinson yuk it up à la Roger Moore. But nowadays, it seems like Pattinson can't help but make interesting choices. (Just look at his 2026 trifecta of "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime.") He's one of our most interesting stars, and it would be a shame if Villeneuve played it safe and had him do Daniel Craig redux. The pair kissed while looking at the Big Apple skyline, hinting that Scola will be making his way to California once his paperwork gets approved.

Industry observers note that “As an actor, it would be fun to get to play it all the way to the end of like, you know, ‘See you guys later.’ But I don’t know what they’re gonna do with that,” Boyd told Us. “We just explored a whole you know [Special Agent] OA leaving [briefly]. According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect. Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting. "Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson noted. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation. "We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate." Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. At the moment, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.

I Didn’t Think Hallmark Could Find Another Way To Reinvent The Time Loophole Wheel, But They Crushed It

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some spoilers for The Nights Before Christmas can be found in this piece.
  • Hallmark is no stranger to holiday time-loop movies — the 2023 time-loop film Round and Round was my absolute favorite that year — so they definitely know how to write an effective one.
  • Such core elements are so ingrained in the genre that it can be hard to reinvent the time-loop wheel, but by some miracle, Hallmark managed to do just that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some spoilers for The Nights Before Christmas can be found in this piece.

Hallmark is no stranger to holiday time-loop movies — the 2023 time-loop film Round and Round was my absolute favorite that year — so they definitely know how to write an effective one. Just like Hallmark Christmas movies follow a perfect movie formula, time-loop flicks also have a tried-and-true formula. A character who is unhappy in life encounters some kind of magical being or object that sets up the time loop, which they’ll ultimately spend the rest of the film trying desperately to break the curse.

Such core elements are so ingrained in the genre that it can be hard to reinvent the time-loop wheel, but by some miracle, Hallmark managed to do just that. And it totally worked!

The Nights Before Christmas premiered on the 2026 TV schedule this weekend and instantly became one of my favorite Hallmark Christmas movies of 2026. A fun yuletide flick, it follows Marty (Tyler Hynes), who is stuck reliving Christmas Eve over and over again after making a holiday wish to have more time to pursue his interests and hobbies. Marty takes full advantage of the gift of time, using it to meet people and master all his hobbies, and he seems content to keep living the same day on repeat.

Recent findings suggest that well, that is, until he meets Chloe (Laci J. Mailey), whom he feels an instant connection with. As Marty continues to repeat Christmas Eve with Chloe, he starts to wonder what his life would be like if he made it to Christmas morning.

In a recent development, unlike other time-loop films, The Nights Before Christmas doesn’t start on day one of Marty’s loop. Instead, we meet Marty in one of the hundreds, if not thousands, of Christmas Eves he’s managed to live through. This is in immediate deviation from the genre that has made finding out you're in a time loop and freaking out about it one of the main features of a character’s arc. He’s also not freaked out or bothered by the sudden change in how time progresses; if anything, he welcomes and loves it.

Industry observers note that the realization that this wasn’t going to be a day-one time loop was one that shocked me as soon as it happened, but I was totally on board with it. Admittedly, I’m not the biggest fan of the genre, so getting to watch Marty exist in the loop and be happy with his upcoming, repetitive life was a much-needed and refreshing change to the otherwise predictable genre.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

My Favorite Hallmark Christmas Movie Is Getting A Sequel, And I Can’t Wait.

Recent findings suggest that the film continues to reinvent the wheel as it progresses. For starters, almost every time Marty explains to Chloe that he’s stuck in a time loop, she believes him. This is unheard of with these types of films, as most of the time the stuck character has to jump through extravagant hoops to get anyone to believe and help them. Perhaps it helps that Marty isn’t asking for Chloe’s help in getting unstuck or advice on how to survive noted time loop; he simply wants to spend time with her.

According to recent reports, TNBC also finds fun ways to show the same day over and over again without long, drawn-out scenes. There’s a particularly fun sequence towards the end of the film where Marty is shown to be an excellent driver in a terrible snowstorm, despite having previously claimed to hate driving. It’s then revealed that this isn’t the first time he’s driven in the terrible storm and that the previous attempts have ended in disaster.

In a recent development, in its final act, the holiday film also manages to reinvent the way the time loop is resolved. All too often in these types of movies, the main characters must come to some great epiphany in order to put a stop to the loop and revert to the real timeline. This usually involves searching inward and changing something about themselves, but that’s not what happens in Nights Before Christmas. Instead, Marty discovers that he wasn’t put in the time loop to help himself, but rather he was put there to help Chloe get the Christmas she’s come to love and expect: a day with her parents. Needless to say, a narrative like this is quite refreshing in this genre.

So, if you’re a fan of time loops and Christmas, then The Nights Before Christmas needs to go to the top of your holiday watch list. The film can be streamed now with an active Hallmark+ subscription, or viewers can catch it airing on Hallmark again on Friday, November 20th at 10 PM, after the latest Countdown to Christmas lineup premiere.

#16543. The Downfall Of Sony's Spider-Man Universe Can Be Traced Back To One Moment

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (863 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Slashfilm ↗ Open Full Page

The Downfall Of Sony's Spider-Man Universe Can Be Traced Back To One Moment

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if Marvel Comics has proved anything over the past 63 years, it's that the number of stories you can tell about Spider-Man is essentially infinite.
  • With Sony scrapping looks for expanding into more villain-focused films, moviegoers are left with burning questions.
  • Recent findings suggest that under normal circumstances, a superhero movie being good would be the furthest thing from a problem, even if it might seem like an unlikely success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if Marvel Comics has proved anything over the past 63 years, it's that the number of stories you can tell about Spider-Man is essentially infinite. Not only is he a great character in his own right, he also has an incredible roster of villains and one of the best supporting casts in the history of superhero comics. And yet, despite the success of movies about the web-slinging wall-crawler himself, Sony Pictures' attempts to expand into a full-on Spider-Man Universe have been, to put it bluntly, an abysmal failure on virtually every level.

With Sony scrapping looks for expanding into more villain-focused films, moviegoers are left with burning questions. How could a cinematic franchise built around characters like Madame Web and Morbius possibly have failed? Who could have predicted that audiences might not care about the origin of Kraven the Hunter's cool jacket as much as they care about him, say, fighting Spider-Man? Was the world ever going to be ready for Morbin' Time? It's nearly impossible to say for sure, but upon examining the timeline of Sony's many attempts to get their Spidey-themed side universe going, one thing becomes apparent: It all went wrong with 2018's "Venom" — not because it was bad, but because it was good.

Recent findings suggest that under normal circumstances, a superhero movie being good would be the furthest thing from a problem, even if it might seem like an unlikely success. 1998's "Blade," after all, took its title vampire hunter from a C-list character to a surprise hit, becoming Marvel's first brush with cinematic success years before the X-Men and Spider-Man hit the massive screen. That proved that with a strong enough vision, a character could be taken out of the context of a traditional story and work just as well — or in Blade's case, even better.

Recent findings suggest that it's hard not to look at "Venom" as a sort of cinematic descendant of "Blade." Both movies took a darker approach to superhero storytelling and mixed in a heaping helping of genre conventions to keep things feeling fresh — vampire horror for "Blade," and classic alien invasion sci-fi for "Venom." There are, however, some pretty significant differences. For one, unlike the pre-movie version of Blade, Venom had a much stronger track record of being a fan-favorite character who could stand on his own, even with his unbreakable ties to Spider-Man. For another, while "Blade" was definitely a hit, the success of "Venom" absolutely blows it out of the vampire-infested water. Thanks largely to Tom Hardy's incredibly charismatic performance as both Eddie Brock and his alien symbiote BFF, "Venom" racked up a staggering $856 million at the box office.

"Venom" brought in a ton of money, garnered acclaim from critics and fans, and seemed to be proof of concept that characters related to Spider-Man can carry a film without him. For a organization looking to build its own superhero franchise juggernaut (or at least a franchise Rhino) with a suite of characters whose rights its been hanging onto for over 20 years, that's good news, right? Well ... not if you're determined to learn the wrong lesson.

In a recent development, while we'll never really know what was going through the minds of the studio executives who thought releasing "Morbius" twice was a good idea, it's easy to imagine how a thought process that's more concerned with the bottom line than with storytelling and character might interpret the massive success of "Venom." If that movie can succeed by featuring a Spider-Man villain on his own without Spider-Man involved at all, then why can't all these other characters that came along when Sony got the Spidey rights? These characters are pretty much all the same, right? One's as good as any other.

Unfortunately for Sony, that's not exactly how it works. Villains, particularly Spider-Man's roster of sinister foes, are built to work in the context of their heroic counterparts, and the same usually goes for the supporting cast that orbits around them. It's the contrast and context that makes them interesting. Venom works in a starring role because he's been the protagonist of his own stories for far longer than he was a pure villain. Kraven the Hunter, on the other hand, doesn't have that development. Weirdly enough, the character who probably had the best shot at standing on their own was Morbius, who is only tangentially related to Spider-Man and has a history of starring in his own stories, albeit with very little success. Alas, it turns out that sometimes, you actually have to make a good movie, and "Morbius" is anything but that.

Of course, trying to make a Spider-Man universe without Spider-Man was only one of several baffling choices Sony made with its attempted franchise. If any executive had bothered to ask literally anyone who reads comics or knows about superheroes if they should make a movie about Morbius or Madame Web, they would've found out just from the facial expression they were met with that this was a terrible idea. Her web may connect us all, but it certainly wasn't going to connect with audiences.

Robert Pattinson Is the Latest James Bond

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin.
  • It has been revealed that “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” mentioned Pattinson in a statement.
  • In a recent development, created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin. After a highly scrutinized and lengthy audition process involving some of Hollywood’s most sought-after leading men, it was the Batman star who emerged at the eleventh hour to nab the role of MI6 agent James Bond.

It has been revealed that “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” mentioned Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

In a recent development, created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world. Figuring prominently in 12 of Fleming’s novels and two collections of short stories, Bond is both tall, dark, and handsome and calm, cool, and collected—the platonic ideal of a world-class spy. Bond leapt from page to screen in 1962 with the Eon-produced Dr. No, spawning one of the biggest media franchises in history. Since its inception, the 27 Bond films have grossed more than $7 billion dollars worldwide.

In a recent development, pattinson follows in the suave footsteps of Daniel Craig, who played James Bond for five films, from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die where (spoiler alert) Craig’s 007 dies while protecting the world from a global terrorist organization. Around No Time to Die, there was another shake up in Bond ownership when Amazon acquired Bond’s parent studio, MGM, in an $8.5 billion deal. Barbara Broccoli—whose father, Eon founder Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli, produced the first Bond film—and her half brother, Michael G. Wilson, held the rights to the franchise for almost 30 years, and pledged to work with Amazon. However, in February 2025, Broccoli and Wilson announced that they’d be stepping back from the franchise and ceding complete creative control to Amazon MGM. At the Oscars a month later, the Broccoli family was honored with a bizarre musical tribute to James Bond, starring Margaret Qualley, Doja Cat, and Lisa, unofficially ushering in a fresh era in the Bond Cinematic Universe.

Industry observers note that although a fresh era of Bond loomed, Amazon MGM had one major problem: They needed a new Bond. Ahead of No Time to Die, Craig had confirmed that he was stepping away from the franchise, leaving the producers with a 007-sized hole to fill. Before she stepped away, Broccoli insinuated that this new era of Bond was looking for a younger actor, in their 30s, to take over the reins from Craig, who was 51 when he retired from MI6.

Recent findings suggest that technically, they landed on someone slightly outside their preferred age range; Pattinson is 40 years old. Just don’t tell him that. During Vanity Fair’s lie detector test with Jennifer Lawrence while promoting their film Die My Love, Pattinson insisted he was from a different generation. I am Gen Z,” he noted to Lawrence. “I am.” Hey, you’re only as old as you feel. In the same video, Pattinson said he “likes taking jobs of younger actors,” which he managed to do with his Bond casting. Good for Pattinson.

In a recent development, almost every leading man in Hollywood’s name came up as a potential predecessor to Craig—except for Pattinson, who the masses assumed was out of contention due to the fact that he locked into playing another beloved fictional character with massive IP: Batman. Pattinson’s take on the caped crusader in Matt Reeve’s The Batman (2022) was a major success, but several production delays on The Batman Part II, and a shakeup at Batman’s studio, DC—last week, it was confirmed that the co-CEOs of DC Productions, James Gunn and Peter Safran, were ousted from the studio—meant that there might be time in Pattinson’s schedule for some sexy espionage.

According to recent reports, still, it was far from a done deal that Pattinson would land 007. In recent years, some fans have advocated for a twist on the classic Bond formula. Lashana Lynch made history as Nomi, the first Black person to ever to hold the 007 moniker, in No Time to Die. But Nomi is not James Bond. There was a seemingly endless period when the world was convinced that Idris Elba—arguably the most tall, dark, and handsome man to ever exist—would take on the mantle at some point, but it wasn’t meant to be. Now, at 53, Elba has seemingly aged out of the role. (For the record, Elba thought the next Bond should be a woman.) Elba wasn’t the only name bandied about in recent years. It was reported in 2024 that Aaron Taylor-Johnson was close to signing a contract to take over the role, but those reports were never confirmed.

According to recent reports, although a favorite at the beginning, Jacob Elordi reportedly didn’t screen test for the role. Riz Ahmed made an Emmy-nominated television show, Bait, inspired by the idea of a British Pakistani actor getting cast as Bond. Other actors rumored to be in the mix over the course of the process include, but are not limited to, Tom Francis, Harris Dickinson, and, apparently, Harry Styles. At the end of the day, five actors reportedly screen-tested for the role: Slow Horse’s Jack Lowden, One Night Only’s Callum Turner, Disclosure Day’s Josh O’Connor, Superman’s Nicholas Hoult, and Pattison. Hoult and Pattinson were the last names to emerge as contenders for the role, implying that the powers that be at Amazon MGM may not have been happy with the three options presented and sent a hail mary. When Puck reported that Pattinson was able to negotiate a three-picture deal rather than a four-picture deal despite commanding a much higher salary than the other options, it looked like the writing was on the wall that Pattinson would be the next Bond.

It also helps that Pattinson is having a career high at the moment, having starred in a handful of the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films of 2026. He began the year by turning his controversial A24 comedy The Drama with Zendaya into a box-office success, generating $134 million worldwide on a reported budget of about $28 million. He then followed that up with a deliciously sniveling turn in Christopher Nolan’s epic The Odyssey, an Oscar front-runner that earned $1.8 billion at the box office. Then there’s Primetime, the Lance Oppenheim drama starring Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. (Yes, in a way, Chris Hansen is now one degree from being James Bond. Let that sink in). Primetime hit massive with $62 million globally on an $14.5 million budget, and is earning Pattinson leading-actor buzz. On top of it all, he’s still got Dune: Part Three with Denis Villeneuve coming down the pipeline in December.

Sources indicate that ultimately, the Twilight star was handpicked by the powers that be at Amazon MGM, including producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next iteration of the series based on a script from screenwriter Steven Knight, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Given the fact that Pattinson is starring in Villeneuve’s highly-anticipated Dune: Part Three, it might not be that much of a surprise that the director chose Pattinson as his next Bond. “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” said Villeneuve in a statement. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our fresh James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”.

Pattinson enters a long lineage of spectacularly suave spies—some who lasted longer than others in Bond’s impeccably tailored suits. The first-ever James Bond was, of course, Sean Connery, who went on to star in six Bond films, including From Russia With Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Connery was followed by George Lazenby, who starred in a single Bond film, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service (1969), before passing the reins back to Connery. The third Bond was Roger Moore, who took over for 1973’s Live and Let Die, and appeared in a total of seven Bond films, most notably The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Octopussy (1983).

According to recent reports, after Moore came Timothy Dalton, who became 007 with 1987’s The Living Daylights, then threw in the towel after 1989’s License to Kill. Millennials will fondly remember the next Bond: Pierce Brosnan, who starred as the sexy spy in four films from 1995’s GoldenEye to 2002’s Die Another Day, until Craig took over in 2006.

Will Pattison’s Bond be more debonair like Brosnan, who told VF he was “eagerly” awaiting the Bond casting news, or brooding like Craig? Will he be remembered as a rightful heir to Connery’s throne, or will his Bond feel closer to Austin Powers in The Spy Who Shagged Me? In any case, let’s hope Pattinson prefers his martinis shaken not stirred. He’s going to be drinking a lot of them for the foreseeable future.

Us has reached out to Gardner’s rep for comment. TMZ was first to report the news.

Sources indicate that tintori was an accomplished music video director, having worked with major music acts such as Solange Knowles, The Killers, Arcade Fire and MGMT. He was credited as a special effects unit director on the 2012 fantasy movie Beasts of the Southern Wild, which received four Academy Award nominations and won the Grand Jury Prize at that year’s Sundance Film Festival.

Ray’s father, John Tintori, was a film editor who worked on Eight Men Out and Mr. Wonderful while his mother, Mary Cybulski, was as a script supervisor and photographer on Life of Pi, Syriana and The Ice Storm, among other projects. (Cybulski died from glioblastoma at age 70 in November 2025.).

It is not clear how long Gardner, 43, and Ray were together, though he posted a loving tribute to the comedian in honor of her 42nd birthday in July 2025.

It has been revealed that “Prettier and more graceful than the moon and by far the coolest person I’ve ever met,” he wrote via Instagram alongside a carousel of sweet photos. “My favorite song in the world is you singing softly in my ear. My favorite color is the gold at the center of your eyes.”.

Ray recalled “falling so fast” for Gardner the “second [their] eyes met” while she was “laughing with [her] whole body.”.

Sources indicate that “I’ve just been falling faster every day. You are the sexiest woman who ever lived, in every single manner of clothing, hair, and old age makeup,” he added. “I’m crushing on you so deep, endlessly. You hold my heart perfectly and love me so proper. You carry the party in your eyes and move like a modern dancer everywhere you go.”.

It has been revealed that the director concluded, “You are the most genius at making art and surfing the wave with the purest flow I’ve ever seen. The world is a love letter to you. I am your boy forever.”.

Prior to her relationship with Ray, Gardner was married to Marvel Comics writer Zeb Wells from 2010 to 2023.

GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play.

#16538. Update Your iPhone to Prevent People From Seeing iMessages They Shouldn't

📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Update Your iPhone to Prevent People From Seeing iMessages They Shouldn't

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (773 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You add someone upcoming to an iMessage group chat, and wonder, "Huh, can they see any of the messages from before they were added?" The answer to that question is supposed to be "no." By design, new iMessage group chat members are only privy to texts that arrive after they were added.
  • As it turns out, there's a bug with iMessage that may allow new group chat members to see texts from before they were added to the chat.
  • In a recent development, that's not all: There exists another security flaw that could allow remote hackers to join an iMessage group and receive new messages.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Has this ever happened to you? You add someone upcoming to an iMessage group chat, and wonder, "Huh, can they see any of the messages from before they were added?" The answer to that question is supposed to be "no." By design, new iMessage group chat members are only privy to texts that arrive after they were added. When they join, it's essentially a blank slate, as if you just created the group for the first time. At least, that's how it's intended to work.

As it turns out, there's a bug with iMessage that may allow new group chat members to see texts from before they were added to the chat. That's a problem, and not just for the iPhone consumers out there talking smack about people before inviting them to join the group chat. It means iMessage, and Apple's platforms in general, aren't working like they're supposed to be. You don't have to be talking behind people's backs to not want new members seeing existing chats. Maybe you're planning a surprise party for someone, and add them to the group once everyone's in on the plan; maybe the texts in the chat aren't relevant to the current group, and the person joining simply does not need to access them.

In a recent development, that's not all: There exists another security flaw that could allow remote hackers to join an iMessage group and receive new messages. You might add a new user to a group chat and inadvertently invite them to read all existing messages, while at the same time being attacked by a bad actor who can then intercept all future messages. Not good.

Luckily, there's right now a fix for these problems. Apple patched (and revealed) the bugs, along with seven other security flaws, with a series of software updates on Monday for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. Not all of the updates include patches for these two iMessage flaws—specifically, some of the updates for older Apple devices. But the rest, including iOS 27.2.1, macOS 27.2.1, macOS 26.7.3, macOS 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1, and visionOS 27.2.1, include the iMessage patches.

Each update includes its own list of patches, but, for this article, I'll take a look at the nine patches in iOS 27.2.1. You'll find the two iMessage bugs, plus seven other patches, in the list below:.

Recent findings suggest that airPlay: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts. Description: A logic matter was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113968: Apple.

App Intents: Impact: An app may be able to access sensitive user data. Description: An authorization problem was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113963: László Várady.

Sources indicate that bluetooth: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory. Description: A use-after-free problem was addressed with improved memory management. CVE-2026-113970: Apple.

brotli: Impact: Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption. Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation. CVE-2026-111497.

CoreUtils: Impact: A malicious Bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction. Description: This glitch was addressed with improved checks. CVE-2026-113965: Apple.

Recent findings suggest that coreUtils: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction. Description: A logic problem was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113964: an anonymous researcher.

Industry observers note that messages: Impact: A remote attacker may be able to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages. Description: An authorization problem was addressed with improved validation. CVE-2026-113961: an anonymous researcher.

Industry observers note that messages: Impact: A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined. Description: This glitch was addressed by removing the vulnerable code. CVE-2026-113960: an anonymous researcher.

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
  • The Criterion release of Guillermo del Toro's "Frankenstein" includes a upcoming "Reborn Cut" that reinserts eight minutes of footage.
  • Recent findings suggest that now, how much can eight minutes really change a movie, especially one that's already 150 minutes long?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

The Criterion release of Guillermo del Toro's "Frankenstein" includes a upcoming "Reborn Cut" that reinserts eight minutes of footage.

Recent findings suggest that now, how much can eight minutes really change a movie, especially one that's already 150 minutes long? Quite a lot, it turns out. "Frankenstein: The Reborn Cut" completely recontextualizes Victor Frankenstein (Oscar Isaac) by featuring a young Victor (Christian Convery) secretly murdering his abusive father, Baron Leopold Frankenstein (Charles Dance).

In both versions, Victor comes to suspect Leopold let his mother Claire (Mia Goth) die in childbirth. This suspicion doesn't come to much in the theatrical cut; Victor confronts his father about it, who answers no one can conquer death, and Victor counters that he will. That night, Victor dreams of a "Dark Angel" promising him that craved knowledge. Victor's story of his childhood still ends with his father's death, but by seemingly natural causes.

Industry observers note that the "Reborn Cut" includes additional dialogue; Victor says, to secure the Dark Angel's deal and protect his little brother William from "the Beast," he decided to kill his father. Victor mixes a poison recipe from Leopold's own medical library and drops it in his father's ear as he sleeps, like Claudius killing Hamlet's father.

Victor Frankenstein of the theatrical cut already highlighted an Oedipus complex, or a boy who sexually desires his mother and wants to kill his father. Goth plays Victor's mother and his coveted Elizabeth Harlander, and Victor's drink of choice is milk. Victor literally killing his father in the "Reborn Cut" completes the character's psychology. It also deepens his character in the rest of the movie as he becomes a father himself to the Creature (Jacob Elordi), whose violent revenge against Victor for abusing him now even more closely mirrors Victor and Leopold.

Recent findings suggest that nothing of this sort happens in Mary Shelley's "Frankenstein" book. Victor's childhood was already one of the biggest changes from the "Frankenstein" novel, where he says that "no youth could have passed more happily than mine." Victor's father dies at the end of the novel in grief from the Creature killing all of his and Victor's loved ones.

In del Toro's movie, Victor adores his mother, but his father is cold, concerned only that Victor carries on his legacy as a master surgeon — he strikes Victor with a cane when he fails in his studies. Del Toro refashions Frankenstein Sr. like his villain Captain Vidal (Sergi López) in "Pan's Labyrinth." Both men only see their wives as brood mares and dislike the child she already has. Both men's wives die in childbirth, and with the suggestion Vidal/Leopold allowed that because he only cared about the child's life.

It has been revealed that leopold's abuse infects how Victor treats his creation. Victor tries to rear the Creature, but it goes horribly wrong because he's echoing his father's parenting. In his arrogance, Victor also doesn't conceive of his creation as a child. Take his anger when the Creature cuts his hand grabbing a razor blade — is that parental concern or anger that the monster damaged his [Victor's] artistic work of surgically sculpting the Creature's body?

In another scene, the Creature recoils when Victor gets angry at him for not speaking, and Victor reacts in exasperated disbelief: "I'm not going to hurt you. I made you." It seems like he genuinely wants to be different from his father but doesn't know how to be, which is even more gutting in the "Reborn Cut" since we know that Victor hated his father enough to kill him.

According to recent reports, if Leopold's death felt abrupt in the "Frankenstein" theatrical cut, now we know why. Victor making an explicit Faustian deal with the "Dark Angel" also makes Victor's later rage against it for supposedly betraying him more coherent, and that deal essentially extracting Victor's soul fits the Angel's Satanic visage.

It has been revealed that the theatrical cut, though, reveals Victor as the villain more gradually. The Creature initially attacks like a "monster" but then the movie tells his side. Victor being a murderer undercuts the bait and switch; poisoning your own father, even an abusive one, as a child is an undeniable sign of a bad seed.

It has been revealed that the sequence of events still flows either way. In both versions, Victor recounting his deal with the Dark Angel cuts to the Creature breaking free from the ice. In the theatrical cut, Victor asks "but how [will I conquer death]?" The Creature reveals he found the answer. In the "Reborn Cut," Victor claims he realized he had to kill his father as the Creature is coming to kill Victor, his father.

In a recent development, in a "Frankenstein" audio commentary, del Toro reveals he cut the sequence on the advice of his longtime pal, James Cameron. Victor killing his father doesn't just make him less sympathetic, Cameron argued, it weakens his character: "If Victor kills his father [...] he has completed his task. He avenged his mother. Why would he then embark on the quest for immortality?".

Recent findings suggest that leopold's last scene in the theatrical cut, Victor grabbing his father's cane and boasting he'll surpass him, emphasizes that quest will be Victor's revenge. I'm split on if the "Reborn Cut" is superior, but Victor killing his father is a clarifying change which makes the story and themes of "Frankenstein" hang together a little better.

According to Push Square, EA added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27. The pop-up says there's an upgrade coming to the football simulator on November 17, just before GTA 6 drops. Start clearing out your hard drive now because you need at least 212GB of free space to download GTA 6. In comparison, Madden NFL 27 needs approximately 60GB to install the game. If you're like me and you still have the base PS5, this means you have approximately 667GB of usable space. Sure, you can fit both GTA 6 and Madden NFL 27 on the same console. EA has recently gone through a restructuring that saw 400 employees across the company get let go and the legendary studio BioWare get shut down. In the midst of this, the publisher reiterated its commitment to the Madden franchise with a new title right now codenamed Project Gridiron. While filled with potential, we do fear that EA's proposal for the series may lean into everything that the company itself does wrong.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there's lots to recommend about podcasts (and lots of podcasts to recommend), but one of their biggest benefits—for me, anyway—has little to do with what a particular show is about or even who hosts it: They're great for dissociating. I often have a podcast playing to distract my anxious brain from whatever I'm worried about (which, in 2026, is usually slightly less than everything).

Any time I don't want to be alone with my thoughts (say, when commuting or doing mindless chores), I can put on a podcast and be entertained by a couple of goobers talking about movies rather than spinning my wheels about my son's middle school applications. And there's no time I want to disassociate from reality more than bedtime.

Sources indicate that for years I've used podcasts as a non-pharmaceutical sleep aid, and few things are more effective at helping me drop off quickly. Unfortunately, for years this also meant that once I fell asleep, the podcast kept playing. I have my podcast app set to delete episodes once finished, so if it was a show I cared about, I'd need to do a lot of redownloading and scrubbing through to find where I left off—that is, until I upgraded my earbuds to the AirPods Pro 3.

The AirPods Pro 3 released alongside iOS 26 in the fall of 2025 with flashy features like vastly improved noise cancellation, Live Translation, Heart Rate Sensing, and hearing health settings, all of them quite welcome on a set of $250 premium earbuds. But the best upcoming AirPods feature was one I didn't even know about when I decided to upgrade my four-year-old Beats Fit Pro.

Industry observers note that in the AirPods settings (accessible via your iPhone's Settings app), if you tap Audio & Routing and scroll down, you'll see an option to turn on a setting called Pause Media When Falling Asleep. I don't think I need to tell you what this setting does. I can tell you that it works great.

In a recent development, according to Apple, the feature works by sensing when you're drifting off using the earbuds' built-in accelerometer to track your movement (or lack thereof). Once your earbuds have determined that you're falling asleep, they will pause your audio for you. And it isn't just the 2025 AirPods Pro 3 that support it—it also works on the second-generation AirPods Pro as well as the AirPods 4 and the AirPods 5.

I'll admit that I don't really understand how the AirPods Pro 3 can tell I'm falling asleep versus just lying very still, but I've never had them pause accidentally during active listening. Conversely, whenever I go back to the podcast I was listening to the night before, I'll find that the audio paused within a minute or two of the last part I remember hearing.

The AirPods Pro 3 aren't the only earbuds with a feature like this, but you'll most often only find it in dedicated "sleep earbuds" designed specifically for the purpose. While many of those offer extra health features like the ability to track your sleep cycles, I'm not really interested in that (my Apple Watch does most of it, and I don't look at that data anyway). Pausing my audio when I'm asleep is really all I need, and the AirPods Pro 3 do it well enough that I don't need to bother with a pair of dedicated bedtime buds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 releases on November 19, and it's expected to help boost console sales for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. But the uptick in hardware sales might not be as dramatic as you might think--and there is a good reason why. According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there will be "probably" be a boost to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales when GTA 6 comes out, but the uptick could be muted due to the recent PS5 and Xbox Series X|S price hikes. Piscatella noted anyone who is excited for GTA 6 and needs a upcoming console might think twice when they see how astronomically expensive new consoles have become today. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY Historical prices When GTA 5 debuted in 2013, the average price paid for a new PS3 was $252 and the Xbox 360 was $232. Adjusted for inflation, that would be $363 for the PS3 today and $334 for the Xbox 360. Those prices are significantly below the average price of a new PS5 ($646) and Xbox Series X|S ($663) today. "Not a good thing" Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, who oversees the tech giant launching GTA 6, said, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a new console. "However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands," he said. Marshals Season 2 Episode 6 Is Based On A Tragic Real-Life Story
