📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Marshals" has had its share of problems, but its latest chapter manages to deliver an emotionally powerful storyline based on a real-life tragedy.
  • It has been revealed that backing up a bit: "Marshals" Season 1 solidified why the pitched Thomas Rainwater (Gil Birmingham) spin-off needs to exist.
  • According to recent reports, cole Brings Plenty was found dead in April 2024 near Kansas City, Kansas, having been reported missing a few days prior.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Marshals" has had its share of problems, but its latest chapter manages to deliver an emotionally powerful storyline based on a real-life tragedy. Season 2, Episode 6, "Roughstock," sees Luke Grimes' Kayce Dutton investigating the death of Mo's (Mo Brings Plenty) nephew, Troy (Will Strongheart), in a storyline based on the real death of Mo Brings Plenty's 27-year-old nephew, Cole Brings Plenty.

It has been revealed that backing up a bit: "Marshals" Season 1 solidified why the pitched Thomas Rainwater (Gil Birmingham) spin-off needs to exist. In lieu of that series, Grimes' procedural has at least given Rainwater and the Broken Rock reservation significant attention so far. Not only that, the "Yellowstone" spin-off has tried to highlight real-life problems faced by Native American communities, such as in the Season 1 episode that saw Kayce and the Marshals tracking down trafficked Broken Rock girls. Now, Season 2, Episode 6 has gone even further by using the passing of Mo's nephew as the basis for its narrative.

According to recent reports, cole Brings Plenty was found dead in April 2024 near Kansas City, Kansas, having been reported missing a few days prior. An actor, Cole previously played Pete Plenty Clouds in the "Yellowstone" prequel "1923" and appeared in an episode of "The Tall Tales of Jim Bridger" and four episodes of "Into the Wild Frontier." Prior to the discovery of his body, police identified Cole as a suspect in a domestic violence incident. After the actor was confirmed as having passed away, The Johnson County Sheriff's Office determined there was "no indication of foul play." But the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe promptly demanded a "full and thorough investigation into Cole's disappearance and subsequent death." Hence, in "Roughstock," Kayce takes it upon himself to carry out such an investigation into Troy's death.

It has been revealed that "Marshals" Season 2 started in disappointing fashion, but "Roughstock" marks its best episode yet. In this chapter, Kayce Dutton and Mo Brings Plenty search for Mo's nephew, Troy, before discovering his body at the foot of a cliff. There, a police officer dismisses the death as suicide and warns Kayce and Mo not to investigate further. They don't listen. Instead, they mount a search for more clues alongside Andrea Cruz (Ash Santos) and Miles Kittle (Tatanka Means). This leads them to a group of poachers, one of whom recalls seeing an as yet unidentified man hit Troy with a flashlight prior to his cliff fall, thus confirming there was more to Troy's passing than police claimed.

For Mo Brings Plenty, highlighting this problem of police failing to investigate the suspicious deaths of Native Americans was important, especially since he had a personal connection to the story. In a TVLine interview, the actor mentioned he was "very thankful" to showrunner Spencer Hudnut and his writers for "Roughstock," explaining, "My brother and I shared our real-life experiences with them and explained to them what occurred, and for them to take that and then create this beautiful storyline and give us, give me the opportunity to share that, I'm just so thankful.".

Sources indicate that "Roughstock" ends with a service to Troy, after which Mo carries out his own ritual by a fire, bidding his nephew farewell before seeing a white horse appear in a field. As the actor told TVLine, "Here, he has his own moment to clear himself and to be able to see the other side. That was the symbolism of the horse. It represented the other side, and Mo knows that his nephew made it, because I know that my real nephew Cole made it.".

As of now, Troy's killer remains unidentified. No doubt, the Marshals will continue to pursue justice for Mo Brings Plenty's nephew. For now, though, it's interesting to see "Marshals" take such a direct approach to representing Native Americans. "Yellowstone" featured several storylines designed to highlight problems faced by Indigenous tribes, and "Marshals" has maintained that aspect of its mothership series. But this is the first time the show has taken a real-life story and adapted it so directly. If nothing else, it adds a little more depth to a series that has thus far struggled to achieve any sense of believability.

Industry observers note that "Marshals" has no idea what it's about, and that indicates no signs of changing after the first six episodes of Season 2. Even Episode 6, its respectful adaptation of a real-life event is otherwise full of stilted dialogue and performances that leave a lot to be desired. "Roughstock" has the series' signature paroxysms of melodrama as well, such as when an Army veteran suddenly pulls a gun in a parking lot, forcing Pete Calvin (Logan Marshall-Green) and Belle Skinner (Arielle Kebel) to hurriedly diffuse the situation. It's a shame, really, given the rest of the episode does a decent and respectful job of highlighting a real-world tragedy.

In a recent development, meanwhile, USA Today reports that the Johnson County Sheriff's Office claimed to have "conducted a thorough investigation" into Cole Brings Plenty's death and that the findings had been presented to the family. But Mo Brings Plenty and the family remain unsatisfied. "When the wheel of justice doesn't turn for us," Brings Plenty told the outlet, "I know it didn't for us, and I know there are a lot of families that are in the same situation as we are.".

And from the sound of it, it was an amazing experience! During her interview with Hollywood ReelTime, Goodwin stated:.

I’ve gone around the park, after midnight in like a robe and slippers.

According to recent reports, first, Goodwin gets to play the original Disney Princess Snow White in the hit ABC drama Once Upon A Time, and then she gets to voice Zootopia's Judy Hopps, one of the most beloved animated rabbits. And now, she gets to go to Disneyland whenever she wants and get to stay the night in the park. It's not like I’m totally not jealous or anything! Seriously, though, what I love is that she can appreciate the privilege, given she's a fellow Disney fanatic. Check out this recap from her late 2025 trip to Walt Disney World Resort:.

A post shared by Ginnifer Goodwin (@ginnifergoodwin).

Most Disneyland fans are likely aware of Walt’s apartment above the firehouse on Main Street, which guests previously were able to visit through a paid guided tour. However, many might not know that the space above the Pirates of the Caribbean attraction was also an apartment built for Walt and his family to stay and entertain guests at, since the aforementioned firehouse apartment was too small. Unfortunately, Disney passed before the suite was completed, and his brother opted to halt construction.

It wasn’t until 2006, when Disneyland ran the “Year of a Million Dreams” promotion, that his dreams came to fruition. Thanks to the plans Walt Disney left behind, the space was turned into a suite that was made available to a randomly selected guest of the park. When the promotion ended, it became a space only Disney elite, like Goodwin and her family, could access.

I’m All In On Zootopia Director’s Response To The Fans Who Want Romance Between Judy And Nick.

Unfortunately, for me and Goodwin, the apartment of Pirates of the Caribbean is no longer an option for hosting an in-park sleepover. In 2017, the space was reimagined into an exclusive dining experience, 21 Royal. Technically, this experience is open to all guests, but it comes with a pretty hefty price tag: $18,000 for up to 12 guests. I guess that’s another item I’m definitely not going to cross off my bucket list!

It has been revealed that from the sounds of the interview, Goodwin still has a few items on her own list that she hasn’t crossed off, like sleeping in the suite inside the castle. Considering the success of Zootopia 2, the reveal of the upcoming sequel Zootopia 3, and her love for all things Disney, I’m sure the Mouse will pull some strings and allow her access to the coveted spot one of these days. I just hope she takes lots of pictures and shares them with her nearly 450K followers.

Industry News: WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.
  • Recent findings suggest that dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry. Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back. Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9AlEQvn4dlc Unfortunately, far too many players playing the game normally were caught in the crossfire. Many of Forever's dungeons have double-digit level ranges, meaning even if a player might find enemies early on in the dungeon trivial, enemies and bosses later on won't be. It also created a scenario where players were leveling up mid-dungeon, only to suddenly find themselves fighting trivial enemies and bricking the experience gains for everyone in the group. As it turns out, committing to a multi-hour adventure, only to suddenly find nobody is earning experience points and everyone is mad at you because you happened to level up, is not a great social experience. Blizzard was at least quick to admit the change "missed the mark" and made adjustments a day later on November 14. "With hotfixes that are now live, we've just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies," Blizzard remarked in a forum post. At least judging from forum comments, that seems to be a more reasonable compromise, even if it still does prevent higher-level players from coming to help their lower-level friends. It's just the latest chapter in what has become one of the biggest ongoing discussions in the Forever community. During the Forever beta, Blizzard made changes to experience earned from dungeon quests, nerfing them significantly. Come launch day, it became apparent Forever's dungeons weren't worth running more than once, as after completing quests, experience earned from kills was extremely low. Blizzard agreed, and issued a change on November 8 to increase the amount of kill experience earned in dungeons by 50%. It was a sizable increase, but is still lower than the experience amount players earned from doing dungeons in WoW Classic. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent-player records, and after one week of adventuring through Azeroth once more, classic WoW feels fresh again. Despite the record-breaking launch, Blizzard hasn't released official stats, but fansites have already pieced together the game's most popular class, race, and faction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the day before the Governors Awards, a studio executive who had attended the past few years told me that she often found herself crying at the star-studded gala. The annual awards ceremony, held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, is often an emotional event, with honorary Oscar statuettes bestowed on influential figures in the film industry. A tribute to Michael J. Fox in 2022 and a posthumous honor for Quincy Jones in 2024 left many guests misty-eyed.

At Sunday’s gala, that teary-eyed trend continued when Glenn Close finally got to hold her own Oscar, after eight nominations without a win. Others got emotional when Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, the independent producers from Killer Films, were honored for their tireless work making boundary-pushing and challenging movies. And when Floyd Norman, the 91-year-old artist who was the first Black animator to join Walt Disney Animation Studios, thanked his wife and five children, the crowd cheered along with him. Even though honoree Ridley Scott couldn’t attend, he dedicated his award to his late brother Tony Scott in a video message. “It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” remarked Matt Damon in his remarks for Scott, who has been nominated for four Oscars but has never won competitively.

Recent findings suggest that the presentation of honorary Oscars is often a way to correct Academy Award history, recognizing those who have been overlooked but deserve to be honored for their lifetime of dedication to storytelling and film. The Governors Awards ceremony is also a major stop on the Oscar season campaign trail, with a room packed full of stars and filmmakers from the year’s contenders.

Industry observers note that this year that meant a surprising number of couple contenders, including Monica Barbaro and Andrew Garfield (who both star in Artificial), Carrie Coon and Tracy Letts (The Liberation), and Zendaya and Tom Holland. Though Zendaya and Holland arrived together and walked through the Ray Dolby Ballroom as a pair, they actually sat at different tables—Zendaya at the Dune table, with Timothée Chalamet and director Denis Villeneuve, and Holland at the Odyssey table, with director Christopher Nolan. Chalamet also made a date night out of the event, bringing Kylie Jenner with him.

The room held a mix of A-list Hollywood stars, like Tom Cruise (in support of Digger), Julianne Moore (The Debut), and Charlize Theron (The Odyssey), and breakout filmmakers of the year, like Obsession’s Curry Barker, La Bola Negra’s Los Javis, and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman.

Sources indicate that another breakout of the season, La Bola Negra star Guitarricadelafuente, has been busy promoting the film as both an actor and a musician, having written the original song “La Nieve.” I wondered if he was exhausted from doing double duty. “I’m not tired,” he noted with a smile, raving that he had enjoyed meeting many of the other songwriters in the race this year.

All four of the presenters who handed the Oscars to the honorees are also in the Oscar race this year. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star Mahershala Ali honored Norman; Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich honored his Dangerous Liaisons costar Close; Julianne Moore, teaming up with Todd Haynes, honored Vachon and Koffler; and Damon, the star of The Odyssey, honored Scott.

In a recent development, as Close took the stage to accept the award from Malkovich, she wiped tears away from her eyes. The star of films including Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, The Wife, Albert Nobbs, and The Big Chill spoke about being raised in a religious cult and how, in her childhood, animated films were her only escape. She also spoke about being nominated for eight Oscars over her career, insisting that it didn’t phase her not to emerge victorious. “As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not,” she says. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room.”.

She wrapped up her speech with a strong statement against AI. “The craft of acting and of great storytelling has never been more vital to the existence of our fragile, violent, but capable-of-transcendence species,” she said. “We are not machines. We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation.”.

Vachon and Koffler have been making indie films through Killer Films since 1995, championing movies like Far From Heaven, Boys Don’t Cry, Kids, Carol, and Still Alice (which won Moore her Academy Award for lead actress). They dedicated their awards to the many people they’d worked with over the years, some of whom were in the room. “We have walked into propellers with you and what has resulted is usually a piece of work that has touched somebody. Sometimes it’s seen by millions of people and sometimes it’s seen by tens of people,” stated Vachon. “But our movies came to life and made it to the screen because writers and directors trusted us with their stories and actors knew we were creating an environment that enabled them to give their best performance.”.

Many of the honorees spoke about the mentors and industry giants who had helped them along the way. Close said she’d promised her World According to Garp director, George Roy Hill, that she’d thank him if she ever won an Oscar. “I never got the chance to thank the man who put me in my first movie. Now I can,” she said, holding her statuette up high. Scott, the director whose prolific career output includes Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien, Blade Runner, and The Martian, told a story in his video message about making his brother star in his very first project, the 1965 short film Boy and Bicycle. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony,” Scott said of his brother, who died in 2012. “His great work would certainly have earned this recognition.”.

That paved the way for Depp's upcoming take on Ebenezer Scrooge to take the crown. Internationally, the movie pulled in a further $23 million, giving it a $42 million global start.

Industry observers note that against a reported $38 million production budget, that makes this an instant winner for Paramount Pictures, especially since Christmas movies tend to hang around during the holiday season. Not to mention that they also tend to have especially long lives beyond the box office. All of this to say, it looked like "Ebenezer" might be the box office hit that Depp's Hollywood comeback needed and it proved out.

The movie is based on Charles Dickens' "A Christmas Carol" but promises a new take on the familiar tale. "If you think you know his story, think again," the tagline boasts. It boasts a star-studded cast that also includes Rupert Grint, Daisy Ridley, and Ian McKellen, among many others.

Industry observers note that "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is going to be a bigger hit than people realize, taking up a lot of oxygen this upcoming weekend. That remarked, if "Ebenezer" holds even decently well, Johnny Depp has a real shot at a meaningful Hollywood comeback, with some caveats.

In a recent development, for one, this is going to be a mid-budget, decent hit. It's going to build a bridge, but not a terribly sturdy one. After all of the fallout from the much-publicized feud between Depp and his ex-wife Amber Heard, many studios may still be reluctant to work with him. However, it's clear the general public is willing to turn up for a Depp-fronted motion picture.

Sources indicate that all of the "Pirates of the Caribbean" movies were massive box office hits. Outside of that though, it's been a long time since Depp has been a meaningful movie star. Depp proved his best days were behind him with the big box office bomb "Mortdecai" in 2015, even before his public fall from grace. His last year as a real movie star was 2017, when "Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales" and "Murder on the Orient Express" both came out.

That remarked, Depp was also named the most overpaid actor of both 2015 and 2016, with box office returns not matching his asking price. In light of "Ebenezer," Depp's path toward a larger comeback is somewhat narrow. He needs to be realistic about what salary he can command and to go for a sure thing. Is that a return as Captain Jack Sparrow? We'll see ... but we probably haven't seen the last of Depp, that much is certain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6's parent manufacturer played a role in bringing the movie to market. Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32. Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Aacz4pPqndk Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone. That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part. So why didn't Zelnick keep making movies? Zelnick was on top of the world as a film executive after Home Alone. However, he said he saw a bright future in the interactive entertainment business, so he left Fox in 1993 to join Crystal Dynamics where he served as president and CEO. "I left Fox voluntarily, which no one ever does, to move to Silicon Valley, take a 95% pay cut and become the pre-revenue CEO of a little tiny video game company called Crystal Dynamics in 1993," he said in the Rubenstein interview. After Crystal Dynamics, Zelnick shifted to the music business in the role of CEO as BMG Entertainment from 1994 to 2000. During that time, BMG started a gaming unit, BMG Interactive, which published the original GTA in 1997. After that, Zelnick and an investor group took over Take-Two, which was in a tough financial spot at the time and was sued by the US government for accounting fraud. Since the takeover, Take-Two has thrived. Its share price exploded from about $10 in 2007 to more than $220 today, and Take-Two today has a market cap of over $40 billion. The GTA franchise is a juggernaut at Take-Two, but it actually only accounts for 15% of the company's revenue in a non-release quarter. Take-Two today owns and operates a number of big non-GTA franchises, including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Mafia, BioShock, Civilization, and more. GTA 6 rolls out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's reportedly already sold close to 15 million copies and generated nearly $1.5 billion in revenue.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, samara Weaving is one of the most charismatic young actresses working right now. She's got one of the most expressive acting faces this side of Saoirse-Monica Jackson in "Derry Girls," and the comic sense to know how to use it.

It has been revealed that 2026 has been good for Weaving — and not just because she booked a part as Emma Frost in Marvel Studios' upcoming "X-Men" movie. This past year, Weaving has starred in three movies. She returned for a sequel to her 2019 horror movie "Ready or Not," and co-starred with Jason Segel in "Over Your Dead Body," a comedy-thriller about two spouses plotting to kill each other (like "War of the Roses" with violence out of "Looney Tunes"). The year's third Weaving film is "Carolina Carolina," which came and went from theaters with not even $1 million to its name. But since being added to Netflix on November 6, 2026, the movie has consistently placed in the service's top 10 most viewed movies.

Directed by Adam Carter Rehmeier, "Carolina Caroline" stars Weaving as Caroline Daniels, working as a gas station attendant in Texas at the turn of the millennium. One day, the slick Oliver Anderson (Kyle Gallner) saunters in and tricks the station's cashier out of $20. Carolina, noticing the con, is nonetheless charmed by Oliver. They hit it off, him teaching her how to run short change cons, and, before long, they're driving across the American South robbing banks together. If you've ever heard the names "Bonnie" and "Clyde," then you know what to expect from this story, but familiar pleasures are pleasures nonetheless.

The engine of "Carolina Caroline" is the central criminal romance. Oliver is Caroline's teacher and her lover, and the sexiness of their romance is intertwined with the lawbreaking. The movie never forgets Oliver is the more experienced criminal, making him more ruthless. That he genuinely loves Caroline only hardens him more when facing the rest of the world, especially when their fortunes predictably take a bad turn in the third act. While Caroline is sometimes shocked by the violence, it reads more as inexperience first, conscience second.

Industry observers note that the casting helps fuel the movie, too. It'd be overstating it to call "Carolina Caroline" a "Heat"-esque movie star collision. But both Samara Weaving and Kyle Gallner (who previously worked with Adam Carter Rehmeier in 2022's "Dinner in America") are genre favorites. Weaving is a scream queen and horror-action star thanks to "Ready or Not," while Gallner is a frequent face in horror movies, too: "Smile," the subverted slasher "Strange Darling," etc. Pair their charms together, and you never doubt for a second what draws Caroline and Oliver to risk it all in their whirlwind love story.

According to recent reports, "Carolina Caroline" prompts comparisons to Upcoming Hollywood movies about fugitive lovers, including not just "Bonnie & Clyde" but also Terence Malick's "Badlands." Like those movies (released in 1967 and 1973, respectively), "Carolina Caroline" sets itself a couple decades in the past for a more nostalgic feeling. The movie doesn't even immediately scan as a period piece until you notice that no-one has a cell phone. With its indeterminate late 90s/early 2000s setting, "Carolina Caroline" stakes itself in the last decade that a story about criminals pulling big jobs then staying anonymous for months afterwards could happen.

"Carolina Caroline" is streaming on Netflix.

Razvan has since spoken on the alleged incident on 90 Day: Hunt For Love, and what he said to Jamal. When someone on Instagram noted that he never denied that he said the slur, Razvan replied with the following (via @90DayFianceUpdate):.

Industry observers note that even if I deny it, people will still believe what they want beacuse their frustrations that 'life isn't fair.' In Europe people are not racist! The only country who are racist is USA, Russia, And Middle East. Europeans are not.

It has been revealed that it would appear that he's sticking with the narrative that he did not utter the slur, which makes me curious if the 90 Day: Hunt For Love team has footage of it. If so, will it air in the episode, and will we get to see Razvan's removal? Those are the substantial questions that remain unanswered amid this situation.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Razvan returned in 90 Day: Hunt For Love after he was initially featured in Before The 90 Days with Amanda Wilhelm. Presumably, his starting a relationship in this spinoff could've led to his return to the franchise, though it seems unlikely he'll work with TLC again after this. As for Jamal Menzies, it's looking like we'll see him and Emma Perry in a future 90 Day season, though it's always possible they'll break up before the season ends.

90 Day: Hunt For Love continues on TLC on Mondays at 8:00 p.m. ET. Tune in next week to see what all goes down, and keep an eye out for what Jamal or Razvan may have to say online afterward.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you hear the name Lil’ Kim, a variety of images come to mind. She’s forever known as the force of nature from Brooklyn who turned the music industry on its head when she entered the scene, and her bodacious lyrics and unique fashion sense have kept her as a source of inspiration on your favorite designer’s mood board ever since. On November 18 and 19, to celebrate the music that cemented her icon status, Lil’ Kim will perform in front of a symphony orchestra at the Kings Theatre in Brooklyn, not far from her humble beginnings.

Today she’s less interested in being in the spotlight and more focused on raising her 12-year-old daughter, Royal Reign. In between practices for her performances, Lil’ Kim spoke with Vanity Fair to reflect on her career, how she spends her days, and her standout looks.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: What do you remember about putting your debut album, Hard Core, together?

Lil’ Kim: I remember Biggie and Un [Lance Rivera], who was the label owner that we had. I watched Un build a record label called Undeas, which [stood] for “Un ideas,” and then he finally sold it to Atlantic Records. At the time, we didn’t know the process, but we became Undeas-Atlantic. I remember Biggie having the idea of how he wanted my album to be red, and he explained it to me and Un. I was able to write according to how his idea was to present me, because when they met me, I was who I was—in high heels, jeans, motorcycle jackets, and furs at 13.

Portrait of members of R&B group 112 and rappers Notorious MASSIVE and Lil’ Kim circa 1996.

That’s incredible. It sounds like your fashion-icon status started very early. Was there anyone that you looked to back then? What inspired you to dress that way?

According to recent reports, my mom was a big inspiration to me when it came to fashion, and so I looked to her for a lot of things. I used to wear her mink coat. She used to wear big sunglasses with her fur coats, with the diamonds and jewelry. She was always taking vacations and I would see her pack her stuff, and she would always have the cutest outfits. They were all matchy-matchy. It’s funny because she would have her outfit to go play tennis in and her outfit would match her tennis racket. So when I bought my big house, I bought a Chanel tennis outfit and I bought the racket to match it, because of my mom.

I love that. Do you keep up with tennis or specifically the ladies in tennis?

No, I haven’t in a while, but, of course, you know, Serena and Venus were like my heroes.

Well, maybe we need to see you on the court one day.

In a recent development, I know. I’m pretty sure I’m rusty, but I like to get out there, though. I used to beat my cousin’s butt back then.

How did the symphony performances come about?

According to recent reports, my agents called me and they’re like, “Kim, what do you think?” And I was like, “That’s a freaking awesome idea.” I love performing with bands. And so I imagine that it could be very similar, if not very close. And I thought this could be something really different for me. Sometimes I even listen to classical music. I don’t have to know who the artist is, but I just put on a station and let it flow.

Do you have a favorite song from Hard Core?

I love “Queen Bitch”; it’s my favorite song. It’s still my favorite to perform. And “Crush on You.”.

Salma Hayek, Donatella Versace, Pamela Anderson, and Lil’ Kim at Versace’s spring/summer 2001 fashion show.

When it comes to fashion, you’re obviously on everyone’s mood board, from stylists to designers, so how important was fashion for you as part of the Lil’ Kim persona?

It has been revealed that I just was being myself, honestly. When I first met Biggie, I was coming from my after-school job at Bloomingdale’s. I was probably 13 or 14 at the time, and they would let the teenagers work there.

It has been revealed that but I had on a motorcycle jacket and high heels. And one of my best friends told Biggie, “You know, my girl can rap,” because we knew he was rapping around the way. And he was like, “I heard you can rap.” And I just laughed. He was like, “Yeah, see, I knew you didn’t know how to rap.” He was very condescending. He knew how to get you to do what you wanted to do, because I was really shy.

And then I started rapping, and he was blown away because I had on high heels. No one had ever seen someone just bust a rap in high heels. When Biggie, Un, and Jacob York started really talking to me, they didn’t want to change me because that was just what they were so blown away about. That was just who I was.

Do you think people ever misunderstood the way you presented yourself?

It has been revealed that to be honest, I never really felt misunderstood by my hardcore fans—the kids my age and the younger kids, they totally got it. I think that’s why I had such a cult following and there was such pandemonium about me when I came out. They understood me. I think it was the older people and the politicians, those are the people who I think misunderstood me.

What did you think of the midterm elections and all of the women who broke barriers in the Senate and gubernatorial offices?

I’m going to be honest with you, I stay away from politics.

Sources indicate that are you keeping up with all of the changes within fashion today? When I listen to your music, you’ve mentioned so many designers and houses, and since then the creative directors have changed. Are you following all of the changes within fashion and seeing how you’re still a part of the conversation?

Sources indicate that that’s what I’m trying to say. As a fashion icon, if you really her, and I’m considering myself really her, that’s never gonna change. That’s never going to change. I might put on a fur coat that my stylist or myself will get asked about, because I style myself a lot. And I was styling myself then.

Lil’ Kim and daughter, Royal Reign, on June 16, 2016, in New York City.

What has motherhood been like for you?

It has been revealed that extremely rewarding. My daughter’s with me all the time. This world is so cruel and so evil; it’s so different. She’s my safe haven. I feel the extra need to keep her safe.

What does a regular day look like for you?

Lately, I’ve just been really getting into myself. I get up and go have a little spa day. I might take my daughter to go do whatever she wants.

In a recent development, singer Mary J. Blige with Diana Ross and Lil’ Kim at the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards on September 9, 1999.

How do you feel that we’re still talking about your MTV VMAs look in 1999?

Industry observers note that I think it’s iconic and I love it. I love when they bring that up, because it was a fun day and it was so good to see people’s faces when they saw my outfit.

Are there any other looks that don’t get as much love as you wish that they did?

I don’t know, because most of the looks that I love, they get the love. There’s a look when I was on the cover of Nylon magazine and I had the teddy bear dress on; that’s one of my favorite looks. The Louis Vuitton look is one of my favorite looks; I love that look. A lot of the Chanel looks and the Versace and the Chanel in the hair.

#16517. Breaking: GTA 6 Will Never Be Able to Beat Clair Obscur at The Game Awards

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (731 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Polygon ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: GTA 6 Will Never Be Able to Beat Clair Obscur at The Game Awards

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (731 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the triumph of Grand Theft Auto 6 at this year's Game Awards has seemed inevitable all year — especially in the face of what has turned out to be relatively weak competition.
  • Sources indicate that the records for most nominations and most wins were set last year by Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.
  • Although the two games are very different, Clair Obscur was similarly dominant in the awards narrative.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the triumph of Grand Theft Auto 6 at this year's Game Awards has seemed inevitable all year — especially in the face of what has turned out to be relatively weak competition. So you might assume that it's going to break records as it sweeps the board, just as it's going to break records commercially. But you'd be wrong.

Sources indicate that the records for most nominations and most wins were set last year by Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Sandfall Interactive's RPG was nominated for 13 awards and won nine. It is practically, if not theoretically, impossible for GTA 6 to beat these totals.

Although the two games are very different, Clair Obscur was similarly dominant in the awards narrative. Like GTA 6, nothing emerged all year that could realistically compete with it. And although it's a much smaller production, it excelled in the craft categories: performance, narrative, art direction, and music. It was nominated for, and won, most of the categories it was eligible for. The same looks likely to be true for GTA 6. So how come it can't beat it?

Recent findings suggest that crucially, Clair Obscur was eligible for two categories where GTA 6 can't compete: Best Independent Game and Best Debut Indie Game. Some have quibbled with Clair Obscur's definition as an indie, as it was a reasonably large-scale and well-funded production. But it was made by an independent studio for an indie-specialist publisher, so it's not an unreasonable definition. Either way, it happened.

Recent findings suggest that clair Obscur was nominated for Game of the Year, for all five craft categories (Game Direction, Narrative, Art Direction, Score and Music, Audio Design), and for the two indie categories. It had no less than three nominations in the Best Performance category (half the field). It was nominated for Best Role-Playing Game, its genre category. (Games can only be nominated in one genre category.) And it was nominated for the fan-voted Players' Voice award.

In a recent development, let's assume that GTA 6 matches Clair Obscur beat-for-beat across GOTY, the craft categories, its genre category (Best Action/Adventure Game, in this case), and in Players' Voice. That seems a pretty safe assumption. Even if it can match Clair Obscur's three performance nominations (a tall order, since jury members haven't spent as long with the characters), it would have to make up those two indie categories somewhere else to equal Clair Obscur's record.

According to recent reports, after ruling out the other genres, there are only a few other categories still on the table where that would be possible. GTA 6 is ineligible for most of them: Best Multiplayer, Ongoing Game, Mobile Game, VR/AR Game, and Community Support (as an unreleased game, it at the moment has no actual community). It hardly seems likely to get picked for Best Family Game or Games for Impact (however worthy it may or may not be). That only leaves Innovation in Accessibility. I have no idea about GTA 6's credentials in this field. It might be great, although, given its late release, it will be untested by the public.

So, in order to match Clair Obscur's record (never mind beat it), GTA 6 would have to be nominated for the accessibility award and get an unprecedented four Performance nominations. It's theoretically possible, but incredibly unlikely. I see GTA 6 netting out at 9 or 10 nominations, depending on whether both of the actors playing Jason and Lucia get nominated (or perhaps one of them plus a character part, such as Stephen Root's Brian Heder).

Sources indicate that it will also be very difficult for GTA 6 to beat Clair Obscur's nine wins. Clair Obscur ran an almost perfect game, winning in every category it was nominated for but two: Audio Design and Players' Voice. GTA 6 would have to win every single category I see it being nominated in to match that. It would need to be nominated in, and win, Innovation in Accessibility to beat it.

Neither scenario is impossible, but both are highly unlikely. These are two records GTA 6 is not going to break. In fact, given the unique circumstances surrounding Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 — an indie game with AAA production values and a beloved cast of actors — I expect these records are going to stand for a long, long time.

Breaking: GTA 6 Has Teamed Up With The Weather Channel To Show How Dynamic Leonida Can Be

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1137 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games has found an unexpected partner to show off one of GTA 6's most impressive features: The Weather Channel.
  • Industry observers note that rockstar Games has found an unexpected partner to show off one of GTA 6's most impressive features: The Weather Channel.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's an unusual collaboration, but a very fitting one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games has found an unexpected partner to show off one of GTA 6's most impressive features: The Weather Channel. The US broadcaster has shared an exclusive look at Leonida's weather system via six newly introduced screenshots and forecasts that make the fictional destination sound like somewhere you'd need to check the weather before visiting. It's an unusual collaboration, but a very fitting one. GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional state inspired by Florida, where sunshine, torrential rain, thunderstorms and tropical storms are all part of the ecosystem. Who better to show off the unpredictable climate than The Weather Channel? https://twitter.com/weatherchannel/status/2122429589326798848?a=eWjLxzkmblchbPp2GoQ&s=20 The broadcaster posted the collaboration on X, writing "Nobody knows weather like we do. That's why Rockstar gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida and the dynamic weather in GTAVI." Instead of just posting the six new screenshots, The Weather Channel provided six different weather reports for the various locations across Leonida. Each has its own conditions and some local facts, making the entire post sound like a genuine forecast. The reports include heavy rain reducing visibility across the Keys, a thunderstorm rolling over the swamps of Pelican Valley--and obscuring some feisty "nippers" at the same time--and sea fog threatening to obscure the expensive beachfront views at South Ocean Beach. There's also a tropical storm making the waters around the Rusty Anchor particularly choppy, and Gambit Bay has a low-lying morning mist ahead of hunting season. One forecast warns commuters traveling from Key Lento to expect more rain and wind. It seems like an almost mundane detail for a game about a pair of criminals, but it's this exact impressive world-building that makes Leonida feel real. The six new screenshots are especially impressive, showing off the towering storm clouds and lightning strikes through to dense fog that makes entire stretches of the coastline disappear. Rockstar isn't treating weather as just a visual effect--it will have a real impact on the way you play the game. Owen Shepherd, Rockstar's VP of Art: Light and Rendering, explained that the studio had to completely reimagine its in-game weather systems to make them feel "more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic." He added that Leonida's weather can range from clear blue skies to towering cumulonimbus clouds, reflecting the unpredictable conditions of the real-world Florida climate. The emphasis on localized weather is interesting. Instead of having the entire map experience the same conditions, Leonida's different environments can have their own atmospheric conditions. A coastal resort might be swallowed by fog, while a storm rolls over the wetlands in the distance. This approach will make exploring the enormous map feel different depending on when and where players visit. The screenshots don't confirm how individual gameplay mechanics will be affected, but they offer a deeper look at the environmental detail Rockstar is aiming for. There's something pretty extraordinary about a real-world weather broadcaster getting involved in the marketing of Grand Theft Auto--and it really puts into perspective how the arrival of GTA 6 is a once-in-a-generation event. GTA 6 launches on November 19, but players in New Zealand will be able to get their hands on the game ahead of the rest of the world, thanks to hitting midnight before anywhere else. For unrelated reasons, if you want to set your Xbox region to New Zealand, we've got you covered.

There's also a tropical storm making the waters around the Rusty Anchor particularly choppy, and Gambit Bay has a low-lying morning mist ahead of hunting season.

One forecast warns commuters traveling from Key Lento to expect more rain and wind. It seems like an almost mundane detail for a game about a pair of criminals, but it's this exact impressive world-building that makes Leonida feel real.

Recent findings suggest that the six new screenshots are especially impressive, showing off the towering storm clouds and lightning strikes through to dense fog that makes entire stretches of the coastline disappear. Rockstar isn't treating weather as just a visual effect--it will have a real impact on the way you play the game.

Owen Shepherd, Rockstar's VP of Art: Light and Rendering, explained that the studio had to completely reimagine its in-game weather systems to make them feel "more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic." He added that Leonida's weather can range from clear blue skies to towering cumulonimbus clouds, reflecting the unpredictable conditions of the real-world Florida climate.

The emphasis on localized weather is interesting. Instead of having the entire map experience the same conditions, Leonida's different environments can have their own atmospheric conditions. A coastal resort might be swallowed by fog, while a storm rolls over the wetlands in the distance. This approach will make exploring the enormous map feel different depending on when and where players visit. The screenshots don't confirm how individual gameplay mechanics will be affected, but they offer a deeper look at the environmental detail Rockstar is aiming for.

There's something pretty extraordinary about a real-world weather broadcaster getting involved in the marketing of Grand Theft Auto--and it really puts into perspective how the arrival of GTA 6 is a once-in-a-generation event.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 rolls out on November 19, but players in Fresh Zealand will be able to get their hands on the game ahead of the rest of the world, thanks to hitting midnight before anywhere else. For unrelated reasons, if you want to set your Xbox region to New Zealand, we've got you covered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

According to recent reports, since his introduction in 2015's "Avengers: Age of Ultron," the Vision (Paul Bettany) has become one of the most enduring Marvel Cinematic Universe characters. Not even getting his vibranium head crushed by Thanos (Josh Brolin) back in "Avengers: Infinity War" stopped him from returning in the TV series "WandaVision" — in which Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) conjures the life she wanted with Vision — and "VisionQuest," which revisits Vision's relationship with Ultron (James Spader), his "father.".

Industry observers note that created by Roy Thomas and John Buscema, Vision debuted in 1968's "The Avengers" issue #57. Unlike in the MCU, where Ultron creates Vision's "synthezoid" body for himself before the Avengers steal it, comic Ultron (then known as Ultron-5) created Vision as a conscious being to lure the Avengers to their doom. Vision then turned against his creator, and the following issue #58 saw him inaugurated as an Avenger.

Industry observers note that but Vision as we know him almost didn't exist. Thomas is a fan of the "Golden Age of Comics," aka the earliest period of superhero comics in the 1940s. Back then, Marvel was called Timely Comics, and its superhero stable included Aarkus, an interdimensional being named The Vision. Created in 1940 by Joe Simon and Jack Kirby (the same year that they created Captain America), the Vision debuted in "Marvel Mystery" #13. Summoned to Earth by scientist Enoch Mason, Aarkus hails from a supernatural dimension called "Smokeworld.".

Sources indicate that originally, Thomas wanted to bring back this Vision as an Avenger, as Stan Lee and Kirby had brought back Captain America in "Avengers" #4. But Lee (without giving a reason) insisted on an android hero instead, so Thomas and Buscema created a latest Vision in the image of the 1940s one. Aarkus has made occasional reappearances, but he definitely sits in the shadow of the later Vision.

Recent findings suggest that roy Thomas, who wrote "The Avengers" from problem #35 through #104, sometimes felt like he was playing in the minor leagues. Speaking to Yahoo in 2015, Thomas recounted: "Stan [Lee] kept taking Captain America, Iron Man, and Thor away from the Avengers. Every few months I would request to bring them back to the fold. I would say, 'You left me with a bunch of losers here.'".

When looking for a new Avenger, Thomas wanted to revive the Golden Age Vision because "[he] didn't like to create new characters for Marvel, because [he] wouldn't own them.".

Vision's origin honored Lee's request to make the new Avenger an android, but Thomas and John Buscema's Vision still looks a lot like Aarkus. They share a mostly green color scheme, a high collar cape, a bald head, etc. Vision's intangibility powers also evoke Aarkus appearing and disappearing in plumes of smoke. There are some different details, granted. Vision has a "solar gem" on his forehead (which Thomas credits to Buscema, and which the MCU tweaked into one of the Infinity Stones), as well as red skin (unlike Aarkus' pale green).

In a recent development, speaking with The Hollywood Reporter in 2015, Thomas surmised that Lee wasn't totally satisfied with the Vision, noting he disliked the hero's red color ("Red's not a good color!") and the "Vision" name. "It seems a little wimpy, but I felt Vision — it really means like a ghost or a mirage or an image," Thomas explained.

Nonetheless, history indicates Vision's creation came with a huge ripple effect, reshaping "The Avengers" forever. Many of the book's core storylines go back to Vision, like his romance with the Scarlet Witch or Ultron's persistent efforts to destroy the Avengers, his son included.

According to recent reports, ultron debuted only a few complications before Vision, in "Avengers" #54. Problem #57 saw Vision seemingly destroy his creator, while issue #58 revealed the Avenger Hank Pym/Ant-Man had created Ultron, leading to the robot rebelling and erasing his creator's memory. Roy Thomas told Yahoo, "I knew right away [Ultron] is a character you would bring back." So he did when, in "Avengers" #66, subliminal programming inside Vision makes him restore Ultron in a new adamantium body. As for Vision and the Scarlet Witch, Thomas told Syfy in 2022 that he paired them because Vision didn't have a solo title, so Thomas had sole control over Vision's story.

It has been revealed that if Aarkus the Vision had become an Avenger, it's plausible he'd have filled a superficially similar role on the team. Perhaps he and Wanda would've even ended up together. But he'd lack the connection to Ultron, which would diminish the villain.

In a foreword to 2015's "Avengers: Rage of Ultron," former "Avengers" writer Kurt Busiek notes the Ultron-Vision thread running through "Avengers" is a family saga. The family theme also heightens the contradictions that make Ultron more than just a killer robot. He's literally inhuman, yet he behaves more like an angry and erratic child than a cold machine, closer to Frankenstein's Creature than Hal 9000.

In a recent development, this makes Thomas and John Buscema creating Vision, instead of resurrecting Aarkus, a lynchpin moment of entertainment history in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Stan Lee, Thomas, and Buscema, when pumping out cheaply-printed "Avengers" comics in the 1960s and '70s, could've hardly predicted Vision would be a major character in the biggest blockbuster property ever. Nor that an entire TV series would rest on Vision and Wanda's romance, and then another on Vision and Ultron's antagonistic bond.

Following her daughter’s death, Vogel told the Daily Mail in August that she was “not abusive by any stretch of the imagination” while managing Hayden’s career.

Industry observers note that “I think that Hayden put a pressure on herself,” Vogel argued. “I know that she has mentioned, you know, [that she] ‘always had to please Mom,’ or make sure it was, you know, I succeeded or whatever. I didn’t put that on her. I think she put that on herself.”.

Beyond security measures, we've also seen base PS5 consoles updated with Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), which is also rolling out to more games. An AI-based upscaling technology derived from the PS5 Pro's PSSR, it initially supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • If you find yourself losing track of time or running late for events, Waze can notify you when it's time to leave—based on your current location and live traffic—so you arrive on schedule.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that waze is a crowdsourced navigation app designed to help you get where you're going as quickly and with as much information about your route as possible. Where Google Maps and Apple Maps offer relatively straightforward directions, Waze tries to outsmart these alternatives by integrating real-time community feedback about hazards, speed traps, road closures, and more. If you are switching to Waze or using it alongside your other navigation tools, these are the hacks to help you maximize everything the app has to offer.

If you find yourself losing track of time or running late for events, Waze can notify you when it's time to leave—based on your current location and live traffic—so you arrive on schedule. You can set up "Time to leave" reminders in advance for individual planned drives, or you can sync your calendar to receive notifications for scheduled events. Calendar sync connects to your device's default calendar app, but you can change this to a third-party alternative if you prefer. Calendar events must include a navigable address to trigger reminders, and you must select Plan a drive in Waze for the event.

Sources indicate that waze has a feature called "child reminders," which are notifications to check for children before you get out of the car. This is clearly an incredibly vital use case, but you can also use these alerts for custom messages, like "Don't forget the groceries!" In Waze, tap the menu button > Settings > Reminders > Child reminder and select Custom message.

Variable speed limits, especially on unfamiliar routes, can result in you speeding when you don't mean to. But Waze can alert you if you exceed a customized speed threshold so you aren't caught by surprise or at higher risk of being ticketed. From the menu, go to Settings > Speedometer and turn on Show speedometer. Tap Speeding threshold to select what limit you want to trigger alerts, and turn on Alert at threshold if you want Waze to play a sound.

Recent findings suggest that waze offers a wealth of information on routes to help drivers navigate obstacles and hazards, but this can clutter your map and distract you from the most critical information, especially in congested, high-traffic areas. Waze says it limits and prioritizes alerts automatically, but you can actually customize which alerts you see based on what's most crucial to you. From the menu, go to Settings > Alerts and reports > Reports and select the relevant alerts.

It has been revealed that in the same Alerts and reports menu, you can enable Alert while driving, which will give you an audio warning and an onscreen pop-up about your selected hazards. This allows you to run navigation via a different map app (like Google Maps or Apple Maps) in the foreground while still getting Waze data in the background.

Waze integrates with toll road and HOV lane passes, so if you have an express or fast lane subscription, your route will optimize for it. If you don't, Waze can still account for HOV lane eligibility if you tell it how many passengers are in your car. From the menu, go to Settings > Toll and HOV passes and tap the plus icon to add your pass(es) from the list. If you need to add your passenger count instead, you can do so from View routes and enable the HOV option.

If you're driving through an unfamiliar, highly congested, or poorly designed area, you can ask Waze to help you avoid tricky maneuvers, such as crossing multiple lanes of traffic or turning left at intersections without lights. This prioritizes ease over speed using protected green arrows, roundabouts, and right turns. From the menu, go to Settings > Navigation, Avoid difficult intersections and select Always. You can also ask Waze to avoid toll roads, ferries, freeways, and unpaved roads.

Recent findings suggest that waze has a built-in audio player that syncs with your preferred listening platform—such as Spotify, YouTube Music, and Pandora—so you can control your music without having to navigate between apps. (As Waze is a Google product, Apple Music isn't included.) Simply tap the music icon on the map to select your audio player and hit Accept. If you don't see the icon, go to Settings > Audio player and turn on Show on the map.

It has been revealed that if you want to make audio directions more interesting, you can select a celebrity or character voice to help you navigate. Recent appearances include Bill Hader's Cat in the Hat and Ziggy Marley. Tap the speaker icon > Current voice to search for the voice or language you want to use. You can also record directions in your own voice.

In a recent development, if you don't want Waze storing certain types of data—or if you want to keep your activity hidden from other owners—you can adjust various privacy settings in the app. You will certainly want to turn off personalized ads (under Settings > Privacy) and consider enabling invisible mode, which keeps your username, mood, photo, and online status hidden from other Waze users. Finally, you can delete recent locations and drives as well as your navigation history at any time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Gilligan's Island" might have been a silly slapstick sitcom, but it remains beloved even almost 60 years after it went off the air.
  • Members of the "Gilligan's Island" cast re-teamed on numerous projects in the years after the show proper went off the air.
  • According to recent reports, this legendary show famously combined the sci-fi, spy, and Western genres to create a unique experience, which ran for four seasons on the network that also hosted "Gilligan's Island," CBS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Gilligan's Island" might have been a silly slapstick sitcom, but it remains beloved even almost 60 years after it went off the air. Of course, after the third and final season, the castaways managed to keep themselves in the public consciousness via a syndication deal, two animated "Gilligan's Island" spin-offs, and three TV movies — and that's to say nothing of the unofficial reunions.

Members of the "Gilligan's Island" cast re-teamed on numerous projects in the years after the show proper went off the air. In fact, Captain Jonas Grumby and Thurston Howell III actors Alan Hale Jr. and Jim Backus couldn't wait to get back on-set together. The pair reunited a couple years after the castaways bid viewers farewell, when they both appeared in one of the best classic Western series: "The Wild Wild West.".

According to recent reports, this legendary show famously combined the sci-fi, spy, and Western genres to create a unique experience, which ran for four seasons on the network that also hosted "Gilligan's Island," CBS. "The Wild Wild West" debuted in September 1965, the same month the castaways returned for their second season. By 1969, however, "Gilligan's Island" had been off the air for two years while "The Wild Wild West" was entering its fourth and final season (though it, too, would live on via TV movies and an infamous big screen reimagining). It was during this final run that Hale Jr. and Backus both appeared in the episode "The Night of the Sabatini Death.".

"The Wild Wild West" debuted at a time when the sci-fi genre was already beginning to supercede the Western. It ultimately took until the mid-'70s for Old West adventures to fall out of favor completely (though, if you'd have asked Roger Ebert he would have stated 2001's Ali Larter-led "American Outlaws" finally killed the Western for good). Before the decline of this once beloved genre began in earnest, however, Michael Garrison conceived of a series which he famously envisioned as "James Bond on horseback." But that was only part of the "Wild Wild West" formula.

The show, set in the post-Civil war era, followed Secret Service agents James West (Robert Conrad) and Artemus Gordon (Ross Martin), who thwarted all manner of threat to the United States using advanced technology. That added a sci-fi element to the show's melding of the Western and spy genres, making it a triple threat that immediately proved popular. By the time Alan Hale, Jr. and Jim Backus guested, the show was well-established as a small screen favorite, even while CBS was preparing to drop the axe.

Recent findings suggest that "The Night of the Sabatini Death" begins with dying crime boss Johnny Sabatini (Ted de Corsia) meeting Jim West. It seems the sickly kingpin wants West to ensure his niece, Caroline (Sylvia Nolan), receives a gift he's leaving her. West then travels to Calliope, Missouri, alongside his new agent colleague (Ross Martin was missing from several Season 4 episodes) Ned Brown, who's played by Hale Jr. In Calliope, West meets mortician Fabian Swanson (Backus) who is dispatched halfway through the episode, becoming a "customer of his own establishment" as West puts it.

At the end of "The Night of the Sabatini Death" Alan Hale Jr.'s Ned Brown departs, telling James West he intends to "spend a vacation all alone on a desert island." The "Gilligan's Island" theme then plays, confirming this is, indeed, a nod to Hale's Skipper role (poor old Jim Backus doesn't get to do anything near as fun).

In a recent development, interestingly enough, Hale Jr. and Backus' appearance in "The Night of the Sabatini Death" was far from the only link between "Gilligan's Island" and "The Wild Wild West." Dawn Wells, who'd played Mary Ann Summers on the CBS sitcom also appeared on "The Wild Wild West" the year prior to her former co-stars. The actress guest starred in the 1968 episode "The Night of the Headless Woman," playing Betsy Jeffers, daughter of Richard Anderson's Commissioner James Jeffers. It was a brief appearance, but it meant she beat her "Gilligan's Island' colleagues to the series.

What's more, "The Wild Wild West" was one of many reveals to make use of "Gilligan's Island" sets, most notably the lagoon which had been built on the CBS Studios backlot. "Gilligan's Island" also shared this set with "Gunsmoke," the show which ultimately forced the sitcom off the air. But it also came in handy for the adventures of James West and Artemus Gordon.

Industry observers note that sadly, those adventures came to an end shortly after Hale and Backus' guest appearances on the show. "The Wild Wild West" was ultimately canceled to appease a Congress eager to prove it was against violence in every form, including the small screen variety. Today, we can at least see Hale Jr. and Backus' "Wild Wild West" guest spots for free on Pluto TV.

That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US blueprint to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game. The odds are in Us’ favor because Jennifer Lawrence just staged an epic Hunger Games reunion.

The Oscar winner was joined by cast members from the original Hunger Games movies — including Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson — at the Newly introduced York City premiere of the latest installment in the franchise, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, on Monday, November 16.

Lawrence, 36, who played protagonist Katniss Everdeen, was photographed posing with Hutcherson (who played Peeta Mellark), Harrelson (Haymitch Abernathy) and Elizabeth Banks (Effie Trinket), all of whom first brought Panem, the devious Capitol and heroic District 12 to life in the first four Hunger Games released between 2012 and 2015.

The actress wore a long black coat with a fur trim and floral detailing, in keeping with the movie’s floral promotional artwork.

Joining the family reunion were fellow Hunger Games OGs Willow Shields, who played Katniss’ sister Primrose Everdeen, Jena Malone, who played Johanna Mason, and Amandla Stenberg, who shot to fame with her epic turn as Rue in the first film.

Sadly, there was no Liam Hemsworth — who played Hutcherson’s love rival Gale Hawthorne — on the red carpet to complete this epic reunion.

However, the original cast was joined by the stars of the 2023 prequel The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes: Rachel Zegler, Tom Blyth, and Josh Andrés Rivera.

In a recent development, the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is a sequel set after the events of The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes and features an all-newly introduced cast taking the deadly Hunger Games, led by Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner. Joseph Zada plays a younger version of Haymitch, while Elle Fanning takes over the role of a younger version of irreverent stylist Effie Trinket.

Lawrence, Hutcherson and Harrelson will also reprise their respective roles in the movie more than a decade after they were last seen together in The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2.

The actress spoke about her cameo during an October appearance on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast.

“Oh my, unbelievable. It was so crazy because it was the same crew. It was like, Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other. It was so beautiful.”.

According to recent reports, as for Harrelson, Lawrence joked, “And Woody obviously came through the window of my hotel room uninvited because it would not be the same. It wouldn’t be the same if he listened to boundaries and used a door.”.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters on Friday, November 20.

Stacey Abrams in Conversation With Ta-Nehisi Coates
